t: Install A9 Voice, set it up in five short steps, then dictate your first sentence and record your first meeting note. A9 Voice is for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). Transcribe is free, always. Notes has a 30-day free trial that starts when you press Try Notes free (no signup, no card), then costs $49 once. It does two jobs. Transcribe types what you say into any app while you hold a key. Notes records a meeting, a video or a voice memo and turns it into a transcript and a summary. This page takes you from a fresh install to both.

Install Download the installer from a9voice.com/download , open it, and follow the steps. Edge or Windows may show a note first, because A9 Voice is new and not code-signed yet; the download page explains each screen. A9 Voice installs for your Windows user only. It does not ask for administrator rights. If A9 Voice does not open by itself, open it from the A9 Voice folder in the Start menu. A9 Voice starts with Windows and waits in the tray (the small icons by the clock). Closing its window does not quit it; the first time you close it, a notice says "A9 Voice is still running in the tray". To quit, right-click the tray icon and choose Quit .

Set up A9 Voice The first time you open A9 Voice, a setup screen walks you through five steps. A row of dots at the top shows where you are. You can click Back , Skip this step or Skip setup at any time, and you can finish later: if you close the window part-way, setup picks up where it stopped.

Step 1: your name A9 Voice asks what to call you. It fills in your Windows name. Your name labels your voice in meeting transcripts and lets summaries say "you" and mean you. Change it any time in Settings › Account . Click Continue .

Step 2: your microphone Pick your microphone, or leave Windows default . Say a few words: the bar moves when you talk and rests when you do not, and the text under it says Hearing you clearly. If nothing moves, check that the microphone is not muted. Click Continue .

h: Step 3: how A9 Voice hears you
t: Step 3: how A9 Voice hears you A9 Voice needs a speech service to turn your voice into text. Pick one; you can change it any time in Settings › Models (see Speech models ). On this PC is marked Recommended: free, private, works offline. Click the tile, then Download Parakeet V2 . It downloads once. Then A9 Voice checks its speed on your PC ("Checking its speed on this PC…") and the tile says Ready . After that, nothing you say leaves your PC. Dictation and meeting notes both use it, and notes tell the other people on a call apart. Windows displayed in English gets Parakeet V2 (English); any other display language gets Parakeet V3 (25 European languages, it picks the language itself). A line under the button says which, with Use the other one to swap. See Free setup . Above the tiles the screen names the two jobs. For dictation a model on this PC is free, private and fast. For meeting notes it is free and works, but the live transcript lags and telling callers apart is less reliable on busy calls. Best for meetings: Deepgram or ElevenLabs : reliable speaker labels, and Deepgram shows the live transcript almost at once. Deepgram gives new accounts $200 of free credit; ElevenLabs has a free plan. Add a Deepgram key or Add an ElevenLabs key opens the service's key page and its key box. When the key is saved, Meeting notes move to it (Deepgram Nova-3 or ElevenLabs's current speech model, with speakers told apart) and a line says so; Keep it on this PC puts them back. Dictation is not changed. Groq , Deepgram , OpenAI and ElevenLabs are cloud services. You bring your own key and pay the service directly. The setup screen notes that Groq has a free plan and that new Deepgram accounts get $200 of free credit. Custom server is for any OpenAI-compatible speech server. You add it later in Settings › Models . To use a cloud service, click its tile and follow the three steps shown: Click Get your free Groq key → . Your browser opens the service's own key page. Sign in there and create a key. (For Groq, this is console.groq.com/keys .) Come back to A9 Voice, click in the Paste API key box and paste the key. Click Test . A9 Voice saves the key and tries it. A line says Connected and shows what it heard. The tile then says Key saved . The key is stored in Windows Credential Manager, never in a file. The first service that has a key becomes the one A9 Voice uses. You can pick nothing and click Continue anyway; A9 Voice reminds you before your first dictation. If you save a first Deepgram key, a box under its tile asks Also use Deepgram for Meeting notes . It starts checked, and Meeting notes move to Deepgram when you click Continue . Uncheck it to keep Meeting notes on the model they use now.

Step 4: try it Click in the box. Hold Ctrl + Space , say a sentence, then let go . Your words appear in the box and a line below says how long it took. While you hold the keys it says Listening… let go of the keys to finish. If something goes wrong, a card says That didn't work , explains why, and offers Try again , Pick another provider , Skip and Copy diagnostics .

Step 5: Summaries The last step tells you that A9 Voice can also record meetings and write a summary, and shows the record key ( Ctrl + Alt + N ). With no language model yet it says Summaries and Ask need a free Groq key. It takes 2 minutes and no card. Click Get your free Groq key → , paste the key, Test . A key you saved on step 3 counts, so you are not asked twice. Click Skip for now to leave it: a note keeps its transcript and says Add a free Groq key to get a summary , and it is written the moment you add the key. This step is optional. Click Finish .

Free setup A new install is set up to cost nothing: Parakeet on this PC for dictation and for meeting notes (speakers told apart, nothing leaves the PC), and Groq's free tier for summaries, Ask and Enhance ( openai/gpt-oss-20b , long meetings written in parts). Saving a Groq key sets Summaries, Ask: Quick, Ask: Deep and Enhance to GPT-OSS 20B · Groq when you haven't picked a model for them. Whether Enhance runs is still your choice: see Enhance with AI . Nothing you chose yourself is ever changed. If you were using A9 Voice before this, or skipped setup, Settings › Models shows one card once: Free setup available . It lists each job with what it uses now and what it would use, and the ones it will keep. Apply what is ready changes only the jobs still on what a fresh install starts with; Not now closes it for good. A day's free allowance on Groq can run out on a very busy day: the note then says when it resets and offers Use another model . If you want to see setup again, right-click the tray icon and choose Help › Restart setup .

Your first dictation You can dictate into any app, anywhere you can type: a document, an email, a chat, a web page. Click in a text box. Hold Ctrl + Space and talk. A small pill appears at the bottom of the screen with a level meter and a timer. It never takes focus from the app you are in. Let go. The pill says Transcribing and then Pasted , and your words appear where your cursor was. A quick tap of the key does nothing. To cancel while you are talking, press Esc . When you finish setup you land on Home , which lists your keys: Everything about dictation, including hands-free mode, is on the Transcribe page.

Home Under your keys, Home counts what you have dictated and recorded. The switch above the four tiles picks the range: 7 days , 30 days or All time . A9 Voice remembers your choice, and a new install starts on All time. Words dictated , Dictations and Time saved count your Transcribe dictations. Time saved compares typing at 40 words a minute with the time you spent speaking. Notes recorded counts your finished notes and shows their length. The tiles show a dash for a moment right after A9 Voice starts, then fill in by themselves, and they update when a dictation or a note finishes while Home is open. Under each number, All time shows what the last 7 days added, for example "+1,284 last 7 days". On 7 days and 30 days it compares with the same number of days just before, for example "▲ 18% vs prior 7 days". When those earlier days have nothing in them, it says First week or First month instead of a change. A range is a rolling count of days: 7 days is today and the 6 days before it.

Your totals keep counting Home reads its own small table of daily counts: the day, how many words, how many dictations and how long you spoke. It never holds the text. Settings › General › History kept deletes old dictations from the Transcribe history, but not from these counts, so the totals keep growing. Clear all and Delete in Transcribe leave them alone too. The count began when you updated to 0.7.8, from the dictations the history still held then. Dictations deleted earlier can't be recovered. The line under the tiles says since when: "Counted on this PC since Oct 6". Nothing leaves your PC. Settings › General › Reset counts starts the dictation counts again from zero, after asking. Your Transcribe history and your notes are not touched.

Your first meeting note A note is a recording of a meeting, a video or a voice memo. A9 Voice records your microphone and the sound your PC plays, so it hears both sides of a call. No bot joins the meeting. New to it? Watch Sara record a first meeting.

h: 1. Check which models it will use
t: 1. Check which models it will use The three chips at the top right show what A9 Voice uses: Dictation (speech to text for dictating), Notes (speech to text for meetings) and AI (the language model that writes summaries and answers questions). Click a chip to switch. Notes can use Deepgram, ElevenLabs, a model on this PC, or the other services you have set up. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and models on this PC tell the people on a call apart. The others label lines Me and Them. If you only added a Groq key, open the Notes chip and pick it. AI needs a key from a language-model service. Without one, you still get a transcript, but no summary. Add one in Settings › Models (see Language models ).

2. Start recording Open Notes and click Record , or press Ctrl + Alt + N from anywhere. The Record button in the left sidebar does the same, and turns into Stop with a timer while you record. If you join a Microsoft Teams or Zoho Cliq call, A9 Voice starts by itself and shows an 8-second notice with Discard and Keep . You can turn that off, or add other meeting apps, in Settings › Recording . A small recording bar appears on your screen: It shows Recording , the time, Pause and Stop . Hover over it for more buttons: Snip (add a screenshot to the note), Live window (watch the transcript as it happens), the microphone and computer-audio pickers, and a button that shrinks it to a small pill. The full story is on Recording a meeting .

3. Stop Click the square stop button on the bar. It asks Stop recording? : choose Stop to keep the recording, or Stop & discard… to delete it (it asks once more before it deletes anything). Esc closes the question.

4. Wait for the note The note appears at once in Notes . Its row says Transcribing… and then Summarizing… . When the status disappears, the note is ready. If it says Needs a look , open it for the reason and click Try again .

5. Open it Click the note. The page has three tabs: Summary , Transcript and Ask AI . The right column lists the speakers: type a real name in a box to rename someone everywhere in the note. If the summary is missing because you had no language model, add a key, then click Regenerate summary in the right column. More on this page in The note page .

6. Export Click Export at the top of the note. Choose what to export ( Summary , Transcript or Audio recording ), pick a format (for the summary: Markdown, plain text, PDF, Word or an HTML email file), and click the blue button, for example Export Markdown . When it says Saved. , click Show in folder . Copy for email puts the summary on the clipboard, ready to paste into a new message. Every note also lives in its own folder on your PC (by default under Documents\A9 Voice\Notes ) with its summary and transcript as plain files. Open it from the ⋯ menu with Show in folder . See Templates and export for all the formats.

If something goes wrong Nothing happens when you hold the key. The sidebar shows Key in use · fix if another app has the same shortcut. Click it, or open Settings › Dictation and choose another key. The pill says a key is missing or rejected. Click the pill's Fix link, then check the key in Settings › Models . The note failed or has no summary. See the steps above and Troubleshooting .

Where to go next The manual is also one click away inside the app: the ? at the top right of every page opens the manual at that screen, and Manual in the sidebar (or Help › Manual in the tray menu) opens its front page. Privacy and data : where your audio, text and keys go. Updates and channels : how A9 Voice keeps itself current.

h: Speech models and your graphics card
t: Speech models and your graphics card Use a cloud service with your own key, or a model that runs on your PC, with the graphics card for the bigger ones. Then choose who handles dictation, who handles meeting notes and the fallback for dictation. Read the guide → · Models → Sara is an AI presenter.

Hold a key, talk, let go, and your words are typed into whatever app you are in. Use it for emails, chats, documents and anywhere else you can type. Transcribe is A9 Voice's dictation. It needs a speech service, which you set up in Getting started or in Speech models . Everything on this page happens on your PC except the speech service you chose: your audio goes there, and nowhere else. See Privacy and data . New to it? Watch Sara walk through it.

Dictate with the dictation key The dictation key is Ctrl + Space . Click in a text box in any app. Hold the dictation key and talk. Let go. After a moment the text appears where your cursor was. A quick tap does nothing: no sound, no pill, nothing sent. A9 Voice treats a key press as dictation only once you have held it for a moment. To change the key, open Settings › Dictation and click the Dictation key box. It says Press keys… . Press the new combination. It needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win in it (F13 to F24 work alone). Press Esc to cancel. If another program already uses that key, A9 Voice tells you, and the sidebar shows Key in use · fix until you pick another. The numbers match the sections below. See Keyboard shortcuts for every key.
Cancel a dictation Press Esc while you are recording. The pill says Cancelled and nothing is sent. Esc is only watched while you record, so it works normally the rest of the time.

Hands-free mode Hands-free lets you talk for as long as you like without holding a key. Open Settings › Dictation . Hands-free mode has three choices: Choice What it does Off Only hold-to-talk. This is how a new install starts. Its own key A second key. Press it once to start, press it again to stop and insert. Its default is Ctrl + Shift + Space . Tap the dictation key A quick tap of the dictation key starts hands-free; the next tap stops it. Holding still works as hold-to-talk. With Its own key , the Hands-free key row appears. Click it to record a new key, or press Backspace while it listens to clear it. If you hold the hands-free key down for a moment and let go, it finishes like hold-to-talk. Esc cancels in every mode. Hands-free limit (1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes; 10 by default) stops the recording and inserts the text after that long. The pill warns you a minute before: the timer turns amber and says how long is left.

The pill While you dictate, a small pill shows what is happening. It appears at the bottom centre of the screen where the app you are working in is (you can move it to the top in Settings › General with Pill at the top of the screen ). It never takes focus, so your cursor stays where it was. It is click-through, except for its buttons. From top to bottom: Recording (red dot, level bars, timer): you are being heard. The bars move with your voice. Hands-free adds the label Hands-free · Ctrl+Shift+Space to finish (your key), a square stop button (stop and paste) and a cross (cancel). Transcribing : your speech is being turned into text. Pasted (or Typed , or Copied ) with the time it took: done. It fades after a moment. If a second service answered, it adds via Deepgram (or the one that did); if there was no internet and a model on this PC answered, it adds offline . Mic muted (in Teams or Windows) : see Microphone and muted mics . An amber message with Fix : something needs your attention, for example a missing key. Click the pill to open the setting that fixes it. Other short messages: Didn't catch that (no speech was heard), Cancelled , Nothing to paste yet , and Timed out after 15 s. Nothing was pasted , which appears if a dictation has not finished after 15 seconds. Turn on Show the pill when idle in Settings › General if you want a small dot to show that A9 Voice is running.

The Transcribe screen Click Transcribe in the sidebar to see your dictations. Each is a row with the text, the time, the app it went into and how long it took. At the top: Today , Typical speed and Words this week , counted on this PC. Words this week is the same count as Home's 7 days, so deleting rows doesn't lower it. Type in Search dictations to find a row. Each row's buttons: Copy puts the text on the clipboard. Paste again hides A9 Voice and pastes it into the app you were in. Delete removes the row. Clear all at the bottom deletes every row, after asking. Neither changes the totals on Home; Settings › General › Reset counts does that. Play recording and Show in folder appear when the audio was saved (see Dictation audio ). Retry appears on a failed row. Under each text, a line says how it went in: the time, the app, and typed or copied when it was not pasted. via Groq (or the other service) means your first choice failed and the backup answered. Hover over the time on the right to see where it went: from the key release to the audio being sent, the model, and the paste. Settings › General › History kept sets how many rows stay (the last 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000 or 20,000).

Failed dictations If the speech service cannot be reached, the row says Transcription failed. The audio is saved; retry when you're back online. Click Retry and the row fills in with the text. A retry does not paste anything; use Copy to take the text. If audio saving was off, the row says The audio is gone.
Enhanced rows When Enhance with AI changed the text, the row says AI and the time it took, with Show original to see what was heard and Show enhanced to go back.

h: Copy the last transcription from the tray
t: Copy the last transcription from the tray Missed the text box? Right-click the A9 Voice icon in the tray (the small icons by the clock) and choose Copy last transcription , or open Recent and click one of your last five dictations. The text goes on your clipboard as a normal copy; paste it with Ctrl + V . Copy last transcription is greyed out while the history is empty.

Paste the last transcription again Press Alt + Shift + V (the Paste last transcription key, number 3 above) to put your newest dictation in again at the cursor. Change it in Settings › Dictation , or press Backspace while it listens to turn it off. If you have not dictated yet, the pill says Nothing to paste yet .

Microphone and muted mics A9 Voice uses the Windows default microphone, which follows what you pick in Windows. To choose one yourself, open Settings › Microphone (or Dictation microphone in Settings › Dictation ; it is the same setting). Click Test and talk: the bar should move when you talk and rest when you do not. Keep microphone ready makes dictation start a little faster. Windows shows the microphone as in use while it is on. Dictation microphone lets you use a second microphone for dictating while your headset is muted in a call. Notes can use another one: Settings › Recording › Microphone (Me) says Same as Transcribe by default. If you speak and the pill says Mic muted (in Teams or Windows) , the microphone's Windows mute switch is on (a headset can do this when you mute yourself in Teams), or the microphone is sending complete silence. A9 Voice never unmutes anything for you. Unmute, or click Use … for dictation on the pill when it offers another microphone that is not muted. Clicking the message itself opens Settings › Microphone . A microphone that is only muted inside Teams, not in Windows, still works for A9 Voice.

Sounds A soft tone plays when recording starts, stops or is cancelled, and a lower tone when something goes wrong. The start tone comes just after you press the key, so a quick tap stays silent. Turn the tones off with Sounds and set Volume in Settings › Microphone . During a call, or with a headset in call mode, the tones play on the headset's call audio and can come a moment late.

How text goes in How text goes in (number 4 above) has two choices: Paste is the default and fastest. A9 Voice puts your text on the clipboard, sends Ctrl + V , and puts back whatever you had copied before. Dictations are kept out of Windows clipboard history ( Win + V and the cloud clipboard). Type types the text key by key. Use it in apps that block paste. Related settings in the same card: Put my clipboard back afterwards (on by default), Add a space after (on by default, so the next sentence does not run on) and Language you speak (English by default, or your Windows language on a new install; Detect automatically, or any of more than 60 languages). Used for dictation and meeting notes. Setting it is faster and more accurate than detecting. It is the same setting as Language you speak under Settings › Models › What each job uses , and it covers meeting notes too, not only dictation. If the speech model you picked can't do the language, an amber line under the row says so, for example Parakeet V2 only understands English. Pick an engine for German. See Languages by engine . Click Show advanced for Paste keys (switch to Shift+Insert for some terminals and remote desktops) and Clipboard restore delay .

Dictating into A9 Voice itself You can dictate into A9 Voice's own text boxes too: Ask, a note's title, tags and transcript lines, search, and Settings. Click in the box first, then hold the dictation key. The text goes in at the cursor and the pill says Typed . If no A9 Voice text box has the cursor, the text is copied and the pill says Copied — click a text box in A9 Voice first .

Enhance with AI Enhance with AI cleans up each dictation before it is inserted. It is off by default. Open Settings › Dictation and scroll to the Enhance with AI heading. Switch Enhance with AI on. Pick a Model . If the list is empty, add a key in Settings › Models first (see Language models ); until then text is pasted as heard. A small, fast model keeps dictation quick. Choose a Style : Light cleanup or Formal (Formal only adjusts tone a little and never adds content). Set Wait at most (1.0 to 3.0 seconds; 1.5 by default). Past this, the plain text is pasted so dictation never stalls. Optionally write Custom instructions , for example which spellings to use. They cannot override the rules below. What it does: removes "um" and "uh", fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. What it never does: rewrite, shorten or answer what you said. If the answer comes back much longer or shorter than what you said, A9 Voice ignores it and pastes your words as heard. The History line then says AI too slow · as heard , AI failed · as heard or AI reply skipped · as heard ; when nothing needed changing it says AI: no changes . When Enhance is on, the text of each dictation is sent to the language model you chose, in addition to the speech service.

Dictation audio saved for retries By default A9 Voice keeps a small compressed copy of each dictation's audio for 7 days, so a dictation that failed can be transcribed again. Open Settings › Dictation audio . Save audio recordings turns it on or off. Audio folder shows where the files go (by default in Documents\A9 Voice\Audio , in a Transcribe folder). Change… moves it; Open shows it. Settings, history and logs stay in AppData. Keep dictation audio is 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever . Older audio is deleted daily. Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it.
If something goes wrong

Nothing pastes Work down this list. Nothing happens at all when you hold the key. Another program may own the shortcut. Look for Key in use · fix in the sidebar and choose another key in Settings › Dictation . Also check the tray: if you chose Pause dictation there, the keys are switched off. Hovering the tray icon says dictation paused or shows your key. The pill says "Pick how A9 Voice hears you first". No speech service is set up. Click Fix and add a key or download a model in Speech models . The pill says "key missing", "key rejected", "rate limit hit" or "timed out". Check the key in Settings › Models . A backup service (see Speech models ) takes over when the first one fails, and the History line shows via and its name. The pill says "No internet". The dictation is kept as a failed row if audio saving is on; click Retry on it later. If you have downloaded a model to this PC, A9 Voice uses it instead and the pill says offline . The pill says "Didn't catch that" or "Mic muted". The microphone heard nothing. Check Settings › Microphone . The pill says "Can't type into an admin window — copied instead". Windows does not let a normal app send keystrokes to a program running as administrator. Press Ctrl + V yourself; the text is on your clipboard. The pill says "Paste was blocked — copied instead" or "Typing was blocked — copied instead". Windows did not let A9 Voice send the keys. The text is on your clipboard meanwhile, so press Ctrl + V yourself. If the pill says Pasted but nothing appears, the app may ignore Ctrl + V (some terminals and remote desktops do): switch How text goes in to Type , or under Show advanced set Paste keys to Shift+Insert . The pill says "The clipboard was busy — try again". Another program was holding the clipboard. Dictate again, or use Paste again on the row. Text pasted somewhere unexpected. The text goes into the window that has focus when the transcription finishes. Keep the right window in front until the pill says Pasted . If it still does not work, see Troubleshooting .

Teach A9 Voice the names and jargon you use, and fix the words it keeps getting wrong. Use it when a name comes out misspelled every time. The Dictionary has two lists. Vocabulary is words to listen for. Always replace is a list of fixes: when A9 Voice hears one phrase, it writes another. The same lists work for dictation and for meeting notes. Click Dictionary in the sidebar. A new install starts with both lists empty. To see a word and a fix added, and where the spelling shows up:

Add vocabulary Use vocabulary for names, products and jargon: anything the speech service might otherwise spell as an ordinary word. Click Add a word or name (number 1 above) and type the word, for example a colleague's surname. Press Enter , or click somewhere else. The word becomes a chip in the list. To remove a word, click the × on its chip. Adding the same word twice, in any capitalization, does nothing the second time. Write each word the way you want it spelled.

What vocabulary does The words are sent to the speech service as hints, so it is more likely to hear and spell them correctly. Deepgram, Groq, OpenAI and custom speech servers use the hints. Deepgram takes the first 100 words in your list, so keep the ones that matter most near the start. ElevenLabs and speech models on this PC do not use the hints; use Always replace for those. The same list is also used when Enhance with AI tidies a dictation, when a meeting is transcribed, and when a meeting summary is written, which is told to spell these words as you wrote them.

Add a fix Use a fix when the same mistake keeps coming out, for example a name that is always heard as two words. Click + Add a fix (number 2 above). A new row appears. In the left box ( Heard ), type what A9 Voice writes now, for example lark spur . In the right box ( Write ), type what you want instead, for example Larkspur . Click out of the box. The fix is saved. To remove a fix, click the × at the end of its row.

How a fix matches Whole words or phrases. A fix for cat changes "cat" but not "concatenate". A phrase such as lark spur matches those words one after the other, however they are spaced. Any capitalization. lark spur , Lark Spur and LARK SPUR all match. Written exactly as you typed it on the right. If you type Larkspur , that is what appears, whatever the capitalization of what was heard. Characters such as $ are written as they are. The longest phrase wins. If you have a fix for see and another for see em dee bee , the longer one is applied first, so the phrase is not broken up. Rows with an empty Heard box are ignored. Fixes are applied to the text that comes back from the speech service, before Enhance with AI and before the text is inserted. They also apply to the transcript of a meeting note. Fixes work with every speech service, including those that do not use vocabulary hints.

h: Add a fix from a note
t: Add a fix from a note When you correct a word in a note's transcript (double-click a line, change one word, press Enter ), A9 Voice offers to apply the change everywhere. Tick Add to Dictionary and click Apply to also save the fix and the spelling here. It is not ticked unless you tick it.

Import and export The Import and Export buttons (number 3 above) share lists with a plain text file. Use them to move your Dictionary to another PC or to share it with a colleague. Windows opens its normal file window; A9 Voice cannot show that window here. Export saves a text file. It suggests the name a9voice-dictionary.txt . The message Exported. appears when it is done. Import opens a text file ( .txt ). A message says Added or updated 3 entries. (with the real number), or Nothing new in that file. Importing only adds and updates: it never deletes your existing words or fixes.

The file format One entry per line: A line with a single word or phrase is vocabulary. A line like heard => write is a fix. → works in place of => . Both sides need text. Blank lines, and lines that start with # , are skipped. An exported file looks like this: # A9 Voice dictionary # Vocabulary: one term per line Priya Larkspur # Replacements: heard => write lark spur => Larkspur ex sample ix => Examplix If a fix in the file has the same Heard phrase as one you already have, in any capitalization, its Write side is updated. Vocabulary that you already have, in any capitalization, is not added again. You can write the file by hand in Notepad. Your Dictionary is also included when you export your data from Settings › Account , which makes a zip of your settings, Dictionary, templates and tag names. API keys are never included.

If something goes wrong A word is still misspelled. If your speech service ignores hints, add a fix as well: put the misspelling in Heard and the right spelling in Write . A fix changes words you did not mean. Fixes match whole words in any capitalization, so a short phrase such as see matches every "see". Make Heard longer and more specific. The import says "Couldn't read the file". Choose a plain text file saved as .txt .

Language you speak The first row sets the language that dictation and meeting notes listen for. A new install on a Windows that is not in English starts with that language (German on a German Windows), or Detect automatically when the language isn't in the list; English Windows starts on English. Nothing changes a language you already chose. If you installed before this and Windows is in another language, a card at the top of this page asks once: Windows is in German. Transcribe in German? Dictation and meeting notes are set to English. Use German changes the setting; Keep English leaves it. Neither answer brings the card back. When the speech model for Dictation or Meeting notes can't do the language, that row turns amber and says why, for example Parakeet V2 only understands English. Pick an engine for German. Fix this opens the model list with only the engines that understand the language, and recommends the multilingual model on this PC (Parakeet V3 for its 25 European languages, otherwise Whisper Small): shown first when it is downloaded, with a Download button when it isn't. Detect automatically gets the same warning on an English-only model. A speech service you added yourself with Add custom API is never warned about: A9 Voice can't know what it understands. Which engine does which language is in Languages by engine .

Free setup A9 Voice starts new installs on Parakeet (on this PC) for Dictation and Meeting notes and on Groq's free tier for Summaries, Ask and Enhance. If you were here before that, or skipped setup, a card at the top of this page says Free setup available once. It shows what each job uses now and what it would use, keeps every job you picked yourself, and Apply what is ready changes the rest. Jobs that need the Parakeet download or a free Groq key say so on their line. Not now closes the card for good. See Getting started . While Meeting notes run on a model on this PC, the row says so quietly: Running on this PC: free, but slower and less accurate at telling callers apart. Deepgram or ElevenLabs are faster. Upgrade opens the engine list with only the cloud engines that identify speakers; with no Deepgram or ElevenLabs key yet it takes you to the keys. In that list each engine has a live-status chip (see below).

Change a job's model Open Settings › Models and click Change on the job. Pick from the list. Choosing Same as Summaries puts the job back on the Summaries model. For a speech job the list shows the speech services you have a key for and the models you have downloaded. For a language job it is the searchable list described below.

h: Telling the other people on a call apart
t: Telling the other people on a call apart Your microphone and the computer's audio are recorded on separate channels, so you and everyone else are always told apart. Telling the other people apart, for example Ana from Ben, needs speaker separation. Deepgram and ElevenLabs do it, and so does a model on this PC when Identify speakers is on and its model files are downloaded. Speaker names, voiceprints and per-person Ask filters all depend on it. When Meeting notes can't do it, its row gets an amber border and says Can't tell the other people apart. Everyone on the call except you will show as one speaker. Choose an engine that identifies speakers. The Meeting notes chip at the top shows a warning triangle too. Amber is a warning, not an error: nothing is broken and the note is still made. Saving your first Deepgram key while Meeting notes can't tell people apart shows a box in the key window, Also use Deepgram for Meeting notes . It starts checked. Checked, Meeting notes move to Deepgram and your meeting audio goes there. Unchecked, the key is saved and Meeting notes stay as they were. You can change it later in the Meeting notes row. Fix this opens the engines that identify speakers. Fix this opens the list with only the engines that identify speakers. Only engines that identify speakers can be unticked to see the rest. In the list, engines that identify speakers come first with an Identifies speakers badge, in one column on the right. The others say One speaker for everyone else . Under each name is one chip that says what the engine does during the call, the same facts the Live window acts on: green Live: speakers named during the call : it writes the live transcript and labels the other people live, so you can tag them and ask about them while the call goes on (Deepgram, AssemblyAI); yellow Live: delayed · speakers named during the call : a model on this PC, behind the call on most PCs, with speakers guessed from their voices as they talk; yellow Live transcript · speakers after the call : live text, with the people told apart only in the finished note; grey No live transcript : the engine works after the call (ElevenLabs, Groq, OpenAI, servers you added). With a model on this PC installed, the Live window can still show a live transcript from it. After the chip, a short note in grey, such as Fast after the call . Choosing one of those asks Use it anyway? once. That is fine when you only record calls with one other person. When the engine can do it but Identify speakers is off, the row says so and Turn on switches it on. Dictation shows no warning: speakers don't matter there.

Pick a language model The list holds every model each of your providers offers, read from the provider itself: OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq and Google, plus your own servers. A model released tomorrow shows up without an update of A9 Voice. The lists are kept for 24 hours and the last one is used when you are offline. Refresh lists asks again now. Type to search. Good for Deep models come first for Ask: Deep. Each row shows the model's name, its provider, its context (how much text it reads at once) and its price in dollars per million tokens, in and out. price unknown means the provider doesn't say. Good for Deep marks a model with a context of 100,000 tokens or more and a stronger tier. Deep answers read up to 120 passages, and a small model gives them thin. For Ask: Deep the list also shows about $0.04 a Deep answer per model. The estimate uses the median size of your last 20 Deep answers, or about 20,000 tokens in and 1,500 out until you have some.

A newer model When your Summary model is a Claude Haiku and a newer one is on offer, the page says Newer: Claude Haiku 5.5, cheaper and stronger. Switch Summaries to it? once. Not now closes it for good. Your own choices are never changed without asking.

Providers and keys Under the jobs, Providers and keys holds the provider cards: keys, tests and downloads. There are no job checkboxes in a provider's window any more; jobs are chosen at the top. See Speech models and Language models for each provider's steps. The old Speech models and Language models pages are this page now. Links and the manual's ? button land here.

h: When your network blocks a speech service
t: When your network blocks a speech service Some work networks block a speech service's address. A9 Voice tells that from the service having a problem (a block answers with a page of its own, not with the service's error) and says so: Your network is blocking Deepgram (api.deepgram.com). Notes then use a model on this PC when one is installed. After two blocked notes, the Meeting notes job offers once: Your network blocks Deepgram. Use the on-PC engine on this network? The setting changes only when you click Use the on-PC engine (or Download the on-PC model first); Not now ends the offer. See Work networks .

h: When a model can't take a request
t: When a model can't take a request If a model is skipped or fails, the answer's footer says why after after: . These are the reasons for a too-big request: request too large for Groq's per-minute token cap on this model : the one request is bigger than your Groq plan allows per minute. It never counts as usage, so Groq's dashboard can show 0%. A9 Voice learns the cap and skips that model for requests it can't take, without sending them. request too large for OpenAI's context window on this model : the question and passages don't fit the model's context. Groq rate limit (429) : a real rate limit; wait a minute or use another model. The next model you have set up answers instead. See Asking your notes .

Related Speech models : keys, models on this PC and your graphics card. Language models : keys for summaries, Ask and Enhance. Asking your notes : Quick and Deep answers. Search and Ask : find words in your notes. Recording a meeting : notes and speakers.

Choose what turns your voice into text, with a cloud service and your own key, a model on this PC, or (new in 0.6.0) your graphics card. A speech model is the engine that listens to audio and writes the words. A9 Voice has no engine of its own that you pay for: you bring a key for a cloud service, or you download a model that runs on your PC. You can mix them, and you can use a different one for dictation, for notes and as a spare. Everything here is in Settings › Models . Which job uses which engine is chosen at the top, under What each job uses (see Models ). Under Providers and keys the speech part has two groups: SPEECH SERVICES (services you reach with a key) and ON THIS PC (models that work offline). 1: the speech services. 2: your own server. A tile with a blue Add key button has no key yet; a gear means it is set up. New to the choices? Watch Sara go through cloud services, models on this PC and the three jobs.

Choose who does what Pick an engine for a job with its Change button in What each job uses : Dictation types what you say when you hold the dictation key. Fallback for dictation steps in when the dictation model fails. It has to be a different model. Meeting notes writes the transcript of your recordings. A model's own window no longer has job boxes. You can't Disconnect the model that does dictation; choose another one for dictation first.

What the fallback does The fallback is tried once when the model in use fails, is rate-limited, or takes longer than the limit shown under Fallback for dictation (4 s). In the pill you see via and the fallback's name when it answered. If you have a model on this PC and both cloud models fail, it answers last. With no internet at all, the cloud fallback is skipped (it would fail too) and a model on this PC answers straight away; the pill says offline . More in Without internet .

Which models tell speakers apart For meeting notes, Deepgram , ElevenLabs , AssemblyAI and Mistral (Voxtral) (and models on this PC with Identify speakers on) tell the people on a call apart. Groq, OpenAI and other custom servers can't: notes label everyone but you as one speaker. Choosing one of those for Meeting notes shows an amber warning with a Fix this button, and asks Use it anyway? once. See Models . When you save your first Deepgram key and your notes model can't tell speakers apart, the key window shows a box, Also use Deepgram for Meeting notes , checked. Leave it checked and Meeting notes move to Deepgram, which means your meeting audio is sent there. Uncheck it and the key is saved while Meeting notes stay on the model they use now. It asks only for a first key, and never when Meeting notes already use Deepgram, ElevenLabs or a model on this PC. Your dictation model is never changed by this. You can change Meeting notes later under What each job uses .

Set up a cloud provider The steps are the same for every provider. The only things that change are where you get the key and which model you pick. Your keys stay on your PC: they go into Windows Credential Manager and never into a file, a log or the app's storage. A9 Voice only ever learns "key saved" or "no key". Open Settings › Models , scroll to Providers and keys and click the provider's tile. Click the big blue Get your Groq key → button (the name changes with the provider). A9 Voice opens the provider's key page in your browser. On that page, sign in, create an API key, and copy it. Come back to A9 Voice: the cursor is already in the key box. Paste the key into API key . Click Test . A9 Voice sends a 2-second test clip and shows what it heard, for example Heard “Testing one two three.” and how long it took. Nothing is saved yet. Click Save . Then choose which job uses it under What each job uses . The strip under the big button follows you: Get a key , Paste it here , Test , with each one ticked when done.

Groq Key page: console.groq.com/keys . The window says Free tier, no card needed. and the button reads Get your free Groq key → . 1: the key button opens Groq's key page. Paste the key and test it. Then choose the model ( Whisper Large v3 Turbo or Whisper Large v3 ). 2: paste. 3: test. 4: save. Groq can't tell speakers apart and doesn't stream. The same Groq key is also used for Language models , so you only add it once.

Deepgram Key page: console.deepgram.com . The window says $200 of free credit, no card needed. and the button reads Get your free Deepgram key → . Models: Nova-3 and Nova-2 . Deepgram tells speakers apart, which makes it the best choice for notes, and it is the one used for the live transcript during a recording (see Live window ). Once a key is saved, the key box folds away and shows Key saved and Manage key . The key is saved. Manage key replaces it.

OpenAI Key page: platform.openai.com/api-keys . The button reads Get your OpenAI key → , with no promise of a free tier. The model list is a drop-down. Models: GPT-4o mini Transcribe , GPT-4o Transcribe and Whisper . OpenAI can't tell speakers apart. For notes, A9 Voice uses Whisper with OpenAI because the GPT-4o models don't give the timestamps a note needs. The same key is used for OpenAI language models .
ElevenLabs Key page: elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys . The button reads Get your ElevenLabs key → . Models: Scribe v2 and Scribe v1 . ElevenLabs tells speakers apart, so it works well for notes.

AssemblyAI Key page: assemblyai.com/dashboard/api-keys . The button reads Get your AssemblyAI key → . Models, under Model : Universal-3.5 Pro (the default, the most accurate) and Universal-2 (cheaper, 99 languages). Test sends the 2-second test clip and shows what it heard and how long it took; a key that is wrong, an account with no credit left, or a model your plan doesn't have is said in plain words. Meeting notes. The two sides are sent separately after the call, and the other people's side has speaker labels switched on, so the people on the call show as Speaker 2, 3 and so on and are named like they are with Deepgram. A "speaker" who says only a few words in the whole call is folded into the person next to them, so a stray label doesn't turn into someone to name. The live transcript. When AssemblyAI writes your notes, the Live window streams to AssemblyAI's Universal-Streaming on the same key, only while the window is open (plus a minute), and says what it costs: about $0.42 an hour for both sides with speaker labels, $0.50 when your Dictionary has words. Nothing goes to a second provider. The other people's side has speaker labels live, so Who's this? , Now: and the names carried into the finished note work as they do with Deepgram; your own side doesn't ask for them. Your Dictionary. The words in your Dictionary are sent as key terms (up to 100 live, up to 1,000 after the call; a phrase can be six words). On Universal-3.5 Pro, AssemblyAI charges extra for key terms; Universal-2 includes them. Cost. After the call, Universal-3.5 Pro is $0.21 an hour and Universal-2 $0.15, plus $0.02 an hour for speaker labels. Live, Universal-Streaming is $0.15 an hour, plus $0.12 for speaker labels (the other people's side only) and $0.04 for key terms. In Usage & cost each combination is its own row under Prices , and the live stream is billed by how long it stays connected. Dictation. It works for dictation too, but it is an upload-and-wait service, so a few seconds slower than Groq or Deepgram. A9 Voice asks AssemblyAI to delete each transcript right after it has read it. AssemblyAI's own terms say it may use what you send to train its models unless a paid account opts out under Data Controls in its dashboard, so the window and the tile say so in one line.

Mistral (Voxtral) Mistral's Voxtral has its own tile with an Add key button: it opens the Mistral (Voxtral) choice of Adding another service below, and once you save it your Mistral entry is the tile.

What the capability line means Every cloud window shows three facts under its name: Languages , Streaming and Diarization . Diarization is telling speakers apart. Streaming means the service can return words while you are still talking; the live transcript during a recording uses Deepgram (or AssemblyAI when it writes your notes), or a fast model on this PC.
Add a custom API Use Add custom API for a service the app doesn't list, or your own server. It asks Which service? first, so you only need to know a key.

Adding another service Service You need Good to know Together its API key Whisper and other speech models. Mistral (Voxtral) its API key Tells speakers apart in Meeting notes, after the call. On Mistral's free plan, requests may be used for training. Speaches (on this PC) nothing; its server must be running ( http://localhost:8000/v1 ) Nothing leaves your PC. Other (OpenAI-compatible) the server's address, and a key if it wants one Any server with an /audio/transcriptions address, on this PC or your network. Together, Speaches and Other are Whisper-style: A9 Voice sends the audio, the model name, your dictation language and your Dictionary words as a hint, and gets back the text. None of them is asked to tell speakers apart, so in Meeting notes each shows One speaker for everyone else : it works for dictation and for notes with you and one other voice, but use Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Mistral (Voxtral) or a model on this PC when you need Ana told from Ben. The window says so under the key box. Mistral (Voxtral) uses Mistral's own transcription request instead ( voxtral-mini-latest , Voxtral Mini Transcribe, after the call). The window opens with that model already filled in, so you can paste a key and Test at once. It is used for dictation and for Meeting notes, where it labels the other people (Speaker 2, Speaker 3) so naming and voice tags work as they do with Deepgram. Your Dictionary words (up to 100) are sent along as spelling hints. Mistral's live model is not used: the live transcript stays on Deepgram or a model on this PC. In Usage & cost its audio is priced at Mistral's per-minute rate, which you can edit under Prices . Click Add custom API at the end of the cloud tiles (or the Mistral tile for Voxtral). Pick the service. Its Name and address are filled in for you. Paste the key into API key . Don't have one? Get a Together key → (with the service's own name) under the box opens the service's own key page in your browser. Speaches shows Runs on this PC: no key needed instead, and has no link. Look at Model . A moment after the key is in (at once for Speaches) it becomes a list of that service's speech models, with a Whisper-class one already chosen. Refresh list asks again; Type a name… at the end of the list lets you enter one the list lacks. If the list can't be loaded, Model stays a box you type in, and one line says why. Click Test . It sends a 2-second test clip, the same way a dictation is sent, and shows what it heard and how long it took, for example Heard “Testing one two three.” · 0.31 s . Click Save . Save never waits for Test. If you type a model name and Test fails, or can't be run yet (no key pasted), you can still save: the window says "You can still save it", and the service's tile then shows Not tested yet: with the reason, until a Test passes (open the tile, Test , Save ). A Test that failed still shows its error. This is the same for language models. Pick the service; the address is filled in. 1: key. 2: the model list. 3: test. Advanced is closed to begin with. For a service from the list it holds Name , Base URL (the filled-in address, which you can change), Extra header (optional) and Header value ; the line under them says Only needed for company servers that ask for an extra ID. The value goes into Credential Manager like a key. When something is wrong, Test and the list say so in plain words, for example Local server not running: nothing answers at localhost:8000. Start Speaches on this PC, then try again. , … rejected the key , Nothing answers at this address (404). The Base URL looks wrong; it usually ends in /v1. or … doesn't have a model called "…" . Other (OpenAI-compatible) is the plain form: Name , Base URL such as http://localhost:8000/v1 , API key (optional) , Model and, under Advanced , the extra header. Servers added before presets existed open this way, unchanged. Only the Base URL is required to save. For notes, the server must answer with timestamps (the Whisper verbose_json style). Disconnect on a custom server removes the provider and its saved key and header.

h: Change a key or remove a provider
t: Change a key or remove a provider To replace a key: open the tile, click Manage key , paste the new one, Save . To remove one: open the tile and click Disconnect . This deletes the saved key from Credential Manager. If the provider was your fallback, the fallback is cleared. To see the keys in Windows: open Credential Manager, then Windows Credentials . A9 Voice's entries end in a slash and the provider's name (for example /groq ). Groq and OpenAI use one key for speech and for language models . Disconnecting it in either place removes it for both.

On this PC Models in the ON THIS PC part run on your computer. They are free, work offline, and nothing you say leaves the PC. They don't need a key. English-only models first, then multilingual ones. The tiles are split into ENGLISH ONLY and MULTILINGUAL : Model Languages Runs on Parakeet V2 English the processor Whisper Small, Base, Tiny (English) English the processor Parakeet V3 25 European languages, picked by the model the processor Whisper Small, Base, Tiny 99 languages the processor (Small can also use the graphics card) Whisper Medium, Large v3, Large v3 Turbo 99 languages the graphics card only The multilingual Whisper models use Language you speak . Parakeet V3 detects among its 25 languages by itself, so it ignores the setting.

Download a model Click a model's tile. The window says what it is, its languages, its Size , and how much room is free: for example 111.8 GB free on this drive . Click Download . A9 Voice downloads from Hugging Face, checks every file before use, and also fetches a small set of shared tools (finding speech and telling voices apart) the first time. A progress bar shows Downloading… … of … . Click Cancel to stop. When it finishes, A9 Voice runs a quick speed test by itself. It says what it needs before you click. Cancel stops it. If the drive is too full you get Not enough free space: it needs …, and … is free ; A9 Voice keeps 500 MB spare. A download that stops, because you cancelled or the connection dropped, picks up where it stopped when you click Download again. If it ends in an error, Discard partial download clears what was fetched.

Use a model Open the model's window. It says what uses the model now, and its speed on this PC. To give it a job, use Change on that job under What each job uses in Models . 1: speed on this PC. 2: what uses it.

Speed on this PC The window shows Speed on this PC , for example 0.2 s for 3 s of speech (14× faster than speaking) . It is measured on a short built-in clip after the download. Click Test speed to measure again. Under the speed, one line tells you about live notes: Fast enough for the live transcript. The model is at least twice as fast as speech. Too slow for the live transcript on this PC; notes are transcribed after the call. The note is still recorded and gets its transcript afterwards. If notes use a model that is too slow, the live transcript stays off for that recording with the message Live transcript needs a cloud speech key or a faster PC. The note is still recorded.

Which one to pick Parakeet V2 is the app's recommendation for English, especially on a PC without a graphics card: it adds punctuation and capitals. It's the one setup offers first. Parakeet V3 if you dictate in a European language. Whisper Small, Base and Tiny : Small is more accurate, Tiny is the smallest and the least accurate. Whisper Medium, Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 are for a PC with a graphics card; see Graphics card .

Languages by engine Language you speak (on Settings › Models and on the Dictation page) is sent to the speech engine for dictation and for meeting notes. What each engine understands, read from the provider's own pages on 20 October 2026: Groq: every language in the list. OpenAI: every language in the list. ElevenLabs: every language in the list except Albanian and Basque. Deepgram: every language in the list except Albanian, Azerbaijani, Basque, Galician, Icelandic, Malayalam, Maltese, Swahili, Uzbek and Welsh. AssemblyAI: every language in the list. Its live transcript does English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese and Italian. Mistral: English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, Arabic, French, Portuguese, Russian, German, Japanese, Korean, Italian and Dutch. Parakeet V3 (this PC): Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Russian and Ukrainian. Parakeet V2 and the English Whisper models (this PC): English only. Whisper Tiny, Base, Small, Medium, Large v3 and Large v3 Turbo (this PC): every language in the list. Where the pages are silent, A9 Voice assumes the newest model: Deepgram's list is Nova-3's for both pre-recorded and live audio, OpenAI's is Whisper's, and Scribe v1 is treated like Scribe v2. When an engine can't do your language, Settings › Models says so and Fix this shows the engines that can. See Models .

Without internet With no internet, dictation and notes use a model on this PC by themselves, no clicking needed. For dictation, A9 Voice picks the best model you have downloaded for your language, in this order for English: Parakeet V2, Parakeet V3, then Whisper Small, Base and Tiny. For another language, only a model that understands it is used: Parakeet V3 if the language is one of its 25, otherwise a multilingual Whisper, the largest you have first. With Detect automatically : Parakeet V3, then a multilingual Whisper, then the English-only models. A language no downloaded model understands gets no offline fallback (rather than a model that would write the wrong language). Models that need a graphics card are only chosen when this PC can run them. The pill says offline when this happened. Notes whose cloud model can't be reached are transcribed on the PC the same way. If you have no model downloaded, dictation ends with No internet .
The models folder Models are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice\models . Click the models folder under the tiles to open it.

Delete a model Open the model's window, click Delete , then click it again to confirm. If the model is in use, the button says what uses it, for example Delete (used for dictation and notes) . Pick another model for dictation first. Deleting removes both versions of a model (processor and graphics card). The shared tools go when the last model goes.

Graphics card New in 0.6.0. A9 Voice can run the larger Whisper models on your graphics card, which is much faster than the processor on a modern graphics card. It is optional, it works with any brand of card that supports DirectX 12, and if anything goes wrong it finishes the job on the processor by itself, so you are never worse off than without it.

What uses the card Whisper Small , Medium , Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 can use the card. Medium , Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 run on the card only. Small has a processor version and a card version, so you can have either. Parakeet , voice detection and telling speakers apart always stay on the processor.

h: Turn it on and download support
t: Turn it on and download support At the top of ON THIS PC is a box with the Use graphics card switch. It is on by default. Under its name you see the card it found and its memory, written like Your card's name · 12.0 GB of memory . Below it, Graphics-card support is a small one-time download (the page shows its size: 23.9 MB). It holds the software that lets the models use your card. A9 Voice checks it when it arrives. 1: the switch. 2: the one-time download. Click Download next to Graphics-card support . A progress line shows Downloading… … of … (…%) and Cancel stops it. When it is done the line says Ready. Checked when it was downloaded. and the button becomes Remove . Remove deletes it; Download brings it back. Cancel stops the download. Remove deletes it again. You don't have to do this first. Downloading a card model downloads the support with it if it isn't there yet, and the model's window lists it: graphics-card support (23.9 MB, once) .

h: Download a model for the card
t: Download a model for the card Click a model's tile, for example Large v3 Turbo . The window says Runs on and your card's name, then It needs about 3.5 GB of graphics memory. Click Download . Support comes with it the first time. For Small (multilingual) you choose: Download for the graphics card or Download for the processor . Add the AI models that write your meeting summaries, answer Ask, and tidy your dictation with Enhance with AI. Use a cloud key or a model on your own PC. A language model reads text and writes text. Speech models turn your voice into words; language models do things with the words: Summaries: after a meeting, one request writes the summary, a title and tags for the note. Ask: answers your questions about one note, about the call you are in right now, or across all your notes. Enhance with AI: tidies each dictation before it is typed: removes “um” and “uh”, fixes punctuation and capitals. None of this is required. Dictation and recording work without a language model; you just don't get summaries, Ask or Enhance. Keys live in Settings › Models , under Providers and keys › LANGUAGE MODELS . Which model does which job is chosen at the top, under What each job uses (see Models ). The speech engines are on that page too. To see how to choose them for dictation and notes: 1: the providers. 2: your own server. A tile with a blue Add key button has no key yet; a gear means it is set up.

Set up a provider The app offers five: OpenRouter , OpenAI , Anthropic , Groq and Google . The steps are the same for each. Your key goes into Windows Credential Manager, never into a file, a log or the app's storage. Open Settings › Models , scroll to Providers and keys and click the provider's tile. Click the big blue Get your OpenRouter key → button (the name changes with the provider). Your browser opens the provider's key page. There, sign in, create an API key, and copy it. Back in A9 Voice the cursor is already in the key box. Paste it into API key . Check the Model . It is the provider's default for jobs that don't name one. It is a box you can type in; the list offers the provider's usual choices, and you can enter any model name the provider knows. Click Test . A9 Voice sends a short phrase full of fillers (“um so uh the release is on uh Thursday you know”) and shows the cleaned-up answer and the time, for example “So the release is on Thursday.” · 0.64 s . Nothing is saved yet. Click Save . Then choose where to use it with Change on a job under What each job uses . 1: the key button opens OpenRouter's key page. 2: key. 3: model. 4: test. 5: save. The strip under the big button, Get a key , Paste it here , Test , ticks as you go.

Choose which model does what Each job has its own row under What each job uses in Models : Summaries , Ask: Quick , Ask: Deep and Enhance . Change opens a searchable list of every model your providers offer, with its context window and price. Ask: Deep also shows what one answer costs.

Summaries and titles Summaries picks the model that writes the summary, title and tags. The other three follow it unless you give them their own. Leave it on Automatic and A9 Voice uses the first one you have set up, in this order: OpenRouter (the newest Claude Haiku, Claude Haiku 5.5 today), Anthropic (the same), OpenAI (GPT-4.1 mini), Groq. Groq comes last because a long meeting can be more than a free Groq key allows per minute. Any other model you set up, including your own server, is tried after those. The Summary model row in Settings › Transcript & summary is the same choice. Automatic shows which model it would use.

Long meetings Some models take only so much text in one request. Groq's free tier, for example, allows its GPT-OSS models 8,000 tokens a minute, which is less than a 30-minute meeting. When a meeting is more than the Summary model takes at once, A9 Voice writes it in parts: it reads the transcript a part at a time, never cutting a turn in two, keeps short notes on each part, then puts the notes together into the same summary, title, tags and action items as any other. The finished summary looks the same. Where Groq's per-minute limit asks for it, A9 Voice waits for the minute to pass, so a long meeting takes a few minutes longer. While it works the note says Writing summary… part 2 of 4 , and waiting for Groq's per-minute limit when it is waiting. You can have it the other way. Settings › Transcript & summary › Long meetings has two choices: Chunk on the same model (the default): the Summary model writes the meeting in parts. Use fallback model : when another model you have set up takes the whole meeting in one request, it writes the summary instead, and the Summary model is tried after it. With Groq as the only language model, Settings › Models says under Summaries that long meetings are handled in parts and take a bit longer. Another provider's key makes them single-pass. A meeting that failed before with request too large for Groq's per-minute token cap on this model in the last 30 days is summarized again by itself the first time you open this version, oldest first, one at a time. Nothing needs a click. If it still can't be done, the note names the limit and when it resets, for example Groq's daily token limit for this model is used up; resets in 3 h. Try another model or try again later.

Ask Ask: Quick and Ask: Deep each take their own model, or Same as Summaries . Deep reads more passages, so a stronger model is worth it; the list marks models that are Good for Deep . Ask: Quick also thinks of the extra search words for a Deep answer.
Enhance Enhance follows Summaries until you pick a model for it, here or under Settings › Dictation › Enhance with AI › Model . A small, fast model keeps dictation quick.

The AI chip The AI: chip at the top of every window shows the model Summaries use now. Click it to switch: Automatic (with the model it would pick) or one of your set-up models. When Enhance or Ask uses a different model, the chip says +1 override . Settings… opens the Models page. When a model recently failed or hit a limit, the chip shows an amber dot for 10 minutes. The menu says what happened and who answered instead, for example OpenRouter rate limit (429) 2 min ago. Anthropic · Claude Haiku 4.5 answered instead. The amber dot means a recent problem.

When a model fails For summaries and Ask, if the chosen model is rate-limited, takes too long, can't take a request that big, or the provider has an error or rejects the key, A9 Voice tries the next model you have set up, one per provider, in the order above. The footer says why: after: Groq rate limit (429) or after: request too large for Groq's per-minute token cap on this model . A request known not to fit is skipped without being sent. With no internet it stops, because the next one would fail the same way. So the most reliable setup is two providers with keys. Enhance is different: it uses only its own model and has a short time limit. If it can't answer in time, you get the text as heard (see below).

Enhance with AI Enhance tidies each dictation before it is typed. It is off until you turn it on, in Settings › Dictation , under Enhance with AI . Model, style, time limit and your own instructions. Enhance with AI: the switch. It removes “um” and “uh”, fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. Model: the model that does it. Same as Summaries is the default. If no model is set up, the row says Add a key in Settings › Models first. Until then, text is pasted as heard. Style: Light cleanup or Formal . Formal only adjusts the tone a little: it can expand contractions and swap very casual words for neutral ones. It never adds content. Wait at most: 1.0 s , 1.5 s (the starting value), 2.0 s or 3.0 s . Past this, the raw text is pasted so dictation never stalls. Custom instructions: your own rules, for example how a name should be spelled. They can't override the rules below.

What it never does It never rewrites, shortens, reorders, summarizes, translates or answers what you said. If you dictate a question, you get the question, tidied, not an answer. What you dictated is treated as text to edit, never as instructions.

When it is skipped Dictation never fails because of Enhance. When Enhance is too slow, fails, or returns something that doesn't look like a cleanup (much longer or shorter than what you said), the text is pasted as heard. In Transcribe , the item shows AI too slow · as heard , AI failed · as heard or AI reply skipped · as heard , and a good one shows AI with the time. A link on each item switches between Show original and Show enhanced . Enhance sends the text of each dictation to the model's provider. Pick a model on your own PC if that matters; see below.

What your notes, dictation and Ask cost at your own keys' rates, how the estimate is made, and how to change the prices it uses. A9 Voice is free. The speech and language services you connect bill you directly, with your own keys. Settings › Usage & cost estimates that bill. It has four tabs: Overview , Savings , History and Prices . The estimate is built from what A9 Voice sent and a price table, so your provider's own bill is always the final word. Overview, for a fictional October.

What is counted Every time something is sent to a service you pay for, A9 Voice writes it down, with the model and how it was sent: A meeting's audio, live. With the live transcript on and a Deepgram key saved, each side of the call (you, and the other people) is streamed while the Live window is open. That is billed at the provider's live rate, for each side, for as long as it streams: only the seconds that were really sent are counted, and a meeting nobody watched has none. A meeting's audio, after the call. When the meeting ends, each side is uploaded again to the Meeting notes model for the final transcript, at its after-the-call rate. A side that was silent is not uploaded and costs nothing. Dictation. Each clip you dictate, at the after-the-call rate of the dictation model that answered. Dictation on this PC costs nothing. Summaries, Ask and Enhance. Each call to a language model, by the tokens the provider counted. OpenRouter also says what each call cost, and that number is used instead of the table. A meeting you watched is billed twice for the part you watched: once live, once after the call. The live part runs only while the window is open ( Settings › Notes › Live window › Live transcript ), and it goes to Deepgram when another engine writes the notes only if you chose that. Set it to Off if you only want the final notes. Models on this PC (Parakeet, Whisper) are always $0.00.

Overview Pick a period at the top right: this month (the default), last month , 90 days or All time . Everything on the tab follows it. The gauge shows what you spent against an optional monthly budget . The pale arc is where the month ends if you keep this pace. With no budget the arc scales to that projection and the card says Set a budget . Over budget it turns amber and says so in words. Cost per meeting hour is what a meeting costs per hour of recording, transcript and summary together. Set a target and the bar shows it, and says how many cents you are over it. Meetings shows the count, the hours, and a small line of daily spend. Imported notes aren't counted: nothing was billed for them. Dictation shows the cost, the count, the minutes and the engine. When dictation is free, it says about how much the same minutes would have cost on the cloud model you use for Meeting notes. Summaries & Ask shows their cost, their share of everything you spend, and which providers it went to. Daily spend has a bar for every day, split by provider. Point at a bar, or press the left and right arrow keys once the chart has focus, to read that day. A dashed line is the average per day. By provider is the same money by provider, with one sentence about where most of it goes. Most expensive lists the three notes that cost the most. Click one to open it.

Savings The Savings tab asks one question: are you on the right models for what you do? It reads the last 30 days of your own usage. A verdict for each job , in the same order and with the same names as the model chips at the top: Dictation , Meeting notes and AI (summaries and Ask). Good fit means nothing comparable is both more than a quarter cheaper and at least $1 a month cheaper at your pace. Otherwise it says Could save and how much a month. Only a Could save counts toward the number on the tab and the headline. Dictation on this PC says Already free . How the AI card decides. It takes the tokens your summaries and Ask used in the last 30 days and prices them on the model you use today , then on each other model you have a key for, so money you spent on a model you have since left is never counted as a saving. It only suggests a model of the same tier or better : Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1 mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-OSS 120B are Standard; GPT-OSS 20B, GPT-4.1 nano, GPT-4o mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite are Basic. A model A9 Voice has no tier for (OpenRouter's Any model , a custom API) is never suggested and never compared against, and a model with no price says so. When it says Could save it names the model ( Switch to GPT-4.1 mini to save $1.40/mo ) with a Switch button. A call whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens is priced at the model's long-prompt rate: Claude Haiku 5.5 charges five times its usual price for those. A price check (amber) appears when a provider you use was billed in a way the price table has no rate for, or when a price you typed is far from the shipped one. It links to Prices. The map puts each meeting engine by what it costs per audio hour after the call (left is cheaper) and by its live speed: Live, instant , After the call only or Live, falls behind . Your engine is ringed. A card for each option : what it would cost a month at your pace, what you would save a month and a year, its live speed, how well it tells speakers apart, and its accuracy. Accuracy says Not measured yet until you run a comparison. Your live transcript. Deepgram streams a live transcript from the cloud, and so does AssemblyAI when it writes your notes (billed by how long the stream stays connected). The monthly figure uses the live hours really sent, so the default (stream only while the window is open) shows up as less to pay right away. If you chose Deepgram for the live part while another engine writes the notes, a card says it stays on, billed separately. A nudge for "Always". If Live transcript is set to Always and the Live window was closed for most of the streamed time in the last 30 days, a line says how many hours and what they cost, with Switch to While open to change it in one click. Switch on a meeting engine card changes the Meeting notes engine after you confirm, and nothing else: Dictation, Summaries and Ask keep their models, and notes you already have stay as they are. With no key saved for that provider it takes you to Settings › Models to add one. Switch on the AI card changes only the AI chip, after you confirm, to a model you already have a key for. Compare on a meeting sends one recent meeting's audio to a second provider after the call and shows both transcripts' word counts, how many words differ, speaker counts, the time it took and its cost. It shows the cost before it sends anything, it counts in Usage & cost like any upload, and your note is not changed. The result fills in that engine's Accuracy and Source . A model on this PC can't be compared this way. The other side of the comparison is the transcript your note already has, from whichever engine wrote that meeting, which may not be the engine you use today: the window names it above the provider list ( Compared against: AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro , or your existing transcript on an older note that didn't keep it), and that engine is left out of the list, because it can't be compared with itself.

History Every note and dictation, newest first. Today and Yesterday are open. The rest of the month is one group, Earlier in October , and every past month is one line with its total. Open one and it shows 25 rows at a time, with Newer and Older buttons. A day's dictations are one row, for example Dictation · 53 clips . A row shows the note's title, each provider it used and how ( live , after the call , on this PC ), its length and its cost. Click a note to open it. All , Meetings , Dictation and Ask filter the rows. The search box looks in titles. Export CSV saves every row that matches the filter and the search: date, kind, title, providers, mode, units and cost. The calendar colors each day by what it cost; darker is more. The box under it gives the busiest day, the longest meeting and the averages. A row that says Not tracked is a note nothing was recorded for. That is every note imported from another app, and any note whose engine was never written down. It is not counted as $0.00. A stretch that mixes older notes with newer ones says so: older notes were written down before live and after-the-call audio were told apart, so they are priced at the after-the-call rate. No usage is deleted. Clearing your dictation history or deleting a note does not take its spending out of these pages.

Prices Every estimate is units times the price of that model, in that mode. Ships with the app. Each provider's public list price, checked on the date shown on the page. A new version of A9 Voice brings new defaults. You can override any price. Got a discount or a credit? Click a price and type yours. Press Enter to keep it, Esc to cancel; clear the box to go back to the shipped number. An edited price is marked Edited and stays through every update. A price you change re-prices everything in the period, old rows too. Real cost where offered. OpenRouter reports what each call cost. A9 Voice uses that number, and its row says Real cost per call . Speech has two rates: After the call and Live , per audio hour. Language models have Input and Output , per 1 million tokens. A dash means that model has no rate for that mode, and anything billed that way shows no price and counts as $0.00 until you set one. Only the providers you use show at first. Show unused providers lists the rest. A new live rate carries a new mark the first time you open the tab. Reset to defaults removes every price you typed, after a confirmation.

If something looks wrong The total is lower than your provider's bill. Check Live in Prices: a rate that is blank is counted as $0.00. Check for a promotion or a discount your account has; type that rate and the page follows it. A note says Not tracked. It was imported, or it was recorded before A9 Voice kept usage. Nothing is hidden: it simply has no numbers. Costs went up after an update. Meetings recorded before this version were priced after the call only. The live stream is now counted too, which is what Deepgram bills.
