Notes records a call, a video or a voice note from your microphone and your computer's audio, with no bot in the meeting. Use this page to start, watch and stop a recording, by hand or by itself. New to it? Watch Sara record a first meeting.

What Notes records Notes records two sides at once and keeps them apart: Microphone (Me): your side. The meeting app keeps using the microphone as before; nothing is muted or changed. Computer audio (Them): whatever your speakers or headset play, which is the other people on a call. No bot joins your meeting. A9 Voice listens on your PC. While you record, the note is already in the Notes list. When you stop, it turns into a finished note: first the transcript, then the summary. See The note page for what you get.

Turn Notes on first Notes records nothing until you turn it on. Until then, Notes shows what it does and one button, Try Notes free for 30 days . Press it and the 30 days start: no signup, no card, and a PC that never presses it never starts a trial. If a call starts before that, a small card asks Want notes for this call? with Start trial and Not now . Nothing is recorded unless you press Start trial , and Not now keeps the card quiet for 7 days. If you were already using Notes (you have notes, or a meeting app set to start by itself) when you updated to 0.7.4, A9 Voice starts the 30 days for you on that first launch, so your recordings never just stop. The Notes page says so once, with Buy Notes , Enter a license key and Got it . Your notes stay in the list either way.

The recording-consent notice Under Try Notes free , and under Start trial on that card, a short line says that by starting Notes you agree to get any consent the law requires before you record other people, because some places, including several US states, require everyone's consent. Pressing the button is the agreement; there is no checkbox. Learn more opens Recording consent . If your trial was started for you, or you already had a license, you see the same line once as a small card on the Notes page and the first time the recording bar appears. Got it closes it. Settings › Notes › Recording always shows it. The notice never blocks, delays or stops a recording: no bot joins your meeting and A9 Voice does not announce itself, so telling the people on the call is up to you.

Start a recording by hand Use this for anything: a call A9 Voice did not notice, a video, a voice note. Open Notes and press Record . You can also press Ctrl + Alt + N anywhere, or right-click the A9 Voice tray icon and choose Start recording . The Record button, top right of Notes. The recording bar appears on your screen and the note appears at the top of the list marked Recording . The sidebar button changes to Stop with the time. If you pressed the button in the app, A9 Voice also opens the new note. While you record, the note is in the list. A note that has just been stopped shows Transcribing or Summarizing. You can change the record key in Settings › Notes › Recording ( Record key ), or clear it.

h: Let A9 Voice start it for you
t: Let A9 Voice start it for you

Choose the apps A9 Voice can start a recording by itself when a meeting app starts using your microphone. Open Settings › Notes › Recording and look at Meeting apps : Turn on the apps you use. Microsoft Teams and Zoho Cliq and Zoho Meeting are on to begin with. The others are Zoom , Webex , Slack huddles , Discord and Browser calls , and they start off. For a call in a web page (Google Meet, or Teams or Zoom on the web, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox), turn on Browser calls . Any web page that uses the microphone then counts. A9 Voice asks Windows' audio system which apps are using any of your microphones, not only the one set as the default, so a call on a USB webcam's microphone counts too. On Windows builds that still keep a record of microphone use, it reads that as well, and a call is on when either shows it. 3. For any other app, use Other app . Join a call in that app first, press Choose from apps using your mic now… , then press Add next to the app. Press Remove later to forget it. Settings › Notes › Recording. Teams and Zoho Cliq are on by default. Other app lists what is using your microphone at this moment. Apps already covered above say so. Dictation never starts a recording.

How it notices a call A9 Voice reads the list Windows keeps of which apps are using the microphone (the same list behind Windows' own "microphone in use" icon). It only reads it; it never changes anything. It looks every 2 seconds. The app must hold the microphone for 5 seconds in a row before a recording starts. A short blip does not start one. The app must also be running. An app that crashed and left a stale entry does not count. Only the apps you turned on count. If two of them are in a call at once, Teams goes first. If you discard a recording, or stop one that A9 Voice started, in the middle of a call, A9 Voice will not start another one in that same call. It waits until the app lets go of the microphone.

The 8-second notice When a call starts a recording, a card appears above the bar: The notice shows which app, which template, and a countdown. Read it. It says which app it heard and which summary template it will use ( Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Summary template ). Press Discard within 8 seconds if this was not a call you wanted. The recording and its note are deleted. Press Keep , or do nothing. The card goes away after 8 seconds and the recording carries on.

The recording bar The bar is a small window that sits on top of your other windows. It never takes the keyboard away from the app you are in, so clicking it will not interrupt what you are typing. While the live feed is open the bar is its header: the Live window hangs directly off the bar, and the two move as one. The bar at rest: level tile, state and time, Pause, Stop, Snip, the Live feed button and Minimize. The tile on the left moves with the sound on either side. Under Recording is the time so far, with a red dot. Pause stops recording. Press it again ( Resume ) to carry on. Paused time is silence in the recording. Stop ends the recording. It asks first (see below). Snip adds a screenshot to the note ( Ctrl + Alt + S does the same). Only Snip adds screenshots; Windows screenshots stay out unless you turn them on. See Live window . Live feed shows or hides the live transcript under the bar. The button is filled while the feed is open. Hiding the feed never stops or pauses the recording. A9 Voice remembers whether you left it open, for your next meeting too. Minimize shrinks the bar to its left part, in place (see below). Double-clicking the bar does the same. Every button has a tooltip, and all of them are on the bar without a hover. Rest the mouse on the bar to show the two pickers for what is recorded, to the right of Minimize . Nothing else moves, and neither does the Live window under it: 1 Pause, 2 Stop, 3 Snip, 4 Live feed, 5 Minimize, 6 Microphone, 7 Computer audio. Microphone and Computer audio choose what is recorded (next section).

h: Choose the microphone and computer audio
t: Choose the microphone and computer audio Rest the mouse on the bar and press the Microphone button (or Computer audio ). Pick one: Auto (Windows default) follows whatever Windows uses, and shows its name underneath. A device from the list. Off to stop recording that side. The last line shows the result, for example Recording from: and the device name. It says Not recording from this source when you chose Off . The list is the same for Computer audio. The change applies straight away, to this recording only. With Auto on computer audio, A9 Voice listens to every output and uses the one that is playing, so a headset that Windows switches to call mode still works. The Computer audio button only shows when the recording includes computer audio. To set the defaults for every recording, use Settings › Notes › Recording › What gets recorded : Settings › Notes › Recording, further down. Microphone (Me) is Same as Transcribe unless you pick another one. Computer audio (Them) is on or off, and Output device follows the Windows default unless you pick one. A summary template can switch computer audio off for the notes that use it ( Capture system audio in Templates and export ).

h: Move it, minimize it, bring it back
t: Move it, minimize it, bring it back Move the bar: press on its background (not on a button) and drag. With the Live feed open, drag the bar or the feed's header: both move together, with no gap, even onto another screen. Near a screen edge the bar snaps to that edge. It always stays fully on a screen, never under the taskbar and never lost off the edge. Where it opens: the lower left of your main screen, just above the taskbar. A9 Voice remembers where you put it for each set of screens, so a laptop on its own and the same laptop on a dock each keep their own place. One bar, three sizes: Small (the animated level bars, the time and a › button), the full Bar , and the bar with the Live feed hung under it. They share the same left edge, the same top and the same screen. Minimize (or a double-click on the bar) shrinks the bar to Small where it is ; nothing moves to another place or another screen, and the Live feed hides with it. A paused recording shows an amber pause mark instead of the red dot, and a dimmer level tile. Bring it back: click › , or click Small itself (a press that moves is a drag, not a click). Hovering Small does nothing but show a tooltip. The bar opens in place, with the Live feed open or closed as you left it. The left-click on the A9 Voice tray icon and the show / hide key ( Ctrl + Alt + B , Show recording bar in Settings › Notes › Recording ) switch between Small and the bar the same way, so something is always on screen while a recording runs. Move it in any size: press on the bar or on Small and drag. Near a screen edge it snaps there, and it always stays fully on a screen, never under the taskbar. Dragging Small moves the whole thing, and the bar opens from the new spot (the Live feed opens above it if there is no room below). Small is always on top of other windows, the main A9 Voice window included. Remembered: A9 Voice remembers the size you left it at and the spot, for each set of screens, so a laptop on its own and the same laptop on a dock each keep their own place. If the screen it was on is gone, it goes back to the lower left of your main screen. Start over: right-click the tray icon and choose Reset bar position . The bar goes back to the lower left of your main screen. Small: the left part of the bar, same height and left edge. The pulsing dot and the time, and › to expand it. Fade the minimized bar in Settings › Notes › Recording makes Small fade to 60% after 5 seconds. It comes back to full when the mouse is on it. It is off to begin with. Paused: grey tile and the word Paused.
Stop recording

Stop, or stop and discard Press the red square on the bar. The bar asks Stop recording? Press Stop to keep the recording. A9 Voice saves it and starts the transcript. Press the x (or Esc ) to carry on recording. Stop keeps the recording. Stop & discard asks once more. To throw it away instead, press Stop & discard… . The bar asks Discard this recording? It's deleted from this PC. Press Discard to delete it, or Keep recording to carry on. Discard deletes the audio, the files and the note. Every other way of stopping asks the same question. The tray's Stop recording , the record key, the Stop button in the sidebar and on the note page, and the stop button in the Live window bring the bar back (from the mini pill too) and put Stop recording? on it, with Stop , Stop & discard… and the x . Nothing stops until you answer. The cards that already ask something, Meeting ended and Still recording? , have their own Stop now . After you stop, a card says Saved. Transcribing… . When the note is finished the card says Note ready, with an Open button.

h: When a recording stops by itself
t: When a recording stops by itself The call ends. When a recording belongs to a call and the app lets go of the microphone for 4 seconds, A9 Voice shows Meeting ended , Stopping in 10 s. with Stop now , Next meeting and Keep recording , and a thin bar that runs down. If you do nothing it stops and keeps the recording. This also applies to a recording you started by hand while a call was going: it is linked to the call and ends with it. Stop now during the countdown never holds the next call back: a call that starts afterwards is recorded by itself as usual. Keep recording turns it into your own recording: only you stop it (or the end of the next call). Your next meeting starts right away. Press Next meeting , or press the record key during the countdown: the first meeting is saved and the next one starts straight away, in its own note, with less than a second of audio missing between them. The toast says Saved. Recording the next meeting. If a call is already on the microphone it is linked to the new note; otherwise the note links to the call when one starts. The call comes back. If the microphone opens again during the countdown, the countdown is cancelled and the card changes to Call is back with New meeting and Same meeting . Pick New meeting when this is a different meeting: the first one is saved and a new note starts. With no answer in 15 seconds it stays the same meeting, which is right for a reconnect after a network blip. Without an answer it stays the same meeting. The meeting's name changed. A9 Voice reads the meeting window's title while a call recorded by itself runs. By default it only writes down in the log ( logs\meeting-titles.jsonl on this PC) that a different name means a new meeting and would split the note; it doesn't split yet. Nobody is talking. A recording you started yourself asks Still recording? after a stretch of silence on both sides. You choose how long in Settings › Notes › Recording › "Still recording?" : 5, 10, 15 (the default), 30 or 60 minutes. The card says how long is left. Press Keep recording to carry on, or Stop now . With no answer it stops and keeps the recording 2 minutes later. If someone starts talking again, the card goes away. Paused time counts as silence. Recordings that a call started do not ask; they end with the call. The card counts down. Any sound clears it. Four hours. Every recording stops after 4 hours, and the recording is kept. A recording you start by hand with no call going on is never stopped by A9 Voice except by the last two rules: silence and the four-hour limit. If you would rather not wait, set Settings › Notes › Recording › Meeting ended countdown to 5 s , 10 s (the default) or 30 s . Off stops the recording as soon as the call is seen to have ended, 4 seconds after hang-up, with no card.

h: When a call is not recorded
t: When a call is not recorded If Settings › Notes › Recording › Wait while another recording app runs is on (it is on to begin with), A9 Voice does not start by itself while another recording app is capturing the call, so two apps never record the same call. An app that is merely open, with its own recording off, does not hold A9 Voice back. When that happens the bar says so, so a missing recording is never a surprise: Press Record now to record the call anyway. Read Teams call detected: not recording and Another recording app is capturing it. Press Record now if you want A9 Voice to record it too. The message stays for 30 seconds. The Record button and the record key always work, with or without this setting.

After you stop The note stays in the Notes list and shows what it is doing: Transcribing… (with a percentage when the speech model runs on this PC), Summarizing… , or Waiting… . A note that could not be finished shows Needs a look ; open it to see why. A call that A9 Voice started is called "Teams call" (or the app's name) until the note is named. A recording you started by hand is called "Recording". When the note is ready, a card on the bar says Note ready with an Open button. The speech model that makes the transcript is chosen in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Speech model . It can be a cloud service with your own key or a model on this PC; see Speech models . Telling the other people apart (Speaker 2, Speaker 3 and so on) depends on that model. Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Mistral (Voxtral) and models on this PC tell speakers apart. Other models only label lines as you and the other side. Turn Identify speakers off to stop separating them. The summary comes from the language model and template you chose; see Language models and Templates and export .

Name notes after the meeting Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Name notes after the meeting has three choices: On: during the first 90 seconds of a call, A9 Voice reads the title of the meeting window in Teams, Zoho Cliq or your browser and uses it as the note's name. The folder reads like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". Windows with no real meeting name, such as the main Teams window, are ignored. Only log what it would choose: A9 Voice does not rename anything. It records what it would have chosen in a small log file on this PC, so you can check it. Off: the AI names the note. A title you type yourself always wins. When no usable name is found, the AI names the note after the summary.

h: Record something that is not a call
t: Record something that is not a call A video, a webinar, a voice note to yourself: press Record (or Ctrl + Alt + N ) and play or speak. A video or webinar comes in on Computer audio ; your own voice comes in on Microphone . In the list the note says Computer audio , Mic only or Mic + computer audio so you can tell them apart. Turn Microphone or Computer audio to Off on the bar if you only want one side. Nothing here stops on its own except the rules above. Press Stop when you are done.

Dictating during a meeting Dictating into another app while you record does not end up in the note. While you dictate, the microphone side of the recording is silent, and the words you dictated are removed from the transcript. This is Keep dictation out of notes in Settings › Notes › Live window and it is on to begin with. Turn it off if you want everything you say in the note.

The recording badge While you record, Windows shows it outside A9 Voice's own windows: Taskbar button: a small red dot that pulses gently about once a second. While paused it is a grey pause mark. The A9 Voice icon itself never changes color. Tray icon: the usual icon with a small red dot while recording, a grey pause mark while paused, and the plain icon when nothing records, so a minimized bar still tells you the state. Hover it for A9 Voice - Recording 12:34 or A9 Voice - Paused 12:34 ; the time keeps counting. Click it to switch between the bar and Small. Tray menu: Stop recording (it says Start recording when nothing records), Show recording bar , and Reset bar position . Red is only used for recording, so a red dot always means a recording is running.
Your responsibility Some places require everyone's permission before you record them. You are responsible for any consent your location requires before you record or recognize people.

If something goes wrong A call did not start a recording. Check that its app is turned on in Settings › Notes › Recording , that the app is really using the microphone (join with audio), and that the call is longer than 5 seconds. Check Wait while another recording app runs too. Press Record to start by hand. I do not see the bar. Look for Small, the left part of the bar (lower left by default). Press Ctrl + Alt + B or left-click the tray icon to switch between Small and the bar, or choose Reset bar position in the tray menu. The other people are not in the note. Check that Computer audio is not Off on the bar and that the right output is chosen. Everything is labeled Me and Them. The speech model does not separate speakers. Choose another in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary . More in Troubleshooting .

Related Live window : the transcript beside a call, and naming the people. The note page : what you get when the recording is finished. Speech models : cloud or on this PC. Keyboard shortcuts and Settings reference .

What it is The Live window hangs off the recording bar while a note records. It is a working copy of the transcript: each person has their own color, and you can tell A9 Voice who is who as you go. When the call ends, the finished note is made from the whole recording, and the names you gave are carried into it. You do not need it. A9 Voice records without it. The other people can be told apart while the call goes on by a cloud service or, free and private, on your own PC: see Speakers on this PC . Use it when you want names on the note, or answers and markers during the call. For starting and stopping, see Recording a meeting . To see it open beside a call, with the first lines coming in: 1 Speaker strip, 2 Now, 3 Who's talking? field, 4 Live, Ask and Notes tabs, 5 Ask field. Top to bottom the window has: The Ask anything about this meeting… field. A header with what is recording ( Teams call , or Manual recording when you started it), a level meter for Me and for Them , and the time. The speaker strip : one chip per person. The transcript. Each line has a name, the time since the recording began, and the text. A grey line is not finished yet. Now (who is talking) and the Who's talking? field. The footer: the tabs Live , Ask and Notes , the markers Action , Callout and Decision , then the microphone and computer-audio pickers, Snip , pause and stop buttons, a gear and, in the lower right corner, a chevron that hides the feed.

The window holds still The transcript follows the live end, so new lines keep pushing it up. That would move a name under your pointer just as you click it, so the window holds still when you are about to: While the pointer is over the transcript the button says Live · paused . New lines keep arriving below. About a second after the pointer leaves, the window jumps to live again. Press the button to jump at once. While a name box is open the button says Live · paused while naming . The box stays where it opened and the line you clicked stays where it is, whatever the feed does. When the box closes (a name, Not sure , Esc or a click outside) the window jumps to live. When you scroll up to read , the button says Jump to live . Press it to catch up.

Open it The recording bar always has a Live feed button, next to Snip . Press it to open the feed under the bar; the button is filled while the feed is open. Press it again to close it. The Live feed button, at rest. Pressing it again hides the feed. The recording goes on. A9 Voice remembers whether you left the feed open. With Open the Live window when a meeting starts on (it is, to begin with), the next recording opens it the way you left it. If you hide it, it stays hidden for the next meeting until you open it again. If the bar is minimized or hidden, a Live window button elsewhere (for example on the note page while it records) brings the bar back first, then opens the feed under it.

Hide it Two ways, with the same result: press Live feed on the bar, or press the chevron in the lower right corner of the feed (tooltip Hide live feed ). Both collapse to the bar only. Neither stops or pauses the recording, and the live transcript keeps its minute of grace before the cloud stream stops. The feed also closes by itself when the recording stops.

One unit with the bar While a note records the bar is the Live window's header, and the feed hangs directly off it: no gap, their left edges lined up, one surface, with the corners where they join squared off. Where the bar is fixed at the right edge of the screen, the right edges line up instead. It opens below the bar. If there is no room below (the bar is near the bottom of the screen), it opens above the bar, and the bar becomes the bottom edge of the unit. It never goes off the screen. Move the unit by dragging the bar, or the feed's header (the title row). Both go together, onto another screen too. Resize the feed from its edges. It keeps hanging off the bar, and A9 Voice remembers its size and the bar's place for the next meeting and the next start. Minimize the bar and it shrinks to Small where it is (the level bars, the time and a › button); the feed goes with it. Click › and the bar opens in place with the feed as you left it, from the spot you dragged Small to if you moved it. If there is no room below the bar, the feed opens above it. Stop and discard questions replace the bar's buttons in place. The feed stays where it is. With no recording running, the Live window opened from the main window keeps its older behavior: you can drag it by its header to put it somewhere else (it undocks and keeps its own place and size for each screen), and a Dock under bar button appears in the header: Dock under bar puts it back with the recording bar. Press Dock under bar , or right-click the tray icon and choose Reset bar position , which also resets the bar. As soon as a recording starts, the feed is part of the bar again. Pin on top (the pin button in the header) keeps the window above other windows. It is on to begin with. The setting is remembered. The smallest size is 380 by 320 pixels. At narrow sizes the markers and pickers wrap onto a second line. At 380 pixels wide everything is still there.

h: The Live transcript needs a speech source
t: The Live transcript needs a speech source The live lines come from a live speech service, separate from the transcript of the finished note. Where they come from depends on which speech model writes your notes: Deepgram writes the notes. With a Deepgram key, the two sides stream to Deepgram while the window is open. Deepgram bills it per channel, at its live rate. AssemblyAI writes the notes. With its key, the two sides stream to AssemblyAI's Universal-Streaming while the window is open, on the same key (no second bill). The window says Live transcript via AssemblyAI with what it costs; the other people's side has speaker labels, so each person is their own speaker to name. Another cloud service writes the notes (ElevenLabs, Groq, OpenAI or one you added). If a speech model on this PC is installed and keeps up with real time, the live lines are made there, free, and the window says Live transcript on this PC (free). Nothing streams to a cloud service. Another cloud service writes the notes, and no model on this PC takes the live part. Nothing streams to Deepgram on its own, because Deepgram is not the one writing your notes and would bill you separately. The window says so and offers Use Deepgram for the live transcript ; once you do, it says Live transcript via Deepgram, billed separately. Without a Deepgram key it says Live transcript needs a speech model on this PC or a Deepgram key. with an Open Models link. Notes use a model on this PC. The live lines are made there too, if that model keeps up. If it doesn't, the window says Live transcript needs a cloud speech key or a faster PC. The note is still recorded. Settings › Notes › Live window › Live transcript sets when the cloud stream runs, or turns it off. See Speech models .

When the live transcript runs The live transcript is billed by your speech provider at its live rate, and your notes are made from the whole recording after the call either way. So by default it runs while the Live window is open : It starts when the window shows and keeps going for a minute after you close or minimize it, so closing and reopening quickly changes nothing. When you open the window again it starts a new stream from that moment. Where the window was closed, the transcript shows one quiet line: Live transcript paused while the window was closed. Your notes will include everything. Names you give while the window is open still land on the right people in the finished note. Each stream numbers its speakers on its own, so the same person can show as a second speaker after a gap; Merge puts them together. The first time a gap appears, a one-time tip explains it. Got it closes it for good. A recording that nobody watches therefore sends no live audio at all: Usage & cost shows no live line for it. Always keeps the old behavior (the stream runs for the whole recording); Off never streams. A model on this PC isn't billed, so it keeps running whatever you choose. The recording itself never depends on the live transcript. The audio, Still recording? , and stopping when the call ends work the same with the stream off. If you hear the call from speakers instead of a headset, your microphone also hears them. A9 Voice does not show those repeats as lines from you.

Name the people If a live source can't tell the other people apart (the window then says This service can't tell the other speakers apart live. Your notes will. ), a name you give covers the line being spoken and the speech that follows it until a pause, not everything that side has said so far. Undo takes it back, and the finished note separates them. New to naming people? Watch Sara name a speaker live, then on the note page.

The speaker strip and Now The strip lists people in the order they first spoke, except that you come first once you have said something, under your own name from Settings › Account . Everyone else starts as Speaker 2 , Speaker 3 and so on. Each has a color; the first seven are different, then the colors repeat. The chip of whoever is speaking glows, and stays lit for a few seconds after they stop. Now shows only who is speaking now, for example Now: Speaker 2 , or Now: — before anyone has spoken. Under it, small and grey, after Marcus says who spoke before them. A new speaker only shows after about 1.5 seconds of continuous speech, so a short "yes" does not make it flicker. Your own chip is not clickable. It is you. With many people on the call the strip wraps and scrolls: The strip wraps; the window keeps the transcript in view.

h: Name a speaker from their chip
t: Name a speaker from their chip Click the chip of the person you want to name. The box asks Who is Speaker 2? (or Rename Speaker 2 if they already have a name). Type a name, or pick one from the list. The list is one list of everyone you might mean: names you used in this call first, then the people already on the call, your saved voices (if you use Voices ) and names from your other notes. Typing narrows it down by first name, last name or the start of either, in any case: ril and thom both find Riley Thompson, and K puts Kim Jansen above Ana Sharkey. A name already used on this call shows whose it is, and the speaker's own name is listed too, marked current . A name that is not on the list shows last, as + Add "name" to this meeting . Use ↑ and ↓ to move, Enter to choose and Esc to cancel. The note page uses this same picker when you name speakers there. Press Enter or Name . The name goes on every line from that person, past and future, and into the finished note. Press Not sure to close the box without naming anyone. Names used on this call come first. The box is the same size wherever it opens, and it never covers its own buttons. In a short window only the list of people shrinks (and scrolls); the title, the field, Name , Not sure and Apply to stay in view. A9 Voice will not let you give a speaker your own name: That's your own name. Pick the person you mean. What "+ Add" does # The line under + Add says exactly what pressing it will do: Names Speaker 2 · saves a new voice : everything from this speaker gets the name, and with Voices on, the name can teach a new voice after the call. Names Speaker 2 in this meeting : the same, with Voices off. Only this note is named. Names this line only · no voiceprint : one line, with Just this line chosen. A single line never teaches a voice.

h: Add someone who hasn't spoken: + Person
t: Add someone who hasn't spoken: + Person Sometimes you know who is on the call before they have said a word, or one of the people on a track is somebody else. + Person at the end of the strip adds a person to this meeting without waiting for their voice. Press + Person . The box asks Add someone to this meeting . Type a name, or pick one from the list (your saved voices and names from other notes are in it, and typing narrows it down as everywhere else). People already on the call are not listed again. Press Enter or Add . A pill with a dashed outline joins the strip. Rest the pointer on it and its tooltip says no voice yet . An added person has no track and no voiceprint, and adding them changes no line. They are a name you can pick from any line's menu (next section). The × next to the pill takes it away; lines you already named for them keep the name. When someone on the call later gets the same name, the pill goes and that person's chip is used.

Answer a guess With Voices on, A9 Voice can guess who is talking from their voice. A guess shows on the chip as Kim Jansen? . Rest the pointer on the chip. A ✓ and a ✕ appear next to it. Press ✓ if it is right. It names the whole speaker, as if you had typed the name, and shows the Undo line. Press ✕ if it is not them. The chip goes back to Speaker 4 and the name box opens with the guess at the bottom of the list, so you can pick the right person. Or click the chip itself. The box asks Is this Kim Jansen? with ✓ Yes and Someone else… . Enter means Yes. Someone else… takes you to the field. Yes, or Someone else. The guess can still be found by typing its name. In a line's name box (next section), the first row is ✓ Yes, Kim Jansen when the line's speaker is a guess.

h: Name whoever is talking: Who's talking?
t: Name whoever is talking: Who's talking? Use this when someone is talking right now and you want to name them without hunting for their chip. Click the Who's talking? Type a name field and start typing a name. On the first letter, A9 Voice locks on to the person the window shows as talking (not you), or if nobody is, the last other person who spoke. The line above the field changes to Naming Speaker 2 (locked) . The target stays locked, even if someone else starts talking before you press Enter. Press Enter (or Tag ) to apply the name. Press Esc to cancel. If it locked on the wrong person, press change and choose who you meant. change lists the other people on the call. After a name is applied, the bar says Tagged Ana ✓ for a few seconds (the × closes it sooner; in a very short window it stays until the next change). The field goes back to Who's talking? Type a name . Tagged Ana ✓ shows in the bar for a few seconds. If nobody else has spoken yet, it says Nobody else has talked yet. Click a speaker's chip to name them.

h: Fix one line, or everything from a speaker
t: Fix one line, or everything from a speaker Sometimes the person is right but one line is wrong, or a speaker is really two people. Click the name above a line. Lines that are not finished are greyed and cannot be clicked yet. The box asks This is → . Do one of: Type a name, then press Enter or Name . Pick a person from People . Pick one of the pills under In this meeting , or press its number. The pills are the people on the call, then the people you added with + Person , numbered 1 to 9 . With the field empty, pressing a number does what clicking that pill does: a person on the call takes the line; an added person's name goes on it. Once you have typed a letter, digits are part of the name. If the line's speaker is a guess, press the first row, ✓ Yes, Kim Jansen . Under Apply to , choose Just this line or Everything from that speaker. A speaker who has no name yet starts on Everything from , since you most likely mean "this is Ana". A speaker who already has a name starts on Just this line , since you are correcting one mistake. Click a name in the transcript to open it. A line named on its own shows its name with a dotted underline. Click it again to correct it. Typing the name of someone already on the call moves the line to that person. Typing your own name moves it to you. This is the quick way to say "this isn't Ana, it's Riley": click the name above the line, press the number of Riley's pill, done. Apply to decides whether it is that line or everything from the speaker, as it does for a click. Everything from you cannot be renamed or turned into someone else; fix those lines one at a time. With Everything from and a speaker chosen, the two speakers are joined into one (see the next section).

One name, one person A name can belong to only one speaker. If you give a name that someone on the call already has, A9 Voice asks instead of deciding: The question appears above the Who's talking? field. Read Marcus is already Speaker 3. Same person? Press Merge if it is the same person. This speaker's lines, and everything they say from now on, join the other speaker, who keeps their name. Press No, different person if two people share a name. This one becomes Marcus (2) . A name made this way is never used to learn a voice. Press Esc to close the question and do nothing.

Undo Every naming action, including a merge, shows a line with what changed and an Undo button for 10 seconds. Named Speaker 4 → Dana, with Undo. Press Undo within 10 seconds. The window says Undone . Only the newest action can be undone, and the button goes after 10 seconds. An older action cannot be undone any more ( Too late to undo that one. ). Rename the person again to change it.

h: What is learned from your names
t: What is learned from your names Nothing is learned during the call. Undo leaves no trace. A name you gave to a whole speaker can teach that person's voice after the call, but only if Voices is on. A name on a single line, and a name made different like Marcus (2) , never teaches a voice. With Voices on and people already saved, A9 Voice may name someone by itself after they have spoken for about 8 seconds. A sure match names them everywhere. A likely match shows Priya? with a Yes button next to their lines. Pressing Yes counts as a name you gave. Nothing is learned during the call from this either. Your names are carried into the finished note by who was talking at the moment you named them. Look at the speakers on the note page when it is ready: The note page .

Ask during the meeting To see a question asked in the Live window, and the same in your notes: Type a question in the field at the top, for example What was the problem with the approval routing? , and press Enter . The Ask tab shows your question and the answer. It is written from the transcript so far, using the names you gave, and cites the moments as time chips. Click a chip to jump to that line. Pick the language model in the list under the answer. With none set up, the tab says Add a language model key in Settings › Models to ask. See Language models . The answer cites the moment: 12:03. If nothing has been transcribed yet, Ask says so. The transcript text so far goes to the language model you chose, like any Ask. To ask across your finished notes, use the Ask page: see Asking your notes .

Mark moments and add notes The Notes tab holds what you add during the call. Each item lands in the note at that moment. Press Action , Callout or Decision in the footer. A9 Voice stamps this moment and keeps what was just said (the latest line, with its speaker). The header says, for example, Decision marked at 12:26 . To write your own, open the Notes tab, type in Type a note; Enter adds it at this moment , and press Enter . Markers and notes are listed with their time. They show up in the note at that time. See The note page .

Add a screenshot Press Snip in the footer (the number beside it counts the pictures so far) or on the recording bar, or press the Snip key ( Ctrl + Alt + S ). The Windows snipping tool opens. Choose the area. A9 Voice saves it to the note, and the bar shows a thumbnail with Saved to note at 12:03 . Press Undo on that card if you took the wrong one. The picture goes in the note's images folder. Only A9 Snip adds screenshots to a meeting. Press the Snip button on the bar or in the Live window, or the Snip key ( Ctrl + Alt + S to begin with; change it in Settings › Notes › Recording ), and take the picture. A screenshot you take for something else, with Win + Shift + S or PrtScn , stays out of the meeting, and A9 Voice does not read the clipboard for it. To have those in the meeting too, turn on Also add Windows screenshots to the meeting in Settings › Notes › Recording . Then any picture that reaches the clipboard while the recording runs is saved, from any snipping tool. A picture copied before the recording started is not, and the same picture is only ever saved once (a snip that also stays on the clipboard, or an image copied twice). The crop icon in the Live window's footer counts the snips in this meeting ( Snips this meeting (n) ) and follows the note as pictures are added or removed, also after you hide and show the feed or minimize the bar. Snips are placed in the transcript at the moment you took them and are kept in the note's folder under images . Snip works only while a recording is running.

Other buttons Open the note (the document icon in the header) opens the note in the main window. The microphone and speaker buttons choose what is recorded, like the bar. Same as Transcribe / default (microphone) and Windows default (computer audio) follow the usual choice; Off stops that side. The pause and stop buttons work like the bar's. The stop button here does not stop at once: it puts the bar's Stop recording? question up (the bar expands first if it is Small), like every other stop. The gear opens Settings › Notes › Live window .

Settings for the Live window Three switches. Live transcript: when the cloud stream runs. While the live window is open (the default) streams only while the window is showing, plus a minute. Always streams the whole recording. Off means no Live window text; the note is still made afterwards. Use Deepgram for the live transcript: shown when another engine writes your notes. Off by default; Deepgram bills the stream on top of that engine. Open the Live window when a meeting starts: it opens docked to the recording bar and moves with it, open or closed the way you left it. Off means you open it from the bar's Live feed button. Keep dictation out of notes: what you dictate into other apps during a meeting is not recorded as part of it.

If something goes wrong The window says Listening… and stays empty. Nobody has spoken on either side yet, or Computer audio is Off . Check the bar's pickers. The window says "Your network is blocking Deepgram". The network answered in the service's place (a block page), so the Live connection can't be made. The recording goes on and the full transcript with speakers is made when you stop. With a speech model installed on this PC the Live transcript switches to it within a few seconds and says Live transcript on this PC (your network blocks Deepgram) ; nothing is sent to a second paid service. See Troubleshooting . The window says "Live transcript can't connect from this network". The connection to the speech service is blocked, often on a work network. The recording goes on and the full transcript with speakers is made when you stop. A9 Voice keeps trying every 30 seconds, and the line goes away when it connects. With a speech model installed on this PC it switches to that and says "Live transcript on this PC". My words show up under someone else, or theirs under me. Click the name above the line and move it. A headset prevents most of this. A name will not stick. It may belong to another speaker; look for the Same person? question. The window is gone. Press Live window on the bar. If the bar is gone, press Ctrl + Alt + B . More in Troubleshooting .
Related Recording a meeting : the bar, starting and stopping. Voices : recognizing people by voice. The note page : what the finished note shows. Keyboard shortcuts .

Tell the other people on a call apart while it is still going, on your own PC, for free. Nothing is sent anywhere and no key is needed. In the Live window , each person on the other side of the call gets a color and a name, Speaker 2 , Speaker 3 and so on, so you can see who is saying what as it happens. Some speech services do this in the cloud. This page is about doing it on your PC instead, which is how it works when your live transcript is written on your PC (the free setup).

How it works A9 Voice listens to the computer audio , the other people. It never looks at your microphone: you are always Me , because your microphone is its own channel. Every couple of seconds it makes a voice fingerprint of the last few seconds of the other side: numbers that describe how the voice sounds, not a recording. It uses the same speaker model as Voices . Fingerprints that sound alike belong to one speaker. A new speaker appears only after two fingerprints agree that someone new is talking, so one cough or a laugh does not make a Speaker 5 . About once a minute it checks whether two speakers are really one person and joins them; their lines are relabeled in the window. A line shows up a few seconds after the speech, with its speaker. A line is given to the speaker who talked for most of it. When the recording stops, A9 Voice reads the whole meeting again with what it learned, and that final pass gives the note its speakers. The live labels are a draft; the note has the more careful answer. Names you gave during the call are carried into the note.

Turn it on It is Automatic to begin with: Live transcript on this PC: speakers are told apart on this PC. Live transcript from Deepgram or AssemblyAI: their own speaker labels are used, as before. To choose, open Settings › Notes › Live window and use Speakers during the call : Automatic: this PC when the live transcript is written on this PC, otherwise the service's labels. On this PC (free): this PC for any live transcript, including one from a service that has no speaker labels. The live service's labels: only what the live service labels. Nothing is done on this PC. It works while Identify speakers is on, and it needs the speaker model (80.3 MB, the same one Voices uses). If it is not downloaded yet, the Live window says so under its header with a Download button. The live lines show the speakers the transcript has until the model is there, and speakers on this PC start with the next meeting.

Names Naming works as it always has: click a speaker's chip, or type a name in Who's talking? , and the name goes to that speaker everywhere, now and in the note. With Recognize people by voice on, A9 Voice also names people it knows. It does so only when one saved voice is a clear match and well ahead of the next closest one. If two people sound alike, the speaker stays Speaker 3 rather than getting the wrong name. A name you type always wins over a guess. If you click the name box a moment after someone stopped, the name goes to the person who had the floor in the last few seconds.

What stays on your PC The audio, the fingerprints and the speaker labels never leave your PC. Speakers on this PC makes no network request. Each note keeps, in A9 Voice's own data folder, who talked when and one set of numbers per speaker, so that names can be matched again later without the audio. They are not in the note's folder, the exports, the webhooks or the connector. Deleting the note deletes them. The live fingerprints are kept in memory during the recording only. See Privacy and your data .

If something goes wrong Two people show as one speaker, or one person as two. It can happen on a short meeting, or with people who sound alike. Join two speakers or move a line from the speaker's menu, as in the Live window . The final pass in the note is usually better. The Live window says it needs the speaker model. Press Download . The live lines keep the transcript's speakers until it is ready, and speakers on this PC start with the next meeting. Everyone is one speaker in the note. Check that Identify speakers is on in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary .
Related Live window Voices Speech models

Where a finished recording lives. Read the summary, fix a wrong speaker name or a misheard word, leave out something that was never part of the meeting, play any line back, and run the transcript or summary again. Every recording becomes a note. You find it in the Notes list, open it, and the note page shows the summary, the transcript, the people, the pictures and the audio in one place. Everything you change here is also written to the note's folder on your PC at once.

The Notes list Click Notes in the sidebar. The Notes list, newest first, with a recording in progress, two notes being processed and one that needs a look. Type in Search titles and #tags to find a note by words in its title. Type #vendor to show only notes with that tag. You can use both: stand-up #release . Use the chips under the title: All , Auto-recorded , Manual , then your five most used tags. All tags ▾ appears when you have more than five and lists every tag with its count. Click a chip again to turn it off. Press Record to start a recording. While one is running the button says Stop recording . Notes are always newest first, grouped by day (see Days, weeks and jumping to a date ). Each row shows the time, the title, a line saying where it came from (for example "Teams · auto-recorded · Sam, Priya & 2 more" or "Mic only · manual"), the number of images, up to two tags and the length. The word at the right of a row tells you where a note is: Recording (red): still being recorded. Waiting… : queued behind another note. Transcribing… : turning the audio into text. With a model on this PC it also shows a percentage. Summarizing… : writing the summary. Needs a look : something failed. Open the note; see If something goes wrong . Notes you made from another app's folder say Editable copy ; see Notes from an added folder . Filtered by #stand-up, with the row's ⋯ menu: Rename, Show in folder, Delete… Click a row, or select it with ↑ and ↓ and press Enter , to open it. The ⋯ button on a row has Rename (also F2 ), Show in folder and Delete… . The line under the list reminds you how long audio is kept; see Deleting a note and how long audio is kept . The search box at the very top of the page ("Search notes, transcripts and dictations") is a different search that looks inside what was said. See Search and ask .

h: Days, weeks and jumping to a date
t: Days, weeks and jumping to a date The list reads the same however many notes you have. Headers you can read. Each day or week has a header that stays at the top of the list while its notes scroll under it, with how many notes it holds and how long they run: TUESDAY, OCT 13 · 7 notes · 2 h 03 m . A year is added to a date that is not in the current year. This week by day, older weeks folded. TODAY , YESTERDAY and the rest of this week are listed day by day and open. Older notes are grouped under one header per week and start folded: LAST WEEK · Oct 5 – 11 · 23 notes · 6 h 10 m , then WEEK OF SEP 28 , and so on. A week starts on the day Windows' region setting says it does. Open a week and its days appear under it. Fold anything. Click a day or week header (or press Enter or Space on it) to fold or open it; the arrow on the left shows which. Fold all and Open all at the top right of the list do every group at once. What you folded and opened is remembered on this PC for the next visit. Jump to a date. The calendar button next to the search box opens a month. Days with notes show a dot and how many; days without are dimmed. Pick a day, or move with the arrow keys and press Enter , and its week opens, its header scrolls to the top and lights up for a moment. Esc closes it, and the arrows at the top (or Page Up and Page Down ) change the month. A search or filter opens everything. While you type in the search box, or have a tag, Auto-recorded or Manual on, every matching group is shown open, because the results are short. Clear it and the list goes back to how you had it. Older weeks fold. The calendar button jumps to a date.

Open a note Click a note. The page has three parts. The note page: title and chips, the tabs, Export, and the right-hand column. The title and the chips under it. Click the title to rename it. The tabs: Summary , Transcript and Ask AI . Export and the ⋯ menu at the top. The right-hand column: speakers, Regenerate transcript , Regenerate summary and more. It stays in view while the text scrolls. Click ← Notes to go back to the list.

The title A new recording is called Recording , or for a call that A9 Voice started, the app's name plus "call" (for example "Teams call"). It then gets a real name: If Name notes after the meeting is On ( Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary ), A9 Voice reads the meeting's own name from the Teams, Zoho Cliq or browser meeting window during the first 90 seconds of the call and uses it. Otherwise, or if no usable name is found, the AI names the note when it writes the summary, in at most eight words. A title you type always wins, and A9 Voice never replaces it. When the title came from the meeting window or from you, the AI's own title is shown in grey under it, so you keep both. To rename a note, click the title, type, and press Enter . Esc cancels.

The chips under the title The date, time and length. Copied from and the app's name, on an editable copy. The people who spoke ("Sam, Priya & 2 more"). Hover to see everyone. The template used, for example Meeting Notes template . Your tags, each with an × to remove it.

Tags Click + add tag , type a name and press Enter . As you type, the tags you already use are offered; click one to add it. Esc closes the box. Typing a tag shows your existing tags. With AI auto-tag on ( Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary ), the AI tags each note after its summary. It adds up to three tags: the ones you already use that clearly fit, and one new tag when none does, so a new install gets tags to filter by without clicking anything. A new tag looks like any other, with an × to remove it; removing it does not bring it back for that note. Older notes that were waiting on a suggestion got their tag when 1.0.7 first started. A template can also add its own tags to every note that uses it; see Templates and export . To rename, merge or delete a tag everywhere, use Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Tags .

Everything a speaker said A named speaker's ⋯ menu has Everything Priya said . It opens the Ask page on every line Priya said across all your meetings, with no AI involved; see Everything someone said . It is also how you find the meetings where a speaker is not named yet: the view lists them, so you can come here, name the speaker, and have their lines join.

The summary The Summary tab is written from the template. The sections follow the template's order. One section is always first: Your action items , with the tasks that belong to you ("None." when there are none). The section called Action items lists everyone's tasks as check-box lines: task, owner, due date. Where the summary points at a moment in the recording, it shows a small blue time chip, such as 00:22 Priya . Click the chip to play from there. A chip that ends in snip opens the picture taken at that moment. If you rename a speaker, the new name replaces the old one in the summary too. To change how summaries are written, edit the template. See Templates and export .

h: When the summary is out of date
t: When the summary is out of date If you fix a line in the transcript, a bar appears: "Transcript edited · the summary was written from the earlier text." Click Re-summarize to write it again from the corrected text. You can also leave it as it is.

Ask AI The Ask AI tab and the bar at the bottom answer questions about this one note, such as "What did I promise?". Type a question, choose a language model next to the arrow, and press Enter . Answers cite the moment; click the citation to play it. The bar's small tags tell you what the AI is given: the summary (with its word count), the transcript (number of turns) and the images. When the meeting is longer than the model takes in one request, the model is given the summary and the parts of the transcript that match your question, as many as fit, and the answer's footer says so: answered from the summary + 14 relevant passages . To ask across all your notes, use the Ask page: see Asking your notes .

The transcript Click the Transcript tab. Each line has a time, the speaker's name in their own color and what was said. The Transcript tab. The picture card and the dashed box are things added during the recording. Click any line to hear it. This works while the audio is still kept. The hint above the transcript reminds you: Click any line to hear it · Space play/pause · ←/→ 5 s . Pictures taken during the recording appear in place as cards with the time, where they came from ( clipboard , paste or drop ) and the caption. Notes you typed during the recording appear in dashed boxes: your note , or Action , Decision or Callout when you marked the moment from the Live window. See The Live window . On an editable copy of a note that had no times, a ~ before a time means it is an estimate.

Fix a misheard word Double-click the text of a line, or click the pencil ( ✎ ) at the end of the line. Type the correction. Enter saves; Shift + Enter starts a new line in the box; Esc cancels. Editing a line in place. A message appears at the bottom, "Line edited", with Undo . The line gets a small edited label and a Revert button; hover the label to see the original words. A9 Voice keeps the transcript as it was first written in a hidden .original folder inside the note's folder, so a correction never loses the original. If you changed exactly one word, A9 Voice offers to fix it everywhere: After changing rooting to routing, A9 Voice offers to replace the other one. Replace all N in this note changes every other time that word appears in the transcript. and in the summary appears when the summary has the word too. Add to Dictionary also teaches the Dictionary to write it your way next time. See Dictionary . Click Apply to do what is ticked, or No thanks .

h: Fix the speaker of one line
t: Fix the speaker of one line Sometimes one line is under the wrong person. Click the speaker's name at the start of the line. The name picker opens under it, the same one the Live window uses. Type a name, pick a person from the list, or pick one of the Speakers chips to move the line to that speaker. A name that is not on the list shows last, as + Add "name" to this meeting , with a line under it that says what it does: Names this line only · no voiceprint for one line, or Names Speaker 4 · saves a new voice for a whole speaker ( in this meeting when Voices is off). A name another speaker here already has says whose it is, for example Speaker 3 . The speaker's own name is listed too, marked current . Under Apply to , choose Just this line , This and the lines after it, until the speaker changes , or Everything from that speaker. A speaker with no name yet starts on Everything from ; a named speaker starts on Just this line . Press Enter or Name . Not sure and Esc close the picker and change nothing. Click a line's speaker to name it: this line, the lines after it, or everything from that speaker. The Speakers chips are numbered 1 to 9 . With the name field empty, pressing a number moves the line to that speaker, the same as clicking the chip. A message says "Line moved to another speaker" and offers Undo . Naming one line never teaches a voice. Choosing Everything from and a name another speaker already has asks Same person? first. The same box has Not part of the meeting , for a line that was never said in the meeting. It uses the same Apply to choice. See Leave something out of the note .

h: More lines that sound like the same person
t: More lines that sound like the same person When the call's speech was split wrongly, one speaker can hold two people. You fix a few lines by hand, and the rest are still under the wrong name. With Voices on, A9 Voice then checks, once the note is ready, whether more of the lines still on that speaker sound like the person you moved lines to. If it finds some, a bar appears above the note: 12 more lines from Ana Example sound like Ben Sample with Review . Press Review . Each line is listed with its time and text. Press the play button on a line to hear it. Press ✓ to move that line to the person, or ✗ to leave it where it is. ✓ Move all moves every line in the list; None of these leaves them all. Nothing moves until you press a ✓ . A message offers Undo for the lines you moved. How it works: A9 Voice compares each remaining line's voice with the lines you moved and with the rest of the speaker's voice, and offers a line only when it is clearly the moved person's. It needs about four seconds of speech in the lines you moved, and it does not look at lines shorter than about a second. Your own side is never part of this. It reads the recording on your PC while the note is open and keeps nothing: no voiceprint is saved or learned from it. A line you press ✗ on is not offered again until A9 Voice restarts. It only knows about lines you moved by hand on this page; running Regenerate transcript forgets them.

Name the speakers The column on the right lists everyone who spoke, under SPEAKERS . Your own side is marked Speaker 1 · mic . Each person shows their total talk time. To see a speaker named here, after the call: The Speakers list: type a name in the box (1). A suggestion appears under the name (2). Click the name under a speaker. The name picker opens under it: type to narrow the list by first or last name, then click a person or press ↓ and Enter . People you named lately are first. To use a new name, type it and press Enter , or click + Add "name" to this meeting (it comes after the people who match what you typed). Tab goes to Name , Esc or Not sure closes the picker with nothing changed, and Clear name takes a name off. Type to narrow the list. A name another speaker already has shows whose it is. If the box has a suggestion under it, "Sounds like Dana ?", click Yes to accept it or No to dismiss it. A name shown with "Recognized by voice" was matched from a voiceprint. See Voices . A message at the bottom says "Renamed to Dana" and offers Undo . Every rename rewrites the summary and transcript.md in the note's folder straight away, and a rename of a whole speaker can also teach A9 Voice that voice if you have turned Voices on. If you pick a name that another speaker in this note already has, A9 Voice asks Same person? . Merge moves all the lines to one person; No, different person keeps both speakers with that name.

The speaker menu The ⋯ next to a speaker's name opens: This is me : gives that speaker the name from your Account. Merge into and each other speaker's name: moves all of this speaker's lines to that person, and removes this speaker. Not part of the meeting : leaves this speaker out of the note, for a voice that was never in the meeting. Your own side doesn't have it. See Leave something out of the note . The ⋯ menu of a speaker.

Hear who someone is If you are not sure who "Speaker 4" is, click the small ▶ at the right of their name. It plays one of their lines. Each click plays their next line, and wraps to the first after the last. A small label such as Line 1 of 3 tells you where you are. Click the button again, now showing ❚❚ , to pause. Step through one person's lines with their play button.

h: Leave something out of the note
t: Leave something out of the note A9 Voice records everything your PC plays, not only the meeting. If a video, a song or a notification read aloud played during the call, it can show up as its own speaker, and its words end up in the transcript, the summary and your searches. Not part of the meeting takes them out again. Open the ⋯ next to that speaker and choose Not part of the meeting . To leave out only some lines, click the speaker's name at the start of a line, pick Just this line or This and the lines after it, until the speaker changes under Apply to , then click Not part of the meeting . A message says "Speaker 5 left out of this note" and offers Undo for 10 seconds. There is no question first. What changes: The transcript. Their lines are removed from transcript.md . Each stretch is replaced by one line such as *[Not part of the meeting · 06:30–06:32]* . In the app the lines are greyed and collapsed under Show 3 excluded lines ; they stay playable, so you can check what was left out. The summary. It is written again from the rest of the meeting with the note's template and model: the card says "Re-summarizing without Speaker 5…". The title and the action items come from that same pass. If you changed the summary yourself (for example with Replace all … and in the summary ), A9 Voice does not overwrite it: a bar says Speaker excluded · Re-summarize? (replaces your edits) , with Re-summarize and Keep my summary . Until you choose, that summary isn't sent, indexed or shown to a model. Everything else. Their words are not in search or Ask, the people list, talk time, exports, what a webhook sends, or what a connected app can read. A speaker who is left out is never used to learn a voice. The recording is never changed. Speakers who are left out move to Excluded at the bottom of the Speakers list, with their talk time, a ▶ to hear them and Include again . In the transcript, Show 3 excluded lines opens a stretch, and each line has its own Include again . It works any time, not only for 10 seconds: the lines come back, transcript.md is written again, and the summary is redone under the same rule. Undo puts the transcript, the search index and the earlier summary back exactly as they were, and does not ask the language model for anything. If you run Regenerate transcript , the speakers are numbered afresh, so A9 Voice puts what you left out back by time: a new line is left out when at least half of it falls inside a stretch you left out. If a speaker got another number, or only part of it matched, a note says so, for example "Kept 1 exclusion (Speaker 5 is now Speaker 4). Check it." Click OK when you have looked. Your own side, Speaker 1 · mic , can't be left out as a whole, but any single line of it can.

Play the recording When the audio is still kept, a player sits at the top of the note. The player. The Others, Everyone and Me switch (1) appears for recordings of two sides. 10 buttons jump back or forward 10 seconds. Click the wave to jump to a place in the recording. The speed button cycles 1× , 1.25× , 1.5× and 2× . Keys, when you are not typing in a box: Key What it does Space Play or pause ← Back 5 seconds → Forward 5 seconds

h: Who you hear: Others, Everyone, Me
t: Who you hear: Others, Everyone, Me A meeting is recorded on two sides: your microphone, and the computer audio (the other people). Played as they are, they would come out of different ears. So A9 Voice plays both in both ears, and the switch at the right of the player chooses what you hear: Others (the default): the computer audio only, the other people. Everyone : both sides, with your microphone a little lower so your own voice and room noise do not cover the others. Me : your microphone only. Your choice is remembered. When you click a line, or play a person with their ▶ , you hear that person's own side whatever the switch says. The switch only changes how the note plays ; the file on disk keeps both channels. A recording of only one side has no switch. If the audio is gone you see "Audio removed after 30 days. The summary, transcript and images stay." instead of the player (the number is your Keep notes audio setting).

Pictures Pictures captured during a call (a snip, or any image you copy) are saved into the note. You can also add them later. The strip of pictures (1) and the Drop or paste box (2). Drag an image from a folder onto the note page, or copy an image and press Ctrl + V on it. A9 Voice saves it as a PNG in the note's images folder and says "Image added at 00:34". The time is where the player is, or the recording's timer if you are recording now. Click a picture in the strip, or a picture card in the transcript, to open it larger. The player jumps to its moment. Type a Caption (goes into the summary) . The AI reads captions the next time it writes the summary. The picture viewer. The caption is saved when you click out of the box. In the viewer, Show in folder opens the picture's place on disk, Delete removes it from the note, and Close (or Esc ) goes back.

The right-hand column Below the speakers: Run the transcript or the summary again, with a different model or template. Regenerate transcript : see below. Regenerate summary : see below. A small grey line with the speech model and the language model that made this note, for example "Deepgram · nova-3 · OpenRouter · …". One block per webhook you set up, with Send to and its name, and a line such as "Sent automatically at 3:09 AM · delivered". See Webhooks . Other notes from this meeting : see Other notes from the same meeting .

Run the transcript again Use this when the speakers were mixed up, or you want to try another speech model. Under Regenerate transcript , pick a speech model. Models that are not set up yet are greyed out "(set up first)". Models on this PC appear as "(on this PC)". Leave Identify speakers ticked to separate the people. It is greyed out for a model that cannot do it. Click Regenerate transcript . The audio is transcribed again and the note shows "Transcribing…" until it is done. What this does: It replaces every line. Corrections you made to lines are not kept. It keeps the names you gave speakers, matching them by who spoke when. It does not write the summary again. Click Regenerate summary afterwards if you want a new one. A cloud speech model uses your own key with that provider, and is billed by them to you. A model on this PC works without the internet. It needs the audio. If the audio has been removed, the button is greyed out.

Run the summary again Use this after you fixed the transcript or the speakers, or to try another template or language model. Under Regenerate summary , choose a Template and a Language model . Click Regenerate summary . The note shows "Writing the summary…". What this does: It writes the summary, action items and the tags from the template again, using the current transcript, speaker names, captions and typed notes. The template you chose becomes the note's template. It gives the note a new AI title only if the title was not typed by you and not taken from the meeting window. It does not touch the transcript. It uses your own language-model key. See Language models . The button is greyed out when there is no transcript or no language model set up.

h: Other notes from the same meeting
t: Other notes from the same meeting When you have recorded the same meeting more than once, Other notes from this meeting lists up to five of the others, newest first, each with its date. Click one to open it. Two notes belong together when their titles match once dates and numbers are ignored: "Sprint Standup #12" and "Sprint standup Oct 6" are the same meeting. Placeholder titles such as "Recording" or "Teams call" never match. The list of earlier notes of the same meeting.

The menu at the top The ⋯ at the top of the note has: The ⋯ menu at the top of the note. Open recording : plays the audio file in your default player. Greyed out if there is no audio. Show in folder : opens the note's folder in File Explorer. Export… : the same as the Export button. See Templates and export . Copy summary as markdown : copies the summary text to the clipboard. Copy for email : copies the summary as a formatted message, with the template's logo and colors, ready to paste into a new email. Send to and the name of each webhook you set up. Delete… : see Deleting a note and how long audio is kept .

h: A tip after a meeting transcribed on this PC
t: A tip after a meeting transcribed on this PC The first time you open a note that was transcribed by a model on this PC, a card says Running on this PC: free, but slower and less accurate at telling callers apart. Deepgram or ElevenLabs are faster. Upgrade opens Settings › Models with the list of faster engines; Dismiss removes it. It does not come back, and it never shows once you have used Deepgram or ElevenLabs for Meeting notes.

h: Notes still being made, and notes that failed
t: Notes still being made, and notes that failed A note recorded with no language model set up keeps its transcript and says Add a free Groq key to get a summary , with Set up summaries , which opens Settings › Models. The summary is written by itself as soon as you save a key, oldest note first, one at a time. When a model's allowance for the day is used up, the note says so with when it comes back, for example resets in 3 h (around 6:40 PM) , and offers Use another model and Try again .

Recording right now While a note is still recording, the note page shows a red box with the timer and Live window , Snip , Pause (then Resume ), Stop & discard and Stop (the recording bar asks Stop recording? first). Type in the box and press Enter to add a typed note at this moment. The transcript and summary appear when you stop. See Recording a meeting . A note that is recording now. Type a note and press Enter to place it at this moment.

Processing A box with a spinner says what is happening: Transcribing… (with a percentage on this PC), Writing the summary… , or Waiting for the note before it… . A long meeting on a model with a small limit is written in parts and says Writing summary… part 2 of 4 , with waiting for Groq's per-minute limit when it has to wait (see Long meetings ). You can close the note and come back; it finishes on its own. Regenerate waits until it is done.

If something goes wrong A failed note names the reason. Try again runs the transcript again. A note says "Needs a look" and shows a reason. Read the reason, for example that the speech provider could not be reached. Fix that (see Speech models ), then click Try again . Try again needs the audio; if the audio was removed it is greyed out. The audio of a failed or unfinished note is never removed by the retention rule, so you can try again. A note says "Your network is blocking Deepgram (api.deepgram.com). The recording is saved." Your network blocks the speech service. With a model on this PC the note is transcribed there and marked Transcribed on this PC because your network blocks Deepgram. , with Transcribe with Deepgram for later. Without one, the note shows Download the on-PC model and tries again by itself when your network changes and every 15 minutes for 24 hours. See Work networks . The summary is missing and a grey bar shows a message. Often no language model is set up. The transcript is still a good note. Add a key in Settings › Models (see Language models ), then click Regenerate summary . The summary is old after you edited the transcript. Click Re-summarize in the bar. A speaker is wrong everywhere. Rename or merge the speaker in the right-hand column, or run the transcript again with Identify speakers ticked. For anything else, see Troubleshooting .

The note's folder on disk To see the folder, the Export window and a template from the library: Every note is also a plain folder you can open, copy and give to other tools. By default it lives in Documents\A9 Voice\Notes and is named by day and meeting, for example 2026-10-05 Platform stand-up . Change where notes go in Settings › Notes › Storage . The folder holds: summary.md : the summary. transcript.md : every line as [mm:ss] Name: text . notes.md : only if you typed notes during the recording. images : the pictures. The files are always current. A rename, a corrected line, a new tag or a regenerate rewrites them and renames the folder straight away. Branding from a template never goes into these files; it is only added when you export. A9 Voice only changes, renames or deletes folders that it made itself. Each carries a hidden .a9voice file. A folder without that file is never touched. To open the folder, use Show in folder on the list row or in the ⋯ menu.

h: Deleting a note and how long audio is kept
t: Deleting a note and how long audio is kept

Delete one note Click ⋯ on the note (or on its row in the list) and choose Delete… . The item changes to Delete audio, files and note . Click it to confirm. This removes the note, its audio, and the files A9 Voice put in the note's folder: summary.md , transcript.md , notes.md , the pictures and the hidden files. Anything else you saved in that folder stays. The app has no undo for this.

How long audio is kept Settings › Notes › Storage: where notes are kept, and Keep notes audio. Audio is the largest part of a note. In Settings › Notes › Storage , Keep notes audio deletes only the audio, after 1 day , 7 days , 30 days , 90 days or Forever . The summary, transcript and pictures stay until you delete the note. A9 Voice checks about a minute after it starts, then once a day, and right away when you change the setting. Once the audio is gone you cannot play lines or run the transcript again, but you can still read, edit, export and re-summarize the note.

Notes from an added folder If you added a folder in Settings › Notes › Search , notes that live in it can be found and opened. They are read only: A9 Voice never changes, moves or deletes anything in that folder. See Search and ask for how to add one. A note from an added folder. The badge (1) names where it came from. Make editable copy (2) makes a copy that you can change. The page shows a badge with the app or folder it came from, the date, the people, Read only , and the sentence "This note lives in another app's folder. A9 Voice will make its own copy to edit. The original stays untouched." You can read the summary and transcript, play a line if there is audio, and use Open in folder to see the original files. To change anything, click Make editable copy . A9 Voice copies the note into your own notes, leaves the original as it was, and opens the copy as a normal note. It shows Copied from on its chips and Editable copy in the list. If you click a speaker's name, double-click a line, or click Regenerate summary on a read-only note, A9 Voice asks first: Make editable copy? The original stays untouched. Click Make copy to go ahead, or Cancel . Once a copy exists, the read-only page says "An editable copy exists." with Open it .

Related Templates and export : change how the summary is written, and send it as a PDF, Word file or email. Recording a meeting and The Live window : what happens before the note exists. Voices : let A9 Voice recognize people by voice. Asking your notes : question every note at once. Search and ask : find words in every note. Webhooks : send a summary somewhere when it is ready.

Let A9 Voice put names on the people in your meetings by how they sound. It is off until you turn it on, and the voiceprints stay on your PC. Without this, people on a call show up as Speaker 2 , Speaker 3 and so on, until you name them. With Recognize people by voice on, A9 Voice remembers how each person you have named sounds, and names them for you in later meetings, both on the live transcript and in the finished note. The same speaker model also tells the other people apart during a call, without saving anyone's voice: see Speakers on this PC . Recognizing people by name is the part that is off until you turn it on. It works on the other people on the call. Your own voice is never learned or matched: A9 Voice already knows which speaker is you, because that is your microphone.
