What is stored, and where A voiceprint: a set of numbers that describes how a person sounds. It is not a recording. Where: in a file called voices.db in A9 Voice's own data folder on your PC. Not in your Notes folder. Never anywhere else: voiceprints are never put in a note, a log, a webhook, or any request to a speech or AI service, and they stay on this PC unless you include them in an export you make ( Include learned voices in Settings › Account › Export ; the zip then holds the prints themselves, so keep it private). The connector for AI apps never returns them either. Next to each person: a short history in plain words (when the voice was learned or strengthened, renamed, merged). For everything else A9 Voice keeps, see Privacy and your data .

Turn it on Open Settings › Notes › Voices and switch Recognize people by voice on. Voices is off until you turn it on. A window called Before you turn this on opens. It says what is stored, where, how to delete it, and that you are responsible for consent. Read it, then choose Turn on . Not now leaves the switch off. The consent point reads: "you're responsible for any consent your location requires before you record or recognize people." Rules about recording people, and about recognizing them, differ from place to place. A9 Voice downloads the Speaker model once (80.3 MB). A progress bar shows how far it has got. If the download fails, a message appears and the button reads Try again . When you switch Recognize people by voice off again, the voices you already have stay on your PC until you forget them or delete them (see Manage people ).

h: How A9 Voice learns a voice
t: How A9 Voice learns a voice To see the three steps, from naming a speaker to turning recognition on: A voice is learned only when you tell A9 Voice who someone is, in one of two ways: Naming a whole speaker in the Live window. While you record, type the name into Who's talking? and press Tag , name a speaker from their chip, or press Yes next to a likely match. See The Live window . Naming a whole speaker in a note. In the note's Speakers list, type a name for a speaker (or answer Yes to "Sounds like ...?"). See The note page . A few rules keep wrong names out: Never from a single line. Moving one line to another speaker does not teach anything. Only a name for the whole speaker does. Never your own voice. Your microphone channel, and any speaker you name as yourself, are skipped. Never a speaker you left out. A speaker marked Not part of the meeting in a note is never learned from, and leaving one out never changes a stored voice. If that speaker had been named from a voice, the person's history says "Excluded from a note", so a wrong match shows. Never from an editable copy of a note that came from an added folder. See Search and Ask . After the call. Tags taught during a call are learned when the note is processed afterwards, not during the call. That is also why Undo in the Live window leaves no trace. It needs the audio. A voice is learned from the note's recording, so nothing is learned from a note whose audio has been removed (see Keep notes audio in The note page ). Enough speech. A voice is learned only from at least 12 seconds of that person's clear speech. With less, the history says "not enough clear speech". Too different. If the new sample sounds too unlike the voice already stored under that name, it is not added. The history says "voice too different", and it is probably the wrong person. A tag on the wrong person. If you Tag a name that already has a voice stored, but the speaker clearly sounds like a different person you taught, A9 Voice names the speaker with that other person and learns nothing from the tag. The Samples column on the Voices page counts how many times a voice has been learned or strengthened.
How names show up

During a call A9 Voice starts to compare a speaker with the voices you taught it after about 8 seconds of that speaker's talking, and tries again as more speech comes in. A name is shown only once two tries in a row agree on it, and it does not change after that. A sure match (the voice is alike enough, and clearly closer to this person than to anyone else you taught) names the speaker on every line, past and future. A likely match (alike, but not sure enough) shows the name with a question mark, such as Priya? , and a Yes button. One click confirms it and counts as a Tag. A likely match: Priya? with Yes.

In the finished note When the note is ready, speakers nobody named yet are checked against your voices again, using everything that person said. In the note's Speakers list you will see one of three things: Recognized by voice under a name A9 Voice was sure about. Sounds like Dana? with Yes and No . Yes names the speaker, which also teaches the voice. No dismisses the guess. Nothing, and the speaker stays Speaker N . A speaker with very little speech is not judged at all. Two rules apply in every meeting. A speaker gets at most one name, and a person is matched to at most one speaker, so two speakers never both become Priya. A name you have already given in this meeting is never offered again to another speaker. Naming a speaker yourself always wins over a guess.

The Voices page Open Settings › Notes › Voices to see everyone A9 Voice has learned. Each row shows the person's Name , Samples , Last recognized (the date, or Never ) and Meetings (how many meetings they were recognized in). Last recognized and Meetings move when A9 Voice names someone with a sure match in a finished note.

Manage people Each row ends with three links. Rename opens the name picker with the current name. Type the new name and press Enter . If that name already belongs to another saved voice, A9 Voice asks Same person? : Merge joins the two, No, different person keeps both. Merge folds this voice into another one, for when the same person was taught under two names. Pick the other person in the name picker, which lists only people that are already saved. The two voices become one, weighted by how many samples each had. Forget removes the person and their history now. A line opens under the row asking you to confirm with Forget . The space the voiceprint used is overwritten, so nothing about that voice is left on your PC. Click a person's name to open their history, one short line per event. A person's history.

h: Clear out voices you no longer need
t: Clear out voices you no longer need When someone has not been heard for 60 days or more (or was added that long ago and never heard), a box labeled Not heard in 60+ days appears, with the count. Tick it to show only those people. Forget all N shown then asks once more ("This can't be undone") and removes them together.

Check voiceprints Check voiceprints looks for two people whose voices sound too alike. That usually means one of them picked up some of the other person's voice, from a stretch where both talked. It only reports: it changes nothing. Listen in a recent note, then rename or forget the wrong one yourself.

Import voices from a file Import voices from a file... reads a voiceprints file you already have and lets you pick who to add. People who are already here are shown as already here and left as they are, and nothing is replaced. Choose who to add and press Import with the number of people. To move your saved voices to another PC, tick Include learned voices when you export your setup; importing that zip adds them (people already there are skipped, and voice recognition stays as that PC has it). This box is for a voiceprints file that came from somewhere else. A file it cannot use gives an error such as "Not a voiceprints file".

Delete all voices At the bottom of the page, Delete all voices removes every voice from your PC at once. Type DELETE in the box and press Delete all voices . This removes the whole voices.db file. Notes keep the names they already show: only the voiceprints go.

If something goes wrong Nobody is named. Check that the switch is On and the Speaker model has finished downloading. A9 Voice also needs at least one person in the list, so name someone first. Matching needs a few seconds of clear speech from each speaker. The wrong name appears. Rename the speaker in the note. If the same mistake keeps coming, run Check voiceprints , then Forget the voice that is wrong and teach it again. Two people keep getting each other's names. The two voices probably mixed during a call where both talked. Use Check voiceprints , then forget or rename the wrong one. More in Troubleshooting .
Related The Live window : Tag people while you record. The note page : name speakers in a finished note. Privacy and your data : what stays on your PC.

Choose how each summary is written, put your own logo on it, and save or send a note as Markdown, a PDF, a Word file, an email or captions, and move your notes to a new PC. A template decides what a summary contains: which sections, in what order, with what rules. It can also carry your logo and colors. When you export a note, you pick what to save (the summary, the transcript or the audio) and in which file type. Templates live in Settings › Notes › Templates . Export is the Export button on every note page . To see a note's files, the Export window and a template added from the library:
Templates This page covers summary templates. Settings › Templates also has Ask templates , which decide how Ask your notes answers; see Edit the templates .

Open the templates Click Settings in the sidebar. Under the Notes heading, click Templates . The template list. The note's template is selected (1), the star marks the default (2), and Create template (3) adds one. The page is called Summary templates . On the left is your list. The one with the amber star is the default : new recordings use it. It is the same choice as Summary template in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary . You can pick another template for one note on its note page, under Regenerate summary . A9 Voice comes with one template, Meeting Notes . It writes five sections: Overview , Key discussion points , Decisions , Action items and Open questions . You can edit it like any other template; it shows a Built-in label. Click a template to open it on the right. To make it the default, click its star (the tooltip says "Make default"). If you have unsaved changes and click another template, A9 Voice asks "Discard your changes?".

h: Add a template from the library
t: Add a template from the library Click Add from library . Choose one of the four: Template What it writes Meeting Recap A short recap to share: summary, decisions, next steps. Stand-up Yesterday, today and blockers for each person, then action items. It adds the tag #stand-up . 1:1 Updates, feedback and follow-ups. It adds the tag #1:1 . Decision log Only the decisions: what, why, who decided, then alternatives considered and follow-ups. It adds the tag #decision . The Add from library menu. The template is copied into your list at once and opened, so you can change it. The library has no logo; branding is set per template.

Create your own Click + Create template . A new template named New template appears in the list, with two sections ( Summary and Action items ) and the same rules as Meeting Notes. It is saved straight away; change what you like and click Save .

h: Change the name, the sections and the rules
t: Change the name, the sections and the rules Everything below is on the right of the list. Name (1), a section (2) and + Add section (3). Type a name and a one-line description . Click Save when you are done. ( Save and Cancel stay grey until you change something.) Under SECTIONS , each row has a heading and an instruction that tells the AI what to write there: for example heading Decisions , instruction "Each decision made, one bullet each." Drag a row by its grip ( ⋮⋮ ), or use ↑ and ↓ , to change the order. Click × to remove a section. Click + Add section for a new one. A section with an empty heading is dropped when you save. The summary always starts with Your action items , taken from the action items the AI finds, whatever sections you have. Under RULES you can change the rules the AI follows, one per line. Meeting Notes starts with these four: write "Not discussed" when a section has nothing in the transcript and never invent anything; attribute statements to speakers only when the transcript labels them; use the Dictionary spellings; and stay professional about people. A9 Voice adds the last rule to every prompt even if you delete it. The rules box (1) and the options (2). Then four options: Capture system audio : "Record the other people, not just your mic." Turn it off and a recording that starts with this template as the default records only your microphone. It only matters if Computer audio (Them) is on in Settings › Notes › Recording . Generate AI summary : "Off = transcript, title and tags only." With it off, no summary is written; you still get the transcript, a title and tags. Summary language : Same as the meeting (the default), or any language in the list, shown with its own name, for example German (Deutsch). Same as the meeting now follows the meeting: the title, every section heading, the summary, the action items and the tags are written in the main language of the transcript, even though the built-in section headings are in English. A language you set writes all of those in it. The Ask answers follow the language of your question. Tags : tags that are added to every note that uses this template. Type a tag and press Enter ; click its × to remove it.

h: Custom instructions and the full prompt
t: Custom instructions and the full prompt CUSTOM INSTRUCTIONS is free text added to the end, for example "Keep it under 200 words. Write in a neutral tone." Click View full prompt to see exactly what is sent to your language model: the instructions, your sections, your rules, and a place-holder where the transcript goes. Click it again to hide it. It shows the text that the AI receives, so you can check how your changes read. View full prompt shows the whole text sent to the language model.

Save, cancel, delete Save keeps your changes. Cancel goes back to what was saved. Save keeps your changes; "Saved" appears for a moment. Cancel goes back to what you last saved. Delete… removes a template; click Delete template to confirm. You cannot delete the default one: make another template the default first. Notes you already made keep their summaries. Changes to a template do not change summaries that already exist. To use a new version on an old note, open it and click Regenerate summary ; see The note page .

Branding Branding puts your logo, a header and your colors on what you share. Each template has its own, so you can use one look for client notes and another for internal ones. Branding appears on PDF , Word and HTML email exports and on Copy for email . It does not go into Markdown , Plain text , captions or the note's own summary.md , which stay plain. Which branding a note uses depends on its template: the one it was made with, or the one you chose on the last Regenerate summary . If that template was deleted, the default template's branding is used. Scroll to BRANDING in the template.

Add a logo No logo yet. Upload logo… (1) opens the file chooser. Click Upload logo… . In the Windows window that opens ("Choose a logo"), pick a PNG, SVG or JPG file. It can be up to 2 MB. The logo appears at once in the two preview boxes, on a light and on a dark background. It is saved right away, even if you cancel your other changes. If the file is the wrong type or too big, a message says so: "Use a PNG, SVG or JPG file." or "That file is over 2 MB. Use a smaller logo." A9 Voice makes a PNG copy of an SVG logo, because Word and mail apps cannot show SVG. Click Replace logo… to pick another file, or Remove to take it away.

h: Add a version for dark backgrounds (optional)
t: Add a version for dark backgrounds (optional) If your logo is dark and disappears on a dark background, click Add a version for dark backgrounds and pick a second file. It is used in the HTML email file, when the person who opens it has dark mode. Everything else uses the main logo. Replace a version for dark backgrounds and Remove dark version change or remove it.

h: Place and size it, add a header and a footer
t: Place and size it, add a header and a footer The logos (1), placement (2), header text (3) and footer (4), with a preview of the top of a page. Placement : Left , Center or Right . Logo height : 32 px max , 48 px max or 64 px max . Header text : your company or team name, shown under the logo. Second line : for example "Confidential: internal". Accent color : pick a color for headings and the dividing line. Neutral means no color; click Use neutral to go back to it. Footer : tick it and write the text. The text starts as "Notes prepared with A9 Voice"; change it to anything you like. In a PDF it is at the bottom of each page; in an email file it is the last line. The box at the bottom shows how the top of a page will look, with an example title and a Decisions heading. Click Save . A word on Word: in a Word file, the logo, header text and divider are in the page header on every page, headings use your accent color, and the footer is a line at the bottom if you turned it on.

Export a note Open a note and click Export , or choose ⋯ › Export… . Export is greyed out while the note is still recording. Export. What to export (1) and Format (2) are on the left; the preview is on the right. Under What to export , choose one: Summary : "AI summary from the template". Transcript : "Speaker-by-speaker, timestamped". Audio recording : "MP3, M4A or original". A choice is greyed out when there is nothing to export: "Not available yet" if the note has no summary or transcript, and "Audio removed" if the audio has been deleted. Under Format , choose the file type (the list changes with step 1; see the table below). Set the switches under the format list (below). Look at the preview. It shows what will be written. Click Export with the format's name, for example Export Markdown or Export PDF . Windows asks where to save the file. It starts in your Downloads folder with a name such as "Platform stand-up summary.md". Choose a place and click Save. When it is done the window says Saved. and shows Show in folder , which opens the file's place in File Explorer. Then click Close . Cancel closes the window without saving.

h: What each file type is for
t: What each file type is for You export Format What you get Summary Markdown (.md) (best for AI chats) Plain text with headings and - [ ] check boxes. Pictures are links to the files in the note's folder. Summary Plain text (.txt) The same without the Markdown marks. Summary PDF document (with your branding) A printed page with your logo, header, accent and footer. Summary Word (.docx) (edit before sending) The same as a Word file you can change. Summary HTML email (.html) (one file, logo inside) One file that holds the whole message, logo included. Open it in a browser, or send it. Transcript Markdown (.md) Every line as [mm:ss] Name: text . Good to paste into an AI chat. Transcript Plain text (.txt) The same lines without the Markdown. Transcript WebVTT (.vtt) (captions) A captions file for video players: one cue per turn, with the speaker's name. Transcript SubRip (.srt) (captions) The same captions in the other common captions format. Transcript PDF document and Word (.docx) The transcript on a page with your header. Audio MP3 (.mp3) (plays anywhere) The whole recording, both sides, encoded by Windows at 128 kbit/s, 48 kHz. Audio M4A (.m4a) (AAC) The same, as an M4A file. Audio Original (.ogg Opus) (smallest) The file A9 Voice saved: two channels (you on the left, the others on the right). Only the PDF , Word and HTML email files carry your branding. The others stay plain.

The switches Include title & date : starts the file with the note's title, then a line with the date, length and people. Available for every text, PDF, Word and email file; captions do not use it. Include images : adds the pictures of the note (Markdown, PDF and Word; in a text transcript a line such as "(image: Approval routing diagram)"). For a Summary as PDF , Word or HTML email , an Include group lets you cut parts: Choose which parts of the summary go in. Summary : the sections that are not action items or decisions. Action items : sections whose heading contains "action", "to-do", "todo", "follow-up" or "next step". Decisions : sections whose heading contains "decision". Notes : the notes you typed during the recording. Greyed out if you typed none. Images : the note's pictures. Greyed out if it has none. Transcript : adds the full transcript after the summary. Off by default. Under it, a reminder: "Logo, colors and footer come from the note's template (Settings › Templates)."

Summary as a PDF The preview of a branded PDF. Choose Summary and PDF document . The preview shows the branded page. Export PDF prints that page to a file, so any language works, and pictures are included when Images is ticked.

Captions Transcript as WebVTT, previewed as text. Choose Transcript , then WebVTT (.vtt) or SubRip (.srt) . Use the file with a video of the same meeting so that each line appears on screen when it is said.

Audio Audio recording as MP3. Choose Audio recording and one of the three types. There is no text preview, only a note of what you will get. The MP3 and M4A are made by the encoders built into Windows, so nothing extra is installed. Audio is only here while it is kept; see The note page .

Send a summary by email You can send a summary three ways. With HTML email chosen: Copy for email and Open in mail app. Copy for email (a button at the bottom whenever Summary is chosen, also in the note's ⋯ menu): copies the summary as a formatted message with your logo and colors. A line says "Copied. Paste it into a new email." Open a new message in your mail app and paste. The logo is drawn on white so it stays readable if the mail app uses dark mode. The plain-text version is copied too, for apps that cannot show formatting. Open in mail app (when HTML email (.html) is chosen): opens the summary as a new, unsent message in your default mail app, if that app supports it. You add the address and send it. If no mail app can open it, A9 Voice says "No mail app is set up to open emails on this PC. Save the HTML file instead." Export HTML email : saves one .html file that you can attach. After Copy for email. The email versions use the Include switches you set in the window. Copy for email from the note's ⋯ menu uses the title and the usual parts, without pictures. After Export: Saved, with Show in folder.

If something goes wrong Export says "Couldn't write the file". Choose another folder, and make sure a file with that name is not open in another program. The logo does not show. Check that the template you are using (the note's template, or the default) has the logo, and that the file is a PNG, SVG or JPG under 2 MB. Audio is greyed out. The audio was removed after the number of days in Settings › Notes › Storage › Keep notes audio . Open in mail app says "No mail app is set up to open emails on this PC." Use Copy for email and paste, or save the HTML file. For anything else, see Troubleshooting .

h: Moving your notes to a new PC
t: Moving your notes to a new PC Your list of notes lives on each PC (in A9 Voice's data folder); the Notes folder is where the files go. So a new PC that points at a folder already full of your notes (OneDrive, a copied folder) starts with an empty list. There are two ways to bring the notes in, and they work together.

h: Find the notes that are already in your Notes folder
t: Find the notes that are already in your Notes folder This needs nothing but the folder, so it works when the old PC is gone. In Settings › Notes › Storage , press Change… and pick the folder that holds your notes. If notes are in it, A9 Voice offers them at once. You can also press Find… next to Find notes in this folder at any time, and A9 Voice offers them once at startup when your list is empty. It says Found 312 notes in this folder that aren't in your list. Add them? and, when it applies, how many couldn't be read. Nothing is added until you press Add them . Your list fills as the notes are added. Stop keeps the ones already added, and you can run it again for the rest. Each note comes from its own files: the title, date, length, tags and template from the top of summary.md , the summary, and the lines and speakers from transcript.md . There is no audio, so a note shows that no recording is available. It never changes a file: nothing in the folder is renamed or rewritten, which matters when another PC is syncing the same folder. A9 Voice writes to a note's files only when you edit that note. Running Find… again adds nothing that is already in your list, and picks up notes another PC added since. The names you gave speakers, the people you tagged and the lines you left out are kept in the app, not in the files, so a note found this way has the speaker names the files show. To bring the rest across, export from the old PC.

Bring everything with an export On the old PC, open Settings › Account , press Export… and leave Include my notes ticked. The window shows how big the zip will be. Audio is never included. Tick Include learned voices too if you want the new PC to recognize the same people; they are stored in the zip, so keep the file private. On the new PC press Import… , pick the zip and check what is inside ("Settings, Dictionary, 312 notes, 4 voices"). Tick the parts you want and press Import . Notes are merged, never replaced. A note you already have (the same folder name and start time) is left as it is, and nothing is deleted. One exception: a note that Find added and that you haven't edited since takes the zip's speaker names, tags, edits and what you left out. It keeps its place in your list and its folder. So you can run Find first and import later. Folders move with you. Each note's folder is moved from the old Notes folder to this PC's. If the folder is already there (OneDrive synced it), its files stay exactly as they are and the note is just pointed at it; otherwise the files come from the zip. Older and newer files. A zip from an older A9 Voice is brought up to date first. A zip from a newer one says This file is from a newer A9 Voice. Update first. Your API keys, your license and this PC's install ID are never in an export and never imported.

Related The note page : regenerate a summary with another template, and see what a note holds. Webhooks : send a summary to a channel automatically. Settings reference : Export and Import, and Find notes in this folder under Storage. Language models : the AI that writes the summary.

Find anything you or anyone said in your notes with Ctrl+K, and add folders of older notes to search alongside the new ones. To ask a question and get an answer, see Asking your notes. Search finds words in your notes. Ask answers a question from them, on its own page (see Asking your notes ). Both read one index that A9 Voice keeps on your PC, and both open the note at the moment you need. Ask answers in the language of the question, even when the meetings were in another language. To see a search, a question and an answer with links:

What gets searched Every note's title, summary, transcript, the notes you typed during the meeting, image captions and action items. Your dictations, unless you switch off Search dictations too (see Search dictations too ). Folders of past notes you add yourself (see Also search these folders ). The index is a file called search.db in A9 Voice's data folder, on your PC. It is kept current in the background, soon after a note changes. Notes are read from their files in the Notes folder, so an edit you make outside A9 Voice, in summary.md or transcript.md for example, counts too.

Search Press Ctrl + K in the A9 Voice window, or click the search box at the top of Home or Notes . Press Ctrl + K again, or Esc , to close it. The box is marked 1 below. The button marked 2, Ask your notes , opens the Ask page . Type what you remember. Every word you type has to match, and each word also matches longer words that start with it, so "approval routing" finds "approvals" and "routing". Matches are highlighted. The footer says how many results and that the search ran on this PC. Each result shows the note's title and date, what part matched ( Title , Summary , Transcript , Typed note , Image , Action item or Dictation ), who said it and when, and a snippet. A result from an added folder carries a badge with that folder's name. If nothing matches, the panel says so, and tells you if your filters are the reason. Click a result. The note opens at that moment, with the transcript line highlighted. A dictation result opens your dictation history instead. The note opens on the line you searched for.

Narrow it down The row of menus under the box limits what is searched. Changing one runs the search again. When: Any time , Past week , Past month or Past year . What: Notes and dictations , Notes or Dictations . Dictations is greyed out when Search dictations too is off. Template: only notes made with one template. Tag: only notes with one tag. Same meeting: only notes of a meeting that comes back again, such as a weekly stand-up. It appears when you have meetings with the same name on different days. Person: only notes where that person spoke.

Ask your notes Ask when you want an answer instead of a list. Ask has its own page in the sidebar, with a Quick , Deep and Template control next to the Ask button, filters, citations that open the note at the moment, your recent questions and a follow-up. Everything about it is on Asking your notes . From here, you can ask in two ways: Click Ask in the sidebar, or the Ask your notes button next to the search box on Home or Notes . Press Ctrl + K and open the Ask your notes tab. It has the same control and filters, and Open in Ask carries the question and its answer over to the Ask page. The Ask your notes tab. Open in Ask moves the answer to the Ask page. Questions asked here are in Recent questions on the Ask page too. Only the passages A9 Voice picked go to your language model; see What Ask sends and where it goes .

Search by meaning Search finds the words you type. Search by meaning also finds what you meant: ask about "funding" and it finds the meeting that said "finance signed off on the budget", ask about "people who were let go" and it finds "we had to lay off six contractors". It works on your own PC and costs nothing to run. How it works, in plain words: You download a small model once (about 24 MB, or 135 MB for a PC whose Windows is not in English, which reads about 100 languages). It is made by third parties under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license, A9 Voice checks every file against a fixed checksum, and a file that does not match is refused and deleted. In the background, at low priority, A9 Voice reads your notes once and writes a list of numbers for each stretch of conversation, summary paragraph, action item, typed note and image caption. Dictations are left out. It waits while you are recording or a note is being written up, and it picks up where it stopped after a restart. A question is turned into numbers the same way and compared with all of them, on your PC. The words result and the meaning result are merged, so a meeting that matches either way is found. What you type word for word still ranks first: a quoted phrase, a name or a ticket number ( ENG-4417 ) is found by its words before anything else. It applies to Search ( Ctrl + K ), Quick and Deep in Ask , and the connector 's search. The footer of a result or answer says + meaning when it was used. Nothing is sent anywhere for this: the model, the numbers and the comparing all stay on your PC. Turn it on in Settings › Search › Search by meaning , where it also shows how far the reading of your notes has got ("Search by meaning: 812 of 1,240 notes ready"). Search works the whole time: a note that is not done yet is found by its words. Remove deletes the model and the numbers, and search carries on by words, as it did before.

Search dictations too Search and Ask can include everything you have dictated. This is on to begin with. To leave dictations out, open Settings › General and switch off Search dictations too . The same switch decides whether connected AI apps (see the connector ) can see your dictation history.

Also search these folders You can also search notes you kept before A9 Voice: folders of past notes, Markdown or text files, or exports that have a summary and a transcript file. A9 Voice only reads these folders. It never changes, moves or deletes anything in them. Open Settings › Notes › Search . Under Also search these folders , click Add folder... and choose the folder. A9 Voice reads the folder. Its row shows the folder's name, its path and what is in it, such as "142 notes in this folder · read just now". The count fills in while the folder is read for the first time. The row counts notes in the folder itself: N notes in this folder is every note A9 Voice can read there. M already copied into A9 appears when some of those notes already have an editable copy in your Notes folder. Search shows the copy, so they are not indexed twice. Notes that are copied still count here, so a folder whose notes are all copied reads "13 notes in this folder · 13 already copied into A9", not zero. K couldn't be read appears when files were skipped (over 20 MB, in use by another program, or no access). Click it to open the logs folder, which names the files. includes Name appears when you also added a folder inside this one. Each note is read once, under the inner folder's row. You can't add the folder that holds your A9 Voice notes, a folder inside it, or a folder that contains it. Those notes are already searchable, and the Settings page says so. What counts as one note: a folder holding a summary and/or a transcript ( summary.md , transcript.md or .txt versions of them), with notes.md and an audio file beside them if there are any; and otherwise each Markdown or text file on its own. Formats are told apart by what is in the files, not by which app wrote them. A9 Voice's own note folders are skipped, so a folder that contains your Notes folder does not count notes twice. Good to know: The badge is the folder's own name. That is what shows next to results from it. Changes are picked up as they happen , and every folder is read again once a day. Read again now does it immediately. Remove stops searching the folder and forgets what was read from it. The folder itself is not touched. A folder can't overlap another. You can't add your own Notes folder, a folder inside it, or a folder that overlaps one you have already added. The app says which. If a folder goes missing, its row shows the problem, for example "That folder isn't there."

The first-run hint When you open Notes , A9 Voice looks next to your Notes folder for other folders that hold at least three notes. If it finds some, it asks "Bring in your older meetings?" and names them. Add folder adds them; Not now dismisses the question for good. If it finds none and you have added no folder, a plain link "Add a folder of past notes" is there instead.

h: Open a note from an added folder
t: Open a note from an added folder A result from an added folder opens as a read-only note, with the badge and Read only at the top. You can read the summary and transcript, play the audio if the folder has some, and use Open in folder . To change it, click Make editable copy . A9 Voice puts a copy in your Notes folder with the original date, and the original stays untouched. If you start to edit something (rename a speaker, edit a line, or Regenerate summary ), it asks "Make an editable copy to do this?" first, then carries on in the copy. Once a copy exists, search shows the copy instead of the original, and the original's page offers Open it . Copies are never used to teach voices .

Copy a whole folder Under a folder's row, Make editable copies of all notes in this folder... copies everything in one go. Click it. A9 Voice says how many notes it will copy (and how many have a recording), that the copies go to your Notes folder, that the originals stay untouched, and that summaries aren't rewritten, so no AI is used. Click Make copies . A progress bar shows "Copying 3 of 142". When it says "Made N editable copies", you can also rewrite their summaries with a template of your choice. Click Show the cost... first: it shows about what it will cost with which model. Regenerate summaries then works through them one at a time. Not now leaves the old summaries as they are.

If something goes wrong A note you just made is not found. Give it a few seconds: the index updates in the background. Search finds nothing in a folder you added. Check the folder's row on Settings › Notes › Search for a message, then try Read again now . Ask says to add a key, or answers from a different model than you chose. See Asking your notes . Dictations never show up. Check that Search dictations too is on in Settings › General . More in Troubleshooting .

Related Asking your notes : the Ask page, Quick and Deep, and the answer templates. The note page : ask about one note, and read it in full. Connector for AI apps : let Claude or ChatGPT search the same notes. Language models : the keys Ask needs. Voices : names for the people in your notes.

Ask a question in plain words across every meeting you have recorded and get an answer that links to the exact moment. Use Quick for a short answer and Deep to find every meeting a topic came up in. Ask answers a question from your notes. A9 Voice searches everything on your PC, picks the passages that matter, and writes an answer in which every fact links to the moment it was said. Answers come only from your notes (and your dictations, if you search them), and when the notes don't cover the question, it says so. The answer is written in the language of your question, even when the meetings were in another language. Looking for a word instead of an answer? That is Search .

The Ask page Ask has its own place in the sidebar: Home , Transcribe , Notes , Ask , then a divider and Dictionary . The Ask your notes button next to the search box on Home and Notes opens it too. Click Ask in the sidebar. Type a question in the large box, such as "When is the release cut, and what did Priya flag?" Leave the mode on Quick , or pick Deep or a template (see Quick and Deep ). Press Enter or click Ask . Read the answer. Each fact has a citation in blue that names the note, the date, the time and who said it. Click it and the note opens at that moment. The Ask page. The answer is on the left and your recent questions are on the right. The line under the answer says how it was made, for example "Quick answer · Answered by OpenRouter, Claude Haiku 5.5 · 10 passages sent · 1 meeting · about $0.0063 · Searched 168 notes (Jul 2 – Oct 10)". It names the template, the model that answered, how many passages were sent to it, how many meetings they came from, about what that cost, and how much of your notes was searched. Ask needs a language model with a key set up. If none is, you are asked to add one in Settings › Models (see Models ).

Start with an example Before you ask anything, the page shows three example questions, one for each way of answering. Click one to ask it. Three examples to start from. Quick: "When was the last QBR?" Deep: "Every time we discussed the budget" Who owes what: "What do I owe people this week?" If you have never started Notes, the page shows one more line: "Ask works across your meeting notes. Start your 30-day Notes trial ." The button opens Notes . Ask keeps working on notes you have already recorded, during the trial and after it.

Limit the question Under the box are chips and menus: All , This week , Any tag , Any meeting and Anyone . Pick one before you press Ask to answer only from that slice, for example only notes tagged vendor, or only meetings where Marcus spoke. Any meeting lists Same meeting: names, and appears once you have meetings with the same name on different days, such as a weekly stand-up. Any tag lists the tags your notes have, including the ones the AI added after each summary (see The note page ). Until a note has a tag it says No tags yet . Anyone lists every person your notes know, in alphabetical order, all the way to the last name; type to narrow it. Dates and names you write in the question itself work too: see Plain-language times and people .

Quick and Deep The control next to Ask has three parts: Quick , Deep and Template . It picks how this question is answered. Quick is selected every time the page opens. It reads about 10 passages and answers in a few sentences. Deep looks for every meeting the topic came up in and lists them. Template answers in a set shape, such as a briefing or who owes what (see The Template menu ). Deep and a template apply to that one question only . After the answer, the control goes back to Quick . If you would rather start on Deep, change Default answer in Settings › Notes › Search . (A follow-up keeps the mode of the question it follows; see Ask a follow-up .) Quick Deep What you get A short answer in a few sentences. A direct answer, then each item with every dated meeting it came up in, then what was searched. Reads about 10 passages up to 120 passages, up to about 60,000 tokens; when it lands on three meetings or fewer, those meetings in full Searches the words of your question your question 3 to 5 ways Good for "When was the last QBR?" "Every time we discussed the budget", "How many times did we talk about certificate management?"

What Deep does Quick finds a meeting. Deep is built to find every meeting, so a question like "What are the QBR decks we are working on?" lists each deck with the meetings it came from. It searches your question several ways. The Ask: Quick model rewrites it as 3 to 5 searches, with synonyms and abbreviations ("QBR", "quarterly business review"), and A9 Voice merges the results. It covers every meeting. It takes the best few passages of every meeting before taking more from any one, so one long meeting can't crowd out the others. It keeps going for counting questions. For "how many times", "how often", "every time" and "all the", it keeps pulling meetings until another page of results adds none you don't have, within its limits. The answer starts with the direct answer. Then each distinct item follows with every meeting it came up in, dated and cited, for example "IT Operations: Aug 10 QBR planning, Sep 4 stand-up, Oct 2 1:1". A counting question gives the count and a dated list of the meetings. The last line says what was covered, and the same line is in the footer: Searched 168 notes (Jul 2 – Oct 10) with 4 searches; 7 meetings matched. A Deep answer. The coverage line says what was searched. If the notes don't settle the question, Deep says what is missing instead of padding the answer.

h: What Ask reads: passages, or whole meetings
t: What Ask reads: passages, or whole meetings Ask never sends your whole library to the model. It sends what it picked, and the footer says how many passages. Quick sends the best passages, each with the two lines before and after it, and a one-line overview of its meeting. Deep sends the best few passages of every meeting that matched (up to 6 from one meeting), so a question that came up in twelve meetings reads all twelve. When Deep (or a wide template) lands on three meetings or fewer, it reads those meetings whole : the summary and the full transcript of each, with the time and the speaker on every line, so a citation still opens the exact moment. If a meeting is too long for your model's request, which happens on Groq's free tier, it reads the summary and the parts of the transcript that matter most to your question, and gives each meeting an even share. The line under the answer says which it was: "Read the full transcript of 1 meeting (Oct 14).", "Read 2 meetings in full and the best parts of 1." or "Read the best parts of 1 meeting (Oct 14)." With four meetings or more, Deep works as before. Deep takes longer than Quick (the app says up to a minute while it works) and costs more, "a few cents at most". Hover over Deep to see an estimate for your model, such as "Deep · about 2¢ with Claude Haiku 5.5". The footer under each answer says what that answer cost.

Choose the Deep model Open Settings › Models and click Change on Ask: Deep . A template can name its own model too. The list holds every model your providers offer. A Good for Deep badge marks models with a context of 100,000 tokens or more and a stronger tier, and each row shows about what one Deep answer would cost. Same as Summaries is the default. A stronger model writes fuller answers. See Models . Settings › Notes › Search has a Models for Ask row that opens the same page.

The Template menu Template ▾ opens a list of the other ways to answer: Briefing , Latest on… , Who owes what , Decision log , Meeting prep , Exec status , any templates you made, and Edit templates… at the bottom. Pick one and the segment shows its name, for example Who owes what . Like Deep , it applies to that one question. The Template menu. Edit templates… opens Settings › Templates , where you change them (see Edit the templates ).

Answer templates Template What you get Reads Looks back Newest first Quick answer A short answer in a few sentences. about 10 passages any time no Deep A direct answer, then each item with every meeting it came up in, then what was searched. up to 120 any time no Briefing Background, how it developed (dated), core issues, current status, open items with owners, with quotes shown as (Note, date). about 50 any time no Latest on… The most recent mention first with its date, then what changed since the one before, then earlier ones. about 40 any time yes Who owes what Commitments grouped by person, with due dates and where each was said. Flags what is overdue. about 50 90 days yes Decision log Each decision with its date, who decided, the reason and the source quote. about 40 any time no Meeting prep For a person or topic: the last interactions, open items both ways, and points to raise. about 40 90 days yes Exec status Three to five bullets an executive can read in 30 seconds: status, risk, ask, business impact. about 30 any time yes Quick answer and Deep have their own buttons; the menu lists the rest. A template with about 10 passages searches with the words of your question and answers fast. A wider one first asks the model for more search words, searches more widely, and groups what it finds by meeting with each meeting's overview; it takes longer and costs more, "a few cents at most". Newest first. For questions about "the last ask", "the latest", "the most recent" or "now", the newest matching passages must be read even when an older meeting matches the words better. A9 Voice does this whenever the template has Newest first on, and also whenever your question contains "last", "latest", "most recent", "current" or "now". The meetings are listed newest first with their dates, and the model is told to lead with the most recent mention. Every template ends the same way: the answer uses only the passages found, cites each fact, writes about people factually (what they said, asked, decided or did) and says so when the notes don't cover the question. Each template names the model that writes its answer: Same as Ask: Quick , Same as Ask: Deep , or a model of its own. Quick and Deep have their own model under Ask: Quick and Ask: Deep in Settings › Models , and both default to Same as Summaries . If you have not chosen a Summary model, A9 Voice uses the best one you have set up. If a model is busy, too slow or can't take a request that big, the next one you set up answers instead, and the line says "(after: ...)" with what went wrong, for example after: Groq rate limit (429) or after: request too large for Groq's per-minute token cap on this model . A request known not to fit is skipped without being sent. Only A9 Voice's own blue citations appear. If a model writes its own marks, such as 【13】 or [13†source], they are turned into the same citations, or dropped when no passage has that number. The cost is an estimate from the price table in Settings › Usage & cost , not a bill.

Edit the templates Open Settings › Templates and choose Ask templates , or pick Edit templates… in the Template menu. The list holds the eight built-in templates and your own. Built-ins can be edited and Reset to built-in brings the original back. Duplicate copies one to change; + Create template starts a new one; Delete… removes one of yours. The Ask template editor. What to do is plain words for the model, and Sections are the headings of the answer, each with what to write there. The arrows reorder them. Passages to read is about 10 for a short answer and 40 to 60 for a full one. More passages cost more. Look back limits the search to the last 30 or 90 days, unless the question's own filter ( This week , a tag, a person) is narrower. Newest first , Model and Also search for (words searched with every question, for example "action item due owner") finish the template. View full prompt shows exactly what is sent, including the rules that stay fixed for every template.

Plain-language times and people You can write when and who in the question as you would say it. Before it searches, A9 Voice reads the times and the names of people your notes know, and uses them to narrow the search. This works in Quick , Deep and every template. What it understood shows as chips above the answer: What was read out of the question, as chips you can remove. Click the small ✕ on a chip to ask the question again without it.

Times Days: "yesterday", "last Wednesday", "3 days ago", "two weeks ago", or a date such as "September 4" or "2026-09-04". Ranges: "this week", "last week", "in September", "since the 1st". "Last Wednesday" means the most recent Wednesday before today. "This week" runs from your PC's first day of the week. A question that is only a time, such as "what happened last Wednesday", reads the summaries of the meetings from that day.

People A name your notes know becomes a chip, and "What did Priya say?" reads the passages Priya spoke before the passages that only mention her. If a first name belongs to two people, the chip says so, for example Dana: 2 people , and both are used. Click the chip to pick one, and the question is asked again.

When nothing matches A9 Voice never leaves you with an empty page without saying why. If nothing matches the chips, it says, for example, "Nothing from Priya on Wed Oct 7. Showing the nearest days instead." and looks three days either side. If that finds nothing, it searches without the chips and says so.

Everything someone said Some questions are not questions for a model. "What did Nick say over the last month and a half?" is a filter: every line Nick said, across every meeting. A9 Voice answers it from the search index on your PC, so it is instant, free and sends nothing anywhere. Open it from any of these: The Ask page's person filter. Click Anyone , find or type a name, and press Everything Nick said under the buttons. A speaker on a note. In the Speakers panel, the ⋯ menu of a named speaker has Everything Nick said . Ctrl+K. Type a known person's name (a first name works) and Everything Nick said appears above the results. The view replaces the answer area; Back returns to your question. Everything one person said. The totals line is counted on your PC, never written by a model. The person and the range. The name opens the same picker to switch people. The range is This week , 30 days (the default), 90 days , All , or Custom with a from and a to date. Containing. Type words to keep only the lines that have them. It matches the way Search does, and the matches are highlighted. The counts follow. Meetings, newest first. Each shows its title, date, how many lines Nick said in it and about how long that took. The first three lines show; Show all 42 lines opens the rest. A time stamp opens the note at that moment, like a citation in an answer. Fifty meetings show at a time and the next fifty load as you scroll. The totals line. "Nick spoke in 23 meetings (Sep 2 – Oct 15): 1,412 lines, about 3 h 10 m." is counted from the index. When other meetings list Nick but no speaker there is named as Nick yet, the line says so ("4 more meetings list Nick but have speakers not named yet.") and See the 4 meetings lists them. Open one, name the speaker (see The note page ), and those lines are here when you come back. Copy and save. Copy puts the view on the clipboard as Markdown. Save as .md and Save as .csv ask where to save (Downloads by default). The CSV has the columns meeting, date, time and line. Only lines a speaker said count: the summary, typed notes and what other people said about Nick are not in it. Notes from an added folder count when their transcript has speaker names. Names match as written in your notes; pick the full name when two people share a first name.

Ask about what Nick said The one place a model comes in, and only when you press it. Ask about what Nick said opens a question box. Your question goes to the Ask: Quick model with only these lines, after the range and Containing : no summaries, no other speakers. A long list is cut to the lines that matter most to the question and fit your model's request, and the line under the answer says how many were sent ("Sent 120 of 412 lines Nick said, from 23 meetings.") and what it cost. Citations open the exact moment. Without a language model set up, everything above still works; only this button needs one.

Keys in the Ask box Key What it does Enter Asks in the selected mode. Ctrl + Enter Asks Deep , whatever is selected. Alt + 1 Selects Quick . Alt + 2 Selects Deep . Alt + 3 Opens the Template menu. Esc Closes the Template menu. The same keys work in the Ask your notes tab of Ctrl + K . The tab says so along its bottom edge. The full list of keys is on Keyboard shortcuts .
Recent questions and follow-ups

Recent questions The column on the right of the Ask page lists your last 50 questions. Each row shows the question, how it was asked ( Quick , Deep or a template) and when: the time if it was today, the day if it was earlier. Click a row to see its saved answer, with "Saved answer from Oct 8" and Run again . Nothing is sent when you only look. Run again (the circular arrow on a row) asks the question again with today's notes. Delete (the cross on a row) removes that question. Clear all removes every one, after asking you to confirm. Recent questions. Each row has Run again and Delete. In a narrow window, the list folds behind a Recent questions button above the answer. Recent questions are kept on this PC with the app's other data, in a small file in A9 Voice's data folder, and are never sent anywhere. They also include questions you ask from Ctrl + K .

Ask a follow-up Under an answer, Ask a follow-up opens a second box. Type a question about the answer and press Enter . The question and answer above go along as context, and the same filters apply. The follow-up's answer appears under the first, labeled Follow-up . A follow-up stays on the same meetings, in the same mode: Same mode. The mode control beside the follow-up box starts on the mode of the question it follows, so a follow-up to a Deep answer is a Deep follow-up. Change it before you ask if you want another. The main box still goes back to Quick (or your default) after an answer. Same meetings. The follow-up reads only the meetings the answer above cited, shown as a chip, From the 2 meetings above . With three or fewer it reads them whole, in Quick too, so "what did Marcus say about the deadline?" is answered from the full meeting, not a few lines of it. Click the chip's ✕ to ask the follow-up again over all your notes. There is one follow-up, not a chat. To go further, start a new question; the one you just asked is in Recent questions.

From Ctrl+K Press Ctrl + K anywhere in the A9 Voice window and open the Ask your notes tab to ask without leaving what you are doing. It has the same Quick, Deep and Template control, the same keys and the same filters. Open in Ask , at the bottom of the tab, carries the question and its answer over to the Ask page.

h: What Ask sends and where it goes
t: What Ask sends and where it goes Only the passages A9 Voice picked go to your language model , with your question. Never a whole note, and never any audio. For Deep and the wider templates the question is sent once first so the model can suggest more search words. A follow-up also sends the question and answer it follows. Searching is done on your PC. The index is a file in A9 Voice's data folder. The same goes for working out the times and people in your question. Recent questions stay on this PC. They are never sent anywhere and are not part of any request. A model on your own PC keeps all of it on your PC. Add a local server in Settings › Models with Add custom API . See Privacy and your data for everything that can leave your PC.

When there is no answer If nothing in your notes is about the question, you get "I couldn't find that in your notes." Nothing is invented. When the search finds no passages at all, nothing from your notes is sent to the model. Try different words, widen the filters, or remove a chip.

If something goes wrong Ask says to add a key. Ask uses a language model. Add one in Settings › Models . The answer is missing a meeting you know is there. Try Deep , or remove a chip: a date or a name may have narrowed the search. A note you just made can take a few seconds to be searchable. The footer says "after: request too large for Groq's per-minute token cap". One request was bigger than your Groq plan takes in a minute. It is not a rate limit and never counts as usage. The next model answered. Choose a model with more room for Ask: Deep . Dictations never show up. Check that Search dictations too is on in Settings › General . More in Troubleshooting .

Related Search and Ask : find words in your notes, and add folders of older notes. The note page : ask about one note, and read it in full. Models : pick the model for Quick and for Deep. Language models : the keys Ask needs. Connector for AI apps : let Claude or ChatGPT search the same notes.

Let an AI app on your PC, such as Claude Desktop or ChatGPT desktop, search and read your A9 Voice notes, so you can ask it about your meetings. It is read only, off until you turn it on, and nothing leaves your PC except what that app reads. The connector is a small helper that AI apps can start on your PC. Once an app is connected, you can ask it things like "What did Priya say about the approval routing?" or "What action items do I have from this week?" and it looks the answer up in your notes. It is also called an MCP server, which is the name the AI apps use for a connector they run on your own PC. You will see "MCP" in those apps' settings.

What the connector does It runs on your PC. The AI app starts it itself as a small background program with no window and no tray icon. A9 Voice does not have to be open. It reads your notes from the same place A9 Voice keeps them. It is read only. It can search and read. It cannot add, change or delete a note. It is off by default. Until you turn it on, an app that asks gets a short message instead of your notes: "The A9 Voice connector is turned off. Turn it on in A9 Voice › Settings › Connectors." You choose the apps. Nothing is shared until you connect an app yourself.

h: What an AI app can ask for
t: What an AI app can ask for Once you connect an app, it can use four tools. All four are marked read only. Tool What it returns search_notes The best matches for some words: the note's id, title and date, the time in the meeting, who spoke, which part matched and a snippet. It can be narrowed by date range, tag, person, meeting name, or notes versus dictations. Up to 50 results (10 unless it asks for more). list_notes Your notes, newest first: id, title, date, length, tags and people. It can be narrowed by date, tag and person. Up to 100 (20 unless it asks for more). read_note One note: its summary (the default), its full transcript with [mm:ss] Speaker lines, or the notes you typed during the meeting. get_action_items Action items, newest first: the task, owner, due date, whether it is ticked off, and the note it came from. Done items are left out unless it asks for them. The tools cover your A9 Voice notes and any folders you added under Settings › Notes › Search (see Search and Ask ). Your dictations are included in search results while Search dictations too in Settings › General is on. It is on for a new install; switch it off to keep dictations out.

h: What an AI app can never get
t: What an AI app can never get Audio. No recording, ever. Voiceprints. The voices A9 Voice has learned (see Voices ) are not part of any tool's answer. Your keys and settings. The tools return notes only.

h: What it can read once you connect it
t: What it can read once you connect it Plainly: a connected app can read the titles, dates, summaries, full transcripts (with the speakers' names), typed notes, image captions, tags and action items of the notes it asks for, and it can ask for as many as it likes. A transcript is everything that was said in the meeting. When the app reads something, that text becomes part of your conversation with the app. From that point it is handled by that app and the service behind it, under their own terms and privacy settings, not by A9 Voice. A9 Voice cannot see what the app does with it afterwards. Connect only apps you trust with your meetings, and use the switch to turn the connector off when you do not want to share.

Turn it on Open Settings › Connectors . Switch Connector for AI apps on. The switch is marked 1 below. Then connect an app: either Claude Desktop with one button, or any other app by pasting a command.

Connect Claude Desktop Under Claude Desktop , click Connect to Claude Desktop... (or Turn on & connect to Claude Desktop... if the switch is still off). A9 Voice first shows what it will change , before it changes anything. It lists one line: it adds (or updates, if it is already there) an entry called a9-voice , the "A9 Voice notes connector", in Claude Desktop's settings file. The rest of the file stays exactly as it is. Your other connectors and settings are not touched. If the file already exists, A9 Voice makes a backup copy of it first, in the same folder, with .a9v-backup added to the name. Click Connect (or Turn on & connect , which also turns the connector on), or Cancel to change nothing. Quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again, so it loads the new connector. The page says "Connected, and the connector is on. Quit and reopen Claude Desktop to load it." Connected. The switch is On and Recent requests show what has been asked. Claude Desktop's settings file is %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json . If Claude Desktop is not installed on your PC, the page says so ("Claude Desktop isn't installed on this PC. You can connect it later, or use the steps for other apps below.").

A Microsoft Store copy A Store copy of A9 Voice cannot change another app's settings file, so there is no Connect button. The page tells you so and shows Copy settings (JSON) instead. In Claude Desktop open Settings › Developer › Edit Config , paste the settings into that file (add the a9-voice entry next to any others), save, and quit and reopen Claude Desktop. The command in it is a9voice.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps , the shortcut Windows keeps for the Store copy, and it reads the Store copy's notes. A copy from a9voice.com has its own connector and its own notes.

h: Connect ChatGPT desktop or another app
t: Connect ChatGPT desktop or another app Under Other apps , A9 Voice gives you two things to copy. Copy command copies the command that starts the connector: the full path to A9 Voice's program followed by --mcp . Copy settings (JSON) copies the same thing as a settings block, for apps that read a settings file. The steps, as the page words them: ChatGPT desktop: Settings › MCP servers › Add server. Pick STDIO, paste the command, save, then Restart. ChatGPT's web chats can't use connectors on your PC: it has to be the desktop app. Cursor: paste the settings into %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json (or Settings › MCP › Add ). Any other app that runs local connectors (the page calls them MCP servers) can use A9 Voice the same way: paste the command, or the settings, where that app asks for a local server. The names and screens of those apps are theirs and can change. If a step does not match what you see, look for the app's own section on connectors or MCP servers.

See what apps asked Recent requests lists what connected apps have asked for, newest first: the time, what kind of request it was ( Searched , Listed notes , Read , Action items ) and what it was about, such as the words searched. It keeps the latest requests on your PC, nothing more. Requests made while the connector is off are not run, so they do not show here.

h: Turn it off or remove it
t: Turn it off or remove it Pause sharing: switch Connector for AI apps off. Connected apps stay set up, but they get the short "turned off" message instead of your notes. Switch it back on to resume. Remove an app for good: A9 Voice has no remove button. In the other app, delete the a9-voice connector in its own settings. For Claude Desktop that means removing the a9-voice entry from claude_desktop_config.json (A9 Voice's backup, claude_desktop_config.json.a9v-backup , is the file as it was before). The A9 Voice page shows "Connected" for as long as that entry is there.

If something goes wrong The AI app says it has no tools from A9 Voice. Quit and reopen the app fully after connecting, and check that the switch on Settings › Connectors is On. The app says the connector is turned off. Switch Connector for AI apps on. Connect to Claude Desktop shows an error about the file. The settings file is not valid JSON. Fix or remove it, then try again. A9 Voice does not show Connected after you moved or reinstalled it. The connected entry points to where A9 Voice was installed. Click Connect again to update it. More in Troubleshooting .

Related Search and Ask : the same notes, searched from inside A9 Voice. Voices : voiceprints stay on your PC and are never part of the connector. Privacy and your data : everything A9 Voice sends and stores.

Send each note to another service when it is ready: your own second brain, an automation in n8n, Zapier or Make, or a chat channel in Discord, Slack or Telegram. A webhook is a web address that another service gives you. When a note is ready, A9 Voice posts it to that address, and the service does whatever you set it up to do: file the note, make tasks from the action items, or post the summary in a channel. You choose what is sent and which notes are sent. The service on the other end gets what you tick and nothing else. Audio, image files and voiceprints are never sent. Whoever can read that service can read what you send to it, so add only places you trust.

Set up a webhook Open Settings › Notes › Integrations and click + Add webhook . Choose the Type . Under the menu, a line tells you where to get the address for that type. Generic JSON , n8n , Zapier and Make get a JSON payload (see The JSON payload ). Discord , Slack and Telegram get the summary as text, trimmed to fit that service. Give it a Name (optional; the type's name is used if you leave it empty) and paste the URL . The URL is hidden as you type. For the JSON types, tick What to send (see What to send ), then choose When , and optionally limit which notes with Only . Click Send a test to check it (see Send a test ), then Save . Saving needs a URL. If the address is wrong for the type you picked, the form says what it expects, for example "Paste the Discord webhook URL ( https://discord.com/api/webhooks/… )" or "Use an https:// URL".

What each type needs Type Where the address comes from What it receives Generic JSON Any receiver that accepts a web request The JSON payload n8n A Webhook trigger node (POST); paste its production URL The JSON payload Zapier "Webhooks by Zapier", then Catch Hook; paste its URL The JSON payload Make A Custom webhook module; paste its address The JSON payload Discord Server settings › Integrations › Webhooks › New webhook › Copy URL The summary as text Slack An incoming webhook for a channel The summary as text Telegram https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage?chat_id=<chat id> The summary as text Discord, Slack and Telegram addresses are checked: Discord must be a discord.com webhook address, Slack must be on hooks.slack.com , and Telegram must be the sendMessage address with a chat_id . A chat webhook sends the note's title, when it happened and the summary. A note without a summary has nothing to send, and the webhook says "This note has no summary yet". Discord, Slack and Telegram send the summary only, so there is no What to send list.

What to send For the JSON types, tick any of these. Fields you do not tick are left out of the payload. Summary Action items (structured) Decisions Transcript : the whole conversation. This is off unless you turn it on, and the form warns you: "This sends the full conversation to this address." Typed notes and markers Image captions (never the image files)

When When a note finishes sends note.completed once, when the note is ready. When a note finishes, and again when it changes (JSON types only) also sends note.updated after a rename, a speaker named, a summary redone or an edit, 60 seconds after the last change. Use it so a receiver stays in step with the note. Manual only sends nothing by itself. See Send by hand .

Only some notes In the Only row, type tags (for example #customer ) to send only notes that have at least one of them. Tick one or more templates to send only notes made with them. Leave both empty and every note is sent. This works for every type.

Security HTTPS only. An address must start with https:// . For a receiver running on your own PC, http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 are allowed too. Signing secret (JSON types, optional). Paste any secret you make up, and each request carries a signature the receiver can check to be sure it came from A9 Voice. See Check the signature . Header (JSON types, optional). A header name and a value, for example Authorization and Bearer ... . The name can hold only letters, digits and dashes. Kept in Windows Credential Manager. The URL, the signing secret and the header value are stored there, like your API keys. They are not in A9 Voice's settings file or its logs. When you edit a webhook, the fields show "Saved" and you paste a new value only to replace it.

Retries and offline A send that fails is tried again after 10 seconds, after 1 minute and after 5 minutes. Then it gives up and the log says so. A send made while your PC is offline waits, and is tried again every minute, for up to 24 hours. Each attempt waits up to 20 seconds for an answer. Any answer in the 200s counts as delivered.

Send a test Send a test posts a made-up note ("Platform stand-up (test)", with Sam Example and Jane Doe) to the address and shows what came back. For the JSON types it is a real payload with the parts you ticked, signed and with your header. For chat types it is a short message: "A9 Voice test: this webhook works. Note summaries will arrive here." On success the form says "Delivered (200)" and the start of the reply. On failure it says why: "Refused (401): check the URL, secret or header" (also for 403), "Not found (404): was the webhook deleted?", "Rate limited (429)", "No answer in 20 s" or "Couldn't reach it (offline?)". You can also click Test on a saved webhook in the list.

Your webhooks The list shows each webhook with its type, its name, when it sends, and its last result, such as "When a note finishes · Last: Thu 3:09 AM · delivered". A problem shows in amber, and a number says how many sends are waiting to be retried. Each row has Test , Log , Edit and Delete... (click it again to confirm). Deleting a webhook drops any sends still waiting for it.

The delivery log Log opens the list of sends for that webhook: the time, the event ( note.completed or note.updated ), the note's title, the HTTP status the receiver answered with, the size, and Resend . Resend sends that note again, the same way as any other send, with retries.

Send by hand On a note's page, each webhook has a Send to ... button in the right column with its name, and a line under it that says what happened last, for example "Sent automatically at 3:58 AM · delivered". Press it to send that note now as note.completed . A hand send is tried once, and the result is shown right there; use the log's Resend if you want retries.

The JSON payload This is what Generic JSON , n8n , Zapier and Make receive. The data in this example is made up. { "schema_version": 1, "event": "note.completed", "sent_at": "2026-10-05T17:41:00Z", "app": { "name": "A9 Voice", "version": "0.6.0" }, "note": { "id": "8f0c2d1e-5b7a-4c3e-9d21-7a4e5f6b8c90", "title": "Platform stand-up", "started_at": "2026-10-05T16:00:00Z", "duration_sec": 1722, "source": "manual", "template": "Meeting Notes", "tags": ["stand-up"], "participants": [{ "name": "Jane Doe", "is_me": false, "talk_sec": 410 }], "summary_md": "## Overview\n…", "action_items": [{ "task": "Send checklist", "owner": "Jane Doe", "due": "2026-10-07", "mine": false }], "decisions": ["Release cut Thursday 4 PM"], "notes_md": "- [12:03] **Decision:** Release cut Thursday", "images": [{ "at_sec": 723, "caption": "Approval routing" }], "transcript": { "segments": [{ "start": 0.0, "end": 4.2, "speaker": "Jane Doe", "text": "…" }] } } } The fields: schema_version : always 1 for this layout. event : note.completed or note.updated . sent_at : when the payload was prepared, in UTC. A retry sends the same payload, with the same sent_at . app : the app's name and version. note.id : stays the same for the life of the note, in every event, even if the note is renamed. A receiver can use it to update the same item instead of making a new one. note.title , started_at (UTC), duration_sec , template (the template's name) and tags are always there. note.source : a short lowercase id of the meeting app A9 Voice detected, other for an app you added yourself, or manual when you started the recording yourself. note.participants : each speaker who talked, with their name as shown in the note, is_me (this is you) and talk_sec , their talk time in seconds. Someone who never spoke is left out. summary_md : the summary as Markdown ( Summary ). action_items : a list of task , owner , due and mine (it is one of your own items). due is the due date as it was said in the meeting, such as "Tue", "next week" or a date, or an empty string ( Action items (structured) ). decisions : the bullet points under the summary's Decisions heading ( Decisions ). notes_md : what you typed or marked during the meeting, one line each, with its time and, for markers, Action: , Decision: or Callout: ( Typed notes and markers ). images : for each image, at_sec (when in the meeting) and caption . Never the image file ( Image captions ). transcript.segments : each start and end in seconds, the speaker name and the text ( Transcript ). Fields you did not tick are left out. A very large transcript is dropped. If the whole payload would be over 10 MB, it is sent without the transcript and with "transcript_omitted": "too_large" in note .

Headers Each request is a POST with these headers: Content-Type: application/json User-Agent: A9 Voice webhooks X-A9-Event : the event, note.completed or note.updated . X-A9-Timestamp : when this attempt was made, in Unix seconds. X-A9-Signature : only if you set a signing secret. See below. Your own header, if you set one.

Check the signature With a signing secret, X-A9-Signature is sha256= followed by the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body , using your secret as the key. Compute it over the exact bytes you received, before parsing the JSON, and compare it before trusting the body. The timestamp header is not part of the signature. import hashlib, hmac expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(SECRET.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() ok = hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers["X-A9-Signature"])
Examples

n8n In n8n, add a Webhook node. Set the HTTP method to POST and respond Immediately . Copy its Production URL . In A9 Voice, open Settings › Notes › Integrations , click + Add webhook , choose n8n , paste the URL and tick what to send. Click Send a test . In n8n, the test arrives as body.note . For example, add a Split Out node on body.note.action_items to turn each action item into its own task in your tracker, keyed on body.note.id so an update replaces the earlier version.

Zapier In Zapier, start a Zap with "Webhooks by Zapier" and the Catch Hook trigger. Copy the address it gives you. In A9 Voice, add a webhook of type Zapier , paste the address and tick what to send. Click Send a test . Back in Zapier, test the trigger. The test note arrives with the fields from The JSON payload , such as title , summary_md and action_items , which you can use in the steps that follow. Use id to tell notes apart.

Make In Make, add a Custom webhook module as the start of a scenario. Copy its address. In A9 Voice, add a webhook of type Make , paste the address and tick what to send. Click Send a test . In Make, the test note's fields are available to the modules that follow. Use note.id to tell notes apart. How you use the fields next is up to the service. Their own help covers their screens; A9 Voice only sends the payload above.

If something goes wrong Test says Refused (401) or (403). The receiver did not accept the request. Check the address, the signing secret and the header value. If the service needs a token, put it in Header . Test says Not found (404). The address is wrong, or the webhook was deleted at the other end. Nothing arrives, and the log says "trying again". The receiver is answering with errors or is slow. A9 Voice tries again after 10 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes, then gives up. Fix the receiver and use Resend in the log. The webhook never fires. Check its When : Manual only sends only when you press Send to ... . Check Only too: a tag or template filter that no note matches sends nothing. A chat webhook says This note has no summary yet. Chat types send the summary, so the note needs one first. Add a language model and make a summary (see Language models ). "Couldn't reach it (offline?)". Your PC could not reach the address. Offline sends wait up to 24 hours and go out when you are back online. More in Troubleshooting .

Every page in Settings and every option on it, in the order the app shows them, with what it does and what a new install starts with. Open Settings at the bottom of the sidebar. The list on the left has four parts: Account , General and Privacy at the top, then Shared , Transcribe and Notes . In a narrow window the list turns into a drop-down called Settings page . The sidebar itself starts open at any window width; Shrink sidebar at its bottom shrinks it to icons, and A9 Voice remembers your choice. This page follows that list.
