If pressing Restart to update fails, a short message appears under it for a few seconds, for example "Busy dictating; try again in a moment".

Restart automatically when idle On the Updates card, Restart automatically when idle decides whether A9 Voice restarts into a ready update by itself. When it is on, A9 Voice restarts into the update once you have not dictated for 2 minutes. It never does this while you are dictating, or recording, or while a note is being written up. When it is off, the update waits until you press Restart to update . If you have never touched the switch, it is off on Stable and on for Dev. Either way, an update you queued during a recording installs by itself once the recording and its note are done.

The Updates card The card is on Settings › General, under the General options and above the About card. This version shows the version you run and the last check: "Checking…", "You're up to date", "Downloading", an error message, or when it last checked ("Last checked 12 minutes ago"). Check now checks right away. Channel is the Dev / Stable choice described above. Restart automatically when idle is the switch described above. Every option is described on the Settings reference .

The Microsoft Store copy If you installed A9 Voice from the Microsoft Store, the Store updates it, and A9 Voice does not look for updates itself. Settings › General › Updates shows your version and "Updates come from the Microsoft Store." There is no channel, no Check now and no Restart automatically when idle , and the sidebar has no Check for updates link. To check by hand, open the Microsoft Store, then Library , then Get updates . Start with Windows uses the startup setting Windows keeps for apps. If you turned A9 Voice off in Task Manager (Startup apps) or in Settings › Apps › Startup, the switch in A9 Voice cannot turn it back on, and says so under the switch. Turn it on there. Your files are separate. A Store copy keeps its settings, notes and downloaded speech models in a private folder that belongs to the package, under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages . It does not read the folders of a copy installed from a9voice.com, and the other way round. Your API keys are in Windows Credential Manager, which both copies use. Removing the Store copy removes the files in its private folder, so export what you want to keep first (Settings › Notes › Storage, and Moving your notes to a new PC ). Show in folder and Open the logs folder open the folder where the files really are. Both installed. If A9 Voice finds a copy from a9voice.com on the PC too, it says "A9 Voice is also installed from a9voice.com. Keep one; they don't share notes." once, at the top of the window. It removes nothing and moves nothing. Sending a problem report works the same. The report starts with a line that says the copy is from a package. The copy from a9voice.com is unchanged: it updates itself as described above.

If an update is interrupted An update closes A9 Voice, runs the installer and starts the new version. If something in the middle stops it, for example Windows or security software holding the installer back, A9 Voice does not stay closed: Right before it hands over, A9 Voice asks Windows to start it again two minutes later if it is not running. This is a one-time entry in your own Task Scheduler (no administrator rights; it runs only while you are signed in). A9 Voice removes it the next time it starts, and it removes itself an hour after it was due, so it never opens A9 Voice a day later. The installer starts the copy you already had when it cannot finish. Either way A9 Voice comes back quietly in the tray. If it was the old version, it says "The update to X didn't finish" and tries again when nothing is in use.

If something goes wrong "Couldn't reach the update server". The PC is offline or something blocks the connection. A9 Voice tries again at the next check. The update check is the only thing A9 Voice does on its own that is not part of a service you set up; see Privacy and data . "No release on the dev channel yet" (or stable). The channel has no build published yet. Switch channel or check again later. "The update failed its signature check and was not installed". The download did not match what the project signed, so A9 Voice refused it. Check again; if it keeps happening, see Troubleshooting . "The update to 0.6.9 didn't finish." You pressed Restart to update (or A9 Voice restarted itself when idle), but the installer never replaced the app, so this is still the old version. A9 Voice shows this once when it starts, and tries the update again by itself when you are not dictating or recording, once per start. You can also press Restart to update when it shows. If it keeps happening, restart the PC and update again, then see Troubleshooting . "The update didn't install. You can try again now or install it from the download page." The same update failed twice in one day, so A9 Voice stopped trying by itself until tomorrow. The note appears at the top of every page and on the Updates card. Try again installs it now (still never while you are dictating or recording); Download page opens the page for your channel, where you can install by hand. A newer version is not held back by this. "A9 Voice is still closing. Restart your PC to finish the update; A9 Voice will update itself next time it starts." The installer could not end the running copy of A9 Voice, even after waiting and trying to force it. Nothing was changed: the version you had still works. Restart the PC; the update installs by itself the next time A9 Voice starts. The version line says "Couldn't check". The check could not finish. Press Check for updates again in a minute.
Related Settings reference for the whole Updates card. Privacy and data for what the update check sends. Troubleshooting .

What leaves your PC and where it goes, how to keep everything on your PC, where your files live, how long they are kept and how to delete them. A9 Voice keeps your data on your PC. It calls speech and language services with your own keys , and only the ones you set up. There is no A9 Voice server in between, no account and no sign-in. This page lists every place data can go. Where something is a promise about how the app is built rather than a setting you can change, it says so.

The short version Audio and text go only to the services you choose , with your keys. If you use models on this PC, nothing you say leaves it. One anonymous count, which you can turn off. The update check carries a random ID, the version, your channel, your Windows version and your country, so we can count installs, and five one-time messages (setup finished, first dictation, first note, Notes trial started, Notes bought) say how far people get. No crash reports, never what you said or recorded. See Anonymous usage counts . Problem reports are sent only when you press Send, and you can read the exact text first. They hold your words and a scrubbed block of diagnostics, never keys, audio, transcripts or names. See Reporting a problem . Your keys live in Windows Credential Manager and nowhere else: not in settings, logs, the repository or the app's own storage. Logs hold timings, lengths and status codes, never your words or your keys. This is also a rule of how the app is built. Voiceprints stay on this PC , are opt-in, and you can delete any of them or all of them at any time. Notes are plain files in a folder you pick. Recording consent is up to you. Some places require everyone's permission to record a conversation. A9 Voice shows a short notice about it when Notes starts. See Recording consent .

t: What leaves your PC, feature by feature The table says what is sent, to whom, and what happens when you use a model on this PC instead. What you do With a cloud service With a model on this PC Dictate (hold the key) The audio of that dictation, the language, and your Dictionary words as spelling hints go to the speech service chosen for dictation. If it fails or takes longer than 4 seconds, the same audio goes once to your fallback service. Nothing leaves. Enhance with AI The dictated text, your Dictionary spellings and your custom instructions go to the one language model you chose for Enhance. Nothing leaves if that model is a server on your own PC. Live transcript during a meeting While the Live window is open (and a minute after), your microphone and the computer audio stream live, as two channels, to Deepgram. If a speech model on this PC keeps up, the live transcript is made on this PC. Meeting transcript after a recording The audio of each channel (your microphone, and what your speakers played) goes to the speech service chosen for notes. Nothing leaves. Summary, title and tags The transcript with speaker names and times, any notes you typed or marked during the meeting, your name, the template, your Dictionary spellings, your existing tags and the times and captions of your images go to a language model. Images and audio are not sent. Nothing leaves if the model is a server on your own PC. Ask (on a note, or in the Live window) The question goes to the summary model with the note's summary, its image times and captions, and its transcript (in the Live window: the transcript so far). Same as above. Ask page and Ask your notes (Ctrl+K) The question and only the best matching passages (about 10 for Quick , up to 120 for Deep ) go to the language model. Deep and the wider templates first send the question alone so the model can suggest more search words. A follow-up also carries the question and answer it follows. Recognizing times and names in your question happens on your PC. Same as above. Search by meaning (optional) The model is downloaded once from Hugging Face, the way the speech models are. After that nothing leaves: your notes are turned into numbers and compared on this PC, and the numbers stay in meaning.db . Nothing leaves. Recent questions on the Ask page Nothing. The last 50 questions and their answers are kept in a small file in A9 Voice's data folder, on this PC. Nothing. Search (Ctrl+K) Nothing. The search index is a file on your PC. Nothing. Recognize people by voice Nothing, once the speaker model is downloaded. Nothing. Export (Markdown, PDF, Word, email file, captions, audio) Nothing. Files are made on your PC. Nothing. Test button on a provider A 2-second test clip (speech) or a short test phrase (language model) goes to that provider. Nothing. Webhooks Only the parts of a note you ticked go to the address you saved. n/a The connector for AI apps Notes and action items you search for go to the AI app you connected, on this PC. What that app does with them is up to that app and its service. n/a Updates A request for the list of builds, then the update file. Unless you turn it off in Settings › Privacy, the request also carries the anonymous count: a random ID, the version, the channel, your Windows version and your country. n/a Notes trial and license When you open Notes, press Try Notes free or buy, a code made from your PC (a one-way hash of its Windows machine ID; the ID itself never leaves) so the 30 days survive a reinstall and a purchase can unlock this PC by itself. Your email only if you ask for the 14 extra days. One number, the version of the recording-consent notice you saw, goes with the trial start and the next check (see Recording consent ). A purchase goes through Stripe's checkout in your browser; A9 Voice and a9voice.com never see card details. An activated key is checked with a9voice.com about once a week. Nothing you said, wrote or recorded. Transcribe never asks. Notes needs this to run. A few details that matter: Fallback. If the service you use for dictation fails or is slow, A9 Voice sends the same audio to your fallback service. If you do not want audio to reach a second company, set Use as fallback to a model on this PC, or to none. Summaries try more than one model. Summaries, Ask and Deep answers try the model you chose first and, if it fails or is rate limited, the next language model you have set up. If you want text to go to only one place, set up only one language model. OpenRouter is a routing service: your text goes to OpenRouter, which passes it to the model you picked. The same is true of any custom server you point at a remote service. A first Deepgram key asks before meeting audio goes there. When you save your first Deepgram key while Meeting notes use a model that can't tell speakers apart, the key window shows Also use Deepgram for Meeting notes , checked. Meeting audio goes to Deepgram only if you leave it checked. Unchecked, the key is saved and Meeting notes stay where they were. The setup step asks the same way and moves nothing until you click Continue . Deepgram live. With a Deepgram key saved, both sides of the call stream to Deepgram live only while the Live window is open (and for a minute after you close it), and only when Deepgram writes your notes or you chose Use Deepgram for the live transcript . With another engine writing the notes and no choice made, nothing goes to Deepgram. To stop it altogether, set Live transcript to Off , or disconnect the Deepgram key. Keeping the dictation connection ready. While A9 Voice runs and a cloud service is set for dictation, it sends that service a small request every few minutes, so the next dictation starts without delay. The request carries your key and no audio or text. With a model on this PC set for dictation, there is no such request. Dictation uses the clipboard briefly. It puts the text on the clipboard to paste it, keeps it out of Windows clipboard history and the cloud clipboard, and puts back what you had copied. When you ask for a copy yourself (tray Copy last transcription ), that copy is allowed into clipboard history.

What each service receives The services A9 Voice can call are the ones in Settings › Models and Settings › Models . Each one only receives data when you set up its key (or address) and use it. Speech: Groq, Deepgram, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, and any server you add with Add custom API . Language models: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Google, and any server you add with Add custom API . Each service's own terms say what it does with data it receives, and you pay it directly. A9 Voice has no copy of what you send. Where a service's terms say something you would want to know before pasting a key (DeepSeek processes requests on servers in China; Google's free tier and Mistral's free plan may use requests for training or to improve their products; AssemblyAI may train on requests unless a paid account opts out), the window and the tile say so in one line.

Keeping everything on this PC To see the choice between a cloud service and a model on your PC: You can use A9 Voice with no cloud service at all: In Settings › Models , download a model under On this PC (Parakeet V2 for English, or a multilingual model). Under What each job uses , click Change on Dictation and Meeting notes and pick it. Set Fallback for dictation to another model on this PC, or none. In the same page, Disconnect any cloud speech keys you no longer want. With no key saved, nothing can be sent there. For summaries, Enhance and Ask, run a language-model server on your own PC and add it in Settings › Models with Add custom API . The page shows http://localhost:11434/v1 as an example address. Under What each job uses , click Change on Summaries and pick it; Ask and Enhance follow it. Disconnect any cloud language models, because summaries fall back to them. Leave Settings › Integrations empty, and leave Connector for AI apps off if you do not want notes to reach another app. For Live transcript , use a speech model on this PC that keeps up (its window says whether it does), or turn Live transcript off. What still uses the network in this setup: The update check. A9 Voice checks a9voice.com and the project's release files on GitHub a few seconds after it starts and then every 6 hours. There is no switch to turn the check off; the anonymous count that rides on it has one ( Settings › Privacy ), and with it off the check sends nothing extra. If the PC is offline the check simply fails and tries again later. The Notes trial and license. Notes asks a9voice.com about its trial or key when you open it, press Try Notes free or buy (while you finish paying it asks every few seconds, for up to 15 minutes, whether the payment has gone through), a few seconds after A9 Voice starts and then about once a day while it runs (on the update check's timer), and when a recording starts and the last answer is a day old. A refunded or revoked key stops working within a day of the next check. When it can't reach a9voice.com it holds for 14 days (a trial) or 30 days (a key). Nothing waits for it: a recording in progress is never cut. Transcribe never does. Downloads you start. Speech models come from Hugging Face. Graphics-card support (about 25 MB, once) comes from files.pythonhosted.org. The speaker model for voice recognition comes from the project's release page on GitHub. All are fixed to one version and checked against a known checksum before use. After they are downloaded you can work with no internet at all. Web pages you open. The Get your key buttons open the provider's own page in your browser. That is your browser, not A9 Voice.

Problem reports Report a problem sends one report when you press Send : what you typed, an optional email address for the reply, and (if you leave Include diagnostics on) the text that Show what's sent displays. That text is Copy diagnostics with the names of people, note titles, recent dictations, email addresses, the Windows user folder and the microphone's name taken out, plus a summary of switches and engine names. It goes to a9voice.com (or its mirror) and is mailed to support@a9voice.com . See Reporting a problem and Problem reports .

Anonymous usage counts A9 Voice sends no crash reports and no content-based analytics. The one thing it counts is installs and how far they get: with the update check it sends a random ID, the app version, the channel, your Windows version and processor type, and a9voice.com adds the country; and once each, with the same fields, a message when you finish setup, make your first dictation, record your first note, start the Notes trial and buy Notes. Installers downloaded from a9voice.com carry a random code in the file name. The app sends it once with the first-launch count so we know which link the download came from. It isn't tied to you. If you ask us to email you the download link from your phone, we send that one email and don't keep your address. It is on by default and has a switch in Settings › Privacy . With it off, nothing extra is sent and nothing is recorded. The page Anonymous usage counts says exactly what is counted and what never is. The only network calls are to the speech and language services you set up, to the update locations above, to a9voice.com for the Notes trial and license (see the table), to the download locations above, and to webhook addresses you add.

Where your files live To see the folders and what Export offers: What Where Settings, history, notes database, search index, voice database %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice (the folder is named after the app's identifier): settings.json , history.db , notes.db , search.db , meaning.db (the numbers search by meaning makes of your notes, if you turned it on), voices.db , ask-recent.json (your last 50 Ask questions and their answers) and window.json (the main window's size and place) Template logos %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice\templates Logs %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice\logs , the current one a9voice.log ( Open logs folder in Settings › General › About) Notes (summary, transcript, images) Documents\A9 Voice\Notes , or the folder you pick in Settings › Storage Audio (dictation and meetings) Documents\A9 Voice\Audio , or the folder you pick in Settings › Dictation audio . Dictation audio is in Transcribe , meeting audio in Notes Speech models, the search-by-meaning model and graphics-card support %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice\models (the search model is in its search folder) API keys, webhook addresses and secrets Windows Credential Manager, under names that start with ai.atlas9.a9voice/ A copy of a recording is also kept briefly while it is being recorded and written up, in a temporary notes-spool folder in the app's data folder. It is removed afterwards. Settings, the databases and the logs stay in the app's data folder on purpose: Documents may be synced by a cloud-storage service you use, and a synced database file can be damaged. The notes and audio folders are in Documents by default, so if your Documents folder is synced, they are too. That is your choice of folder, not something A9 Voice does. If a hard crash damages the settings file or a database, A9 Voice keeps the damaged file beside the new one and tells you with a notice in the pill. Settings come back from the last good copy (or start from the defaults if there is none); a damaged history or notes database is rebuilt with the rows that could be read.

Your keys API keys are stored in Windows Credential Manager as generic credentials, on this PC. A9 Voice never writes them to settings.json , the logs, the exported settings zip or the app's own storage. The windows in the app only ever learn whether a key is set. Webhook addresses are stored the same way, because many contain a secret. Disconnect on a provider removes its key. Copy diagnostics removes anything that looks like a key before it copies the last 200 log lines.

What the logs hold The log files record timings, lengths ("90 characters"), status codes, provider and model names, and the name of the app a dictation went into. They never hold API keys or what you said. The files are kept to about 2 MB each, with a few older ones; the oldest are removed. One more file is local and worth knowing about: meeting-titles.jsonl in the logs folder. When Name notes after the meeting is on (or logging), A9 Voice reads the call app's window titles for the first 90 seconds of a call to find the meeting's name. This file keeps the titles it saw and the name it chose, for the last 200 calls, so you can check a wrong pick. It stays on your PC.

Voiceprints Speakers on this PC (the Live window's free speaker separation, see Speakers on this PC ) makes voice fingerprints of the other people's side of a call, in memory, while it records. When the recording stops, each note keeps who talked when and one set of numbers per speaker in notes.db : no audio, and not in the note's folder, exports, webhooks or the connector. Deleting the note deletes them. They are matched against saved voices only when Recognize people by voice is on. Recognize people by voice is off until you turn it on, after an explainer. When on, A9 Voice keeps a voiceprint for a person you tag in the Live window or name in a note: numbers that describe how they sound, not a recording. Voiceprints: are stored only in voices.db in the app's data folder, and the database is set up to overwrite deleted data; are never in your notes and never sent anywhere, including to the speech and language services, webhooks and the connector; are learned only from names you give, never from a guess; are deleted for good with Forget (one person) or Delete all voices in Settings › Voices . Turning the feature on downloads the speaker model once. See Voices .

How long things are kept What How long Dictation history The last 1,000 dictations, or the number you choose in Settings › General › History kept . Clear all in the Transcribe history deletes the rest. Home counts Daily totals of words, dictations and speaking time, with no text. History kept and Clear all leave them; Settings › General › Reset counts empties them. They never leave your PC. Dictation audio Saved by default and kept 7 days, or the time you choose in Keep dictation audio . Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it. Notes Until you delete the note. Notes audio 30 days, or the time you choose in Keep notes audio . Only the audio goes; the summary, transcript and images stay. Audio of a note that failed is kept. Voiceprints Until you forget them. The Voices page can show people not recognized in 60 days or more. Logs A few files of about 2 MB. Problem reports 180 days on our server. One that could not be sent is kept on your PC for up to 14 days, then dropped. Meeting-title log The last 200 calls.

Exporting and importing your setup Export… in Settings › Account writes a zip with your settings, Dictionary, templates (with logos) and tag names. It does not contain API keys, webhook addresses or secrets, your license, this PC's install ID, your history or any audio. Two checkboxes add more, and you choose them each time: Include my notes (on by default) adds your notes' summaries, transcripts and images and their details, never audio; Include learned voices (off by default) adds the voiceprints themselves, so keep that file private. The settings do contain folder paths, custom server addresses and your profile, so treat the file as personal. Import… reads such a zip and keeps what belongs to this PC (devices, folders, window places, setup and update state, and the voice-recognition switch). Keys are not carried over; add them again on the new PC. Notes are merged into the ones already there and nothing is deleted. To bring back notes without an export, see Moving your notes to a new PC .

The connector and webhooks Both let something outside A9 Voice receive your notes, and both are off until you set them up. The connector for AI apps lets an AI app on this PC search and read your notes. It is read only. It can see titles, summaries, transcripts, typed notes, image captions and action items (and your dictation history if Search dictations too is on). It never gets audio, images or voiceprints. Each request is logged on the Connectors page. See Connector for AI apps . Webhooks send a note to an address you add, when it is ready. The receiver gets exactly the parts you ticked, nothing else. Audio, image files and voiceprints are never sent. Whoever can read that service can read what you send, so add only places you trust. See Webhooks .

Recording consent You are responsible for getting the consent the law requires before you record other people. Some places, including several US states, require everyone's consent, not just yours. What applies depends on where you and the other people are, so check the rules that cover you. This page can't tell you what they are. A9 Voice records what your microphone hears and what your computer plays. No bot joins the call and the app does not announce itself, so A9 Voice tells nobody on the call. Telling them is up to you.

The notice When Notes starts, A9 Voice shows one sentence and a Learn more link to this section: By starting Notes, you agree to get any consent the law requires before you record other people. Some places, including several US states, require everyone's consent. Where. Under Try Notes free on the Notes page, and under Start trial on the "Want notes for this call?" card. Pressing the button is the agreement. There is no checkbox. If Notes started without it. A trial that A9 Voice started for you when you updated, or a license you already had, never showed the notice. A small card with the same sentence appears once on the Notes page and the first time the recording bar appears. Got it closes it. Always there. Settings › Notes › Recording shows the same sentence and link as plain text. It never stops a recording. The notice doesn't block, delay or interrupt anything. Telling the people you record, and getting their consent, is up to you.

What is recorded about it On your PC: the time you accepted and the version number of the notice, in the settings file. An exported settings file doesn't contain it. With a9voice.com: one number, the notice's version ( consent_v ). It goes with the Notes trial start, and with the next trial or license check if you pressed Got it later, so it needs no extra request. a9voice.com stores it with the time it arrived. It carries no name, email or content, and a9voice.com never sends it back. Transcribe never sends it.

Delete your data Pick what you want gone. Everything below is on your PC only. Dictation history: open Transcribe and use Clear all , or delete single dictations. Set Save audio recordings off in Settings › Dictation audio to stop keeping new audio. Notes: in Notes , open the ⋯ menu of a note and choose Delete… , then Delete audio, files and note . Voiceprints: Settings › Voices › Delete all voices . Keys: Disconnect on each provider in Speech models and Language models. This removes the key from Credential Manager. Webhooks: Delete… on each one in Integrations removes its address and secrets. Models: open a model under On this PC and choose Delete . Everything else: uninstall A9 Voice in Windows Settings › Apps . To also remove the files it leaves, delete the app's data folder, %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice , the models folder in %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice , and your notes and audio folders in Documents\A9 Voice . Then open Windows Credential Manager , choose Windows Credentials , and remove any entries whose names start with ai.atlas9.a9voice/ . If you used a version before 1.0.4, there is an older copy of the same things to remove too: A9 Voice copied your data to its own folder on the first start of 1.0.4 and left the originals where they were, so the previous version still works if you go back. They are the other folder in %APPDATA% that holds the same files (its name starts with com. ; the one to keep is ai.atlas9.a9voice ), the matching folder in %LOCALAPPDATA% , and the Credential Manager entries whose names start with that older folder's name and a / .

What A9 Voice counts, what it is, what never leaves your PC, and how to turn it off or reset it. A9 Voice counts installs so we know whether anyone is using it, which version they are on, and whether people get through setup and use it. The count is anonymous: there is no account to tie it to, and it carries nothing you said, wrote or recorded. It is on by default and you can turn it off in Settings › Privacy .

What is counted When A9 Voice checks for an update, the request to a9voice.com carries a random ID, the app version, your update channel (Stable or Dev), your Windows version (for example "Windows 11, build 26200") and your PC's processor type. a9voice.com adds your country, worked out from the request. The ID is a random number made on your PC the first time A9 Voice ran. It is not made from your name, your PC or your account, and it cannot be turned back into any of them. A brand-new install also sends one extra message the first time it starts, so we can tell a real install from a download that was never opened. Installers downloaded from a9voice.com carry a random code in the file name. The app sends it once with the first-launch count so we know which link the download came from. It isn't tied to you. If you installed A9 Voice from the Microsoft Store, that same first message says so ("store"), so we can count Store installs; it carries nothing else. A Store copy that runs as a Microsoft Store package sends none of these counts: the Store counts its installs and updates it. Five more messages are sent once each, with the same ID and the same fields and nothing else: when you finish setup with a way to transcribe that works, when you make your first dictation, when you record your first note, when you start the Notes trial and when you buy Notes (a complimentary key sends nothing). They tell us whether people get through setup and use the app: never what you said or recorded. An install that was already past one of these steps when it updated to the version that counts it does not send it, and with the switch off none of them is sent. We do not store your IP address, and the website sets no cookies. The site counts three things so we can see which places bring people: a visit (one anonymous message per browser tab, with the website the visitor came from, the first page and the kind of device, such as Windows or phone), a view of the download page, and a click on its download button, each with the link it came from (a post, a profile, a listing) and the button that was used. Nothing is kept on your device beyond that tab's memory, and nothing identifies you. On a phone, the download button says Send it to my PC : when you email, share or copy the link, that counts one more message with the same link and button fields, and a view of the download page counts once each time it loads in a browser. If you ask us to email you the download link from your phone, we send that one email and don't keep your address. To stop abuse we keep a one-way fingerprint of that address and of your IP address for 24 hours, then delete it; the address itself is never stored. The pages themselves are also counted by Cloudflare's cookieless Web Analytics: page views and where visitors came from, with no cookie and no profile of you.

h: The Notes trial and license are separate
t: The Notes trial and license are separate The count above has a switch. The Notes trial and license checks do not, because Notes cannot tell whether your 30 days are used up without asking. They are not part of the usage count and use a different request to a9voice.com. The count only learns, once each, that a trial started or a license was bought, and that message follows the switch. Your PC's code. When you open Notes, A9 Voice sends a code made from your PC, so a reinstall finds the trial you already have; nothing is stored until you press Try Notes free , which starts the 30 days, and the code is kept with them. If you buy, the same code is what lets this PC unlock itself once the payment goes through; it never carries your key to anyone else. The code is a one-way hash of the Windows machine ID with a fixed value mixed in. The machine ID itself never leaves your PC, and the code cannot be turned back into it or into you. It is what lets a reinstall on the same PC keep the same 30 days. Dictating with Transcribe never sends it. Your email, only if you ask for 14 more days. We keep it with that PC's code, to send you the 6-digit code and to answer you. Product updates only if you tick the box. A purchase. Checkout is Stripe's page in your browser. A9 Voice and a9voice.com never see your card. We keep the order record (email, amount, date), your key and which PCs use it. A license key is checked with a9voice.com about once a day. The recording-consent notice's version. When Notes starts, A9 Voice shows a short notice about getting consent before you record other people (see Recording consent ). The Notes trial start, and the next trial or license check if you pressed Got it later, carries one flag with it: consent_v , the version number of that notice, such as 1. a9voice.com stores the number with the time it arrived, on the same trial or license record. It is a number and nothing else: no name, no email, no content. It rides on a check A9 Voice already makes, never as a request of its own, and it is never sent back to the app. What never goes with it. Audio, text, names, notes, file names, your keys and your settings.

Problem reports are separate Report a problem (the About card at the bottom of Settings › General , or the tray menu under Help ) is not part of the count and has no switch, because it does nothing until you press Send . A report holds what you typed in the two boxes, the email address if you gave one, and, if you leave Include diagnostics on, the text under Show what's sent : the version, update channel, Windows version, the type of microphone, a summary of switches and engine names, display and graphics-card details, and the last 200 lines of the log. Keys, the Windows user folder, people's names, note titles, recent dictations and email addresses are taken out first, and it never holds audio, transcripts, summaries, voiceprints or file paths under your profile. The report also carries a code made from your PC (the same one-way hash the Notes trial uses) that only limits reports to five a day. It goes to a9voice.com (or its mirror a9voice.atlas9.ai when a network blocks the first), is stored with a report ID, and is mailed to support@a9voice.com . We use it to find and fix the problem and to reply if you gave an address. Reports are deleted after 180 days. A report that could not be sent stays in the app's data folder, in reports-pending.json , and is sent at the next update check for up to 14 days; delete the file to discard it.

What never leaves your PC Audio, dictated or transcribed text, notes, names, voiceprints, file names and paths, your API keys and your settings never go with the count. (A problem report you choose to send is a different thing; see above.) Audio and text go only to the speech and language services you set up yourself; see Privacy and data for every place.

Turn it off Open Settings › Privacy . Switch Send anonymous usage counts off. With the switch off, the update check sends no ID and nothing about your PC, and neither the first-start message (with its download code, which is then deleted) nor the five milestones are sent. a9voice.com records nothing at all for those requests. Updates work the same. The switch is for the app. It does not affect what the website counts about a visit to a9voice.com, which has no ID and no cookie. If your network blocks a9voice.com, A9 Voice sends the same requests (the update check, the Notes trial and license checks, the counts when the switch is on) to a9voice.atlas9.ai, a mirror of the same server, and remembers which one answered. It sends nothing more and nothing different.

Reset the ID Reset ID in Settings › Privacy makes a new random ID. The old one is forgotten on this PC, and nothing links the old and the new. An exported settings file never contains the ID or the milestones, so importing it on another PC does not copy them.

Every key A9 Voice uses, what each does, its default, and where you can change it. A9 Voice has two kinds of keys. Global keys work from any app, even when A9 Voice's window is closed: dictating, recording a meeting, showing the recording bar. You can change these. Window keys work only while an A9 Voice window is in front: searching, playing a note, moving around a list. These are fixed. Keys are shown as Ctrl+Space , which means hold Ctrl and press Space .

Dictation All of these are set in Settings › Dictation . See Transcribe for what they do. While you choose a key When you click one of the key boxes in Settings , it says Press keys… . Press the combination you want. Esc cancels without changing anything. Backspace or Delete clears the key, for the boxes that can be cleared. They show Not set afterwards. A key needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win in it, so ordinary typing is never caught. F13 to F24 are allowed alone. Ctrl + Alt + R is reserved and cannot be chosen. Two of A9 Voice's keys cannot be the same: the second box shows Same key as and the other key's name, for example Same key as dictation or Same key as paste last transcription . If another program already uses the combination, the box shows "… is in use by another app. Quit that app or choose another key."

Other keys inside the app Enter in the Dictionary page's Add a word or name box adds the word. Esc closes the speech-model windows, the search window and the Tidy folder names window. You can also dictate into A9 Voice's own text boxes: click in the box, then hold the dictation key. See Transcribe .

If something goes wrong A key does nothing. Another program may own it. Look for Key in use · fix in the sidebar, or the message at the top of Settings › Dictation , and choose another combination. A key stopped working after you chose Pause dictation. Pause dictation in the tray menu switches the dictation keys off. Choose it again to switch them back on. Ctrl + K does not open search. The A9 Voice window must be in front, and setup must be finished. See Troubleshooting for more.

Fixes for the things that go wrong most often, how to copy the diagnostics that help someone find the cause, and short answers to common questions. Find the symptom, read the cause, try the fix. Each entry links to the page with the full story. If none of them helps, report the problem from inside the app .
Dictation

h: I hear no tone when I start dictating
t: I hear no tone when I start dictating The start tone is a soft two-note sound that plays about a quarter of a second after you press the dictation key, so a quick tap stays silent. Check the switch. Open Settings › Microphone . Sounds must be on, and Volume must not be at the bottom. Sleepy or Bluetooth outputs. A USB or Bluetooth headset that has gone to sleep used to swallow the tone. A9 Voice now wakes the output when you press the key. If you run an older version, update . In a call. During a call, or with a headset whose microphone is in call mode, the tone plays on the headset's call audio and can come a moment late. Every tone is written to the log with where it played, so Copy diagnostics shows whether it was sent. More: Transcribe .

The pill says "Mic muted" The microphone is muted in Windows or in your call app (for example Teams), so A9 Voice heard only silence. Unmute it and try again. If another microphone is available and not muted, the pill offers a button, Use followed by that microphone's name and for dictation ; press it to switch. Clicking the pill opens Settings › Microphone . To keep dictating while your headset is muted in a call, pick a second microphone for Dictation microphone in Settings › Dictation .

The pill says "Didn't catch that" A9 Voice heard no speech. Open Settings › Microphone , press Test and say a few words: the bar should move when you talk. Check that the right microphone is picked and not muted, hold the key a little longer, and speak after the tone. Make sure Language you speak (in Settings › Models , and on the Dictation page) matches what you speak.

h: "Ctrl+Space is in use by another app"
t: "Ctrl+Space is in use by another app" Another program has the same shortcut, often another dictation tool. A9 Voice shows Key in use · fix in the sidebar until it is solved, and A9 Voice cannot use that key meanwhile. Quit the other program, or open Settings › Dictation and press the Dictation key box to choose a different shortcut. The same applies to the hands-free key and the other keys: the page shows the conflict under the key. More: Keyboard shortcuts .

h: Nothing is pasted, or "copied instead" appears
t: Nothing is pasted, or "copied instead" appears When A9 Voice cannot put text where you are typing, it copies the text to the clipboard so you can paste it yourself with Ctrl + V , and the pill says why: "Can't type into an admin window — copied instead". Windows does not let a normal app type into a program running as administrator. Paste with Ctrl + V . "Paste was blocked — copied instead" or "Typing was blocked — copied instead". The app ignores pasted or typed input. Try the other How text goes in setting in Settings › Dictation , or set Paste keys to Shift+Insert under Show advanced , which some terminals and remote desktops prefer. "The clipboard was busy — try again". Another program was holding the clipboard. Dictate again. "Copied — click a text box in A9 Voice first". You dictated while an A9 Voice window without a text box was in front. Click a text box first. You can also put the last result in again with Alt + Shift + V , or use Copy last transcription in the tray menu. More: Transcribe .

h: The pill shows an amber error
t: The pill shows an amber error Press Fix in the pill: it opens the page where the problem is. The message names the service and the problem: "Groq key missing" or "Groq key rejected" (or the name of whichever service you use). The key is not saved or the service refused it. Open the service in Settings › Models , paste a fresh key and press Test . "Groq rate limit hit". You sent too many requests, or your plan's limit was reached. Wait a moment, or use another service as the fallback . "Groq timed out" or "Groq error 503" (an error followed by a number). The service is slow or down. If a fallback is set, A9 Voice already tried it once. "Your network is blocking Groq (api.groq.com)". Your network answered in the service's place, usually a work network's security gateway, so the problem is not your key or the service. A fallback is tried once; a model on this PC works without the internet. See Work networks . "No internet". A9 Voice could not reach the service. If you have downloaded a model on this PC, it answers automatically, and the pill adds offline to the result. "Groq sent a bad reply" or "Groq couldn't run". The service gave something A9 Voice could not read. Try again; if it repeats, copy the diagnostics. "Pick how A9 Voice hears you first". No speech service or model is set up yet. Open Settings › Models . "Timed out after 15 s. Nothing was pasted". A dictation took longer than 15 seconds. Check your connection and try again. "The microphone stopped". The microphone disappeared while you spoke. Re-plug it and check Settings › Microphone . After a successful dictation the pill may add via Deepgram (or another name): that means your fallback answered because the first service failed. Details: Speech models .
Meetings and notes

h: The recording bar or the pill is gone
t: The recording bar or the pill is gone The recording bar is a small window that stays above other windows. If you cannot see it: Press Ctrl + Alt + B . This is Show recording bar in Settings › Recording . It brings the bar back from wherever it is, including from Small, the minimized bar; pressing it again shrinks the bar to Small, in place. Click the A9 Voice tray icon . While a recording is on it switches between the bar and Small. The tray menu also has Show recording bar . Right-click the tray icon and choose Reset bar position to put the bar back at its default place on this monitor setup. An undocked Live window goes back under the bar. Every button in the Live window also brings the bar back. If the dictation pill looks cut off or the wrong size, copy the diagnostics : they include the display details that help. More: Recording a meeting .

h: A call did not start recording
t: A call did not start recording Check these in order: Is the app on? Open Settings › Recording . Only Microsoft Teams and Zoho Cliq and Zoho Meeting are on in a new install. Turn on Zoom , Webex , Slack huddles , Discord , or Browser calls for calls in a web browser, or add another app under Other app . Is the app using the microphone? A9 Voice starts when the app starts using your microphone, and stops when the app lets go of it. Open Settings › Recording and press Run check under Detection check while the call is on: it lists each app holding a microphone, which microphone, and whether A9 Voice counts it as a meeting. If your call app is missing from the list, it isn't holding a microphone yet. Copy the check into a report if it should be. Is another recording app capturing the call? With Wait while another recording app runs on, A9 Voice holds back only while another recording app is really capturing the call. The bar says, for example, "Teams call detected: not recording" and "Another recording app is capturing it", and offers Record now . Press it to record anyway, or turn the setting off. You can always start a recording yourself with the Record button, Ctrl + Alt + N or Start recording in the tray menu. More: Recording a meeting .

h: Show in folder opens the wrong place
t: Show in folder opens the wrong place Older versions could open Documents instead of the note's folder or file. This is fixed; update to the latest build. If it still opens the wrong place, copy the diagnostics and report it.

h: I named a speaker wrong in the Live window
t: I named a speaker wrong in the Live window Every naming action in the Live window can be undone for 10 seconds with Undo in the small bar that appears. Nothing is learned during a call, so Undo leaves no trace. To fix a name later, click it in the transcript and choose whether the fix is for that line or for everything that speaker said. If the name is already used, A9 Voice asks "Same person?" and can merge the two speakers. After the call you can rename speakers on the note page. More: Live window and Note page .

h: A note is stuck on "Transcribing…" or says it failed
t: A note is stuck on "Transcribing…" or says it failed Wait for it to finish. A long meeting takes a while to write up. The note shows its stage: transcribing, then "Writing the summary…". After a crash or a restart, A9 Voice finishes any note that was left unfinished the next time it starts. Open A9 Voice and give it a minute. If the note says it failed, read the message on the note, then press Try again (this needs the audio, which is kept for a failed note). If a service rejected your key, fix it in Settings › Models first. If it says "Your network is blocking Deepgram (api.deepgram.com). The recording is saved." see Work networks : the note is not lost, and a model on this PC can transcribe it. If the transcript is fine but there is no summary, add a key in Settings › Models , then press Regenerate summary in the right-hand column of the note. You can also choose another speech model and press Regenerate transcript . More: Note page .

h: Speech models and the graphics card
t: Speech models and the graphics card

A model will not download Model files come from Hugging Face and are checked before use. Messages you may see: "The download was cut short; try again". The connection dropped. Press Download again: it picks up where it stopped. "A downloaded file was damaged; try again". The checksum did not match, so the file was thrown away. Try again. "The download server answered …". The server refused or could not find the file. Try later. Also check the free space: the model window shows how much is free on the drive. If the download keeps failing, press Discard partial download and start again. A firewall, proxy or security tool that blocks huggingface.co will stop downloads. More: Speech models .

h: The graphics card is not used
t: The graphics card is not used Open Settings › Models and read the Use graphics card row. It tells you why: "No supported graphics card found. Whisper models run on the processor." The PC has no DirectX 12 card that can run models. That is fine: everything works on the processor. "The driver is too old for DirectX 12. Update the graphics driver." Update the driver from your card's maker or Windows Update. The switch is off. Turn Use graphics card on. A model tile says "Needs Use graphics card" in that case. The graphics-card support is not downloaded. Press Download on the Graphics-card support row. It is a one-time download of about 25 MB. "Needs … of graphics memory". The model needs more memory than the card has. The model window names a smaller model to use. The PC has two cards. A Graphics card row lets you pick which one runs models.

"Graphics card unavailable, used the processor" The card had a problem while a model was running, so A9 Voice finished the job on the processor and told you once. Nothing was lost. To try the card again, turn Use graphics card off and on. If it keeps happening, copy the diagnostics: they list the card, the driver and the last failure.
Settings and files

h: A notice says my settings or a database was damaged
t: A notice says my settings or a database was damaged A hard crash or power cut can damage a file. At the next start A9 Voice keeps the damaged file beside the new one and shows a notice in the pill: "Settings were damaged; restored the last good copy". Your settings came back from the previous good version. You might lose the very last change. "Settings were damaged and reset; the old file is kept beside them". There was no good copy, so settings started from the defaults. Your keys are safe, because they are not in that file. "History was damaged. Rebuilt it and kept what could be read; the old file is saved beside it" (or Notes ). The rows that could be read were copied back. The damaged files are in %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice with a name ending in .bad- or .damaged- and a number. You can send them with a report if you want them looked at; they hold your data, so do not post them in public.

h: "A9 Voice couldn't finish moving your settings"
t: "A9 Voice couldn't finish moving your settings" The first time 1.0.4 or later starts, A9 Voice copies your settings, history, notes, voices, recordings that were still waiting to be processed and API keys to its own folder and Credential Manager names (they used to carry the name of an earlier version). If a step can't finish, this notice says so. Nothing was deleted , the originals are still where they were, and A9 Voice tries again the next time it starts; until then it runs on what was copied. If it shows again after a restart, the log says why: open Settings › General › Open logs folder and look in a9voice.log for lines with "migration incomplete". The usual causes are a full disk (the copy needs room for a second set of your data) and a file another program has open. Free some space or close that program and restart A9 Voice. If it can't be fixed, copy your diagnostics into a report. The logs folder is now %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9voice\logs and its current log is a9voice.log . Logs from before the move are copied there and keep their old names.

h: The window looks wrong, cut off or too small
t: The window looks wrong, cut off or too small The main window needs at least 960 × 640 (more when Windows' Text size is above 100%: the window's smallest size grows with it, up to the screen). The sidebar starts open at any width. If you shrank it to icons with Shrink sidebar at the bottom, the same button ( Keep the sidebar open ) brings the names back; A9 Voice remembers your choice. If Windows' text size is above 100%, see the next entry . Copy the diagnostics and attach them to a report: they include your monitors, scaling, Windows text size, the WebView version and the size the pill and recording bar were given.

h: Larger Windows text size, or a cut-off pill
t: Larger Windows text size, or a cut-off pill Windows has a setting that makes text bigger everywhere: Settings › Accessibility › Text size . A9 Voice follows it: the pill, the recording bar, the Live window and the main window all draw larger and their windows grow to fit. From 0.7.12 nothing is cut off at any Text size. If the pill or the recording bar still looks cut off, copy the diagnostics : the lines for the pill and the recording bar show the scale the page draws at, your monitor's scale and the Text size, and end with MISMATCH when a window is smaller than what it shows. To keep Windows' Text size for other apps but not for A9 Voice, set Settings › General › Interface size to 100% . 125% and 150% make A9 Voice larger than Windows' own setting does. Follow Windows is the default. An older version (before 0.7.12) cut off the pill and mis-sized the recording bar at a Text size above 100%. Updating fixes it; setting Text size back to 100% was the only workaround.
Updates

An update did not finish You pressed Restart to update , or A9 Voice restarted itself, and afterwards the version is still the old one. When it starts, A9 Voice says "The update to X didn't finish. A9 Voice will try again when you're not dictating or recording." and tries once more by itself, once for each time it starts. After two failures of the same version in one day, A9 Voice stops trying by itself until tomorrow and shows "The update didn't install. You can try again now or install it from the download page." Press Try again , or open the Download page and install by hand. If it keeps failing, restart the PC and open A9 Voice again; it picks the update up on its own. A9 Voice does not stay closed when an update is interrupted: it starts again within a couple of minutes (see If an update is interrupted ). The installer adds each run to installer.log in the logs folder ( Settings › General › About › Open logs folder ), with a header line per run ( === Setup 1.0.11 started … ) and how it ended; the last 200 KB or so is kept. A9 Voice's own log, a9voice.log ( scribe.log before 1.0.4), has lines starting "update hand-off", "installer started in … ms" and "relaunch guard". Copy them into a report with the diagnostics . See Updates and channels .

h: A9 Voice was closed after a restart that did not finish
t: A9 Voice was closed after a restart that did not finish You pressed Restart, Windows closed your apps, and then the restart did not complete (a dialog, a stuck update, a cancel). Apps that were running should come back on their own. A9 Voice now does: when Windows closes it for a restart or shutdown, it sets a one-time reminder in your Windows Task Scheduler for two minutes later. If the PC really restarts, Start with Windows opens A9 Voice at sign-in and removes the reminder. If the restart was called off or never finished, the reminder opens A9 Voice again in the tray, with no window. If Start with Windows is off, a restart that was called off still brings it back, because it was running; a restart that happens does not open it. Windows' own "restart apps" path, which installers use, also starts it again. Quitting from the tray menu is your decision: nothing brings A9 Voice back until you open it or sign in again. A recording that was running when Windows closed A9 Voice is kept: the audio is saved and the next start finishes the note. The log ( a9voice.log , Settings › General › About › Open logs folder ) now has a line for every way A9 Voice ends: exit: quit by the user , exit: Windows is ending the session (…) with whether the reminder was set and whether a recording was saved, or panic: with the place in the code. The next start says how it began: started: --autostart (sign-in) , (relaunch guard) , (restart manager) , or started: by hand . Include these lines in a report .

h: "Restart your PC to finish the update"
t: "Restart your PC to finish the update" The installer waited for the running A9 Voice to close, tried to end it twice, and it still would not go. Nothing was replaced, so the version you have keeps working, and the installer starts A9 Voice again before it stops. Restart the PC; the update installs by itself the next time A9 Voice starts.
Work networks

h: Activation, updates or the Live transcript don't work at work
t: Activation, updates or the Live transcript don't work at work Some company networks block a9voice.com because it is a new domain, or re-sign HTTPS traffic with their own certificate. A9 Voice copes with both: a9voice.com is blocked. Activating a license, the Notes trial and the update check then use a9voice.atlas9.ai , a copy of the same server, by themselves, and remember which one worked. If you see "Couldn't reach a9voice.com or a9voice.atlas9.ai", the network blocks both: ask your IT team to allow them, or activate from another network. A note says "Your network is blocking Deepgram (api.deepgram.com). The recording is saved." A work network (a firewall, proxy or security gateway) answered in the speech service's place, so nothing is wrong with your key or the service, and the recording is safe. A9 Voice tells this from the service's own errors, which keep their own words (a rejected key, no credit, the service being down). What happens next depends on whether a speech model is installed on this PC: With a model on this PC, the note is transcribed there by itself and says Transcribed on this PC because your network blocks Deepgram. Transcribe with Deepgram runs it through the service again, for when you are on another network. Without one, the note offers Download the on-PC model (with its size) and tries the service again by itself when your network changes (another Wi-Fi, a VPN switched), and every 15 minutes for 24 hours. The message goes away when it works. Try again tries at once. After two blocked notes, Settings › Models offers once to use the on-PC engine for Meeting notes on that network. Nothing changes until you click. A9 Voice never sends your audio around a block; ask your IT team to allow the address if you want the cloud service. The Live window says the network is blocking the service. The Live transcript connection was blocked the same way. The recording goes on and the full transcript with speakers is made when you stop. With a speech model installed on this PC, the Live transcript switches to it within a few seconds and says Live transcript on this PC (your network blocks Deepgram) . Otherwise A9 Voice keeps retrying, and the line goes away when it connects. The Live window says "Live transcript can't connect from this network". The recording is fine and the full transcript with speakers is made when you stop. A9 Voice keeps retrying, and the line goes away when it connects. With a speech model installed on this PC, the Live transcript switches to it and says so. A network that only lets traffic out through a proxy server can still block the live connection; Windows' proxy is not used for it. More: Live window and Privacy and data .
Getting help

h: Open the manual from the app
t: Open the manual from the app Every page of A9 Voice has a small ? button at the top right, beside the model chips. It opens this manual in your browser at the page that explains the screen you are on, for example the Speech models page opens Speech models . The Live window has the same ? button in its header. The Manual button in the sidebar, and Help › Manual in the tray menu, open the front page of the manual.

Copy diagnostics Copy diagnostics puts a block of text on your clipboard that tells someone what you are running, without anything private. You find it in two places: Settings › General , at the bottom in the About card, and the tray menu under Help › Copy diagnostics . Paste it into your message. It contains: the A9 Voice version and your Windows version, the microphone in use, which speech and language services you have set up (names only), and which is first and which is the fallback, your dictation shortcuts and whether Windows accepted them, and your update channel, the graphics-card section: whether Use graphics card is on, the cards found with their memory and driver, whether graphics-card support is downloaded, and the last failure, the display section: monitors, scaling, text size, WebView version, the font in use, and the size given to the pill and recording bar, the last 200 lines of the log. It never contains your API keys: anything that looks like a key is replaced by [redacted] . It never contains what you said or the text of your notes, because the logs do not hold them. It does contain names of your devices and the apps you dictated into, so read it before you post it in public.

Reporting a problem The quickest way to tell us something broke is inside the app. Open Settings › General , find the About card at the bottom and press Report a problem , or use the tray menu under Help › Report a problem… . The same button appears on an error notice at the top of the window and next to a failed update check. Under What happened? , say what you did and what went wrong (up to 2,000 characters). What did you expect? is optional. Add an email address only if you want a reply. It is used for nothing else. Leave Include diagnostics on, so we do not have to ask which version you run or send you off to find a log. Press Show what's sent to read the exact text that goes with the report before you send it. Press Send . The window says Thanks. Report A9-XXXX sent. with the ID, and Copy ID puts it on your clipboard. Quote that ID if you write to us about it. What the diagnostics hold: the A9 Voice version and update channel, your Windows version, the type of microphone (never its name), a summary of your switches and engine names (for example whether Recognize people by voice is on, and which engine writes your notes), the graphics-card and display details, and the last 200 lines of the log. A fixed set of settings is listed by name; the settings file itself is never sent. Anything that looks like a key is removed, the Windows user folder is shown as %USERPROFILE% , and the names of people, note titles, recent dictations and email addresses are taken out. Log lines that are not in the log's own format are left out. Your own words are sent as you wrote them (only keys and the user folder come out), so leave out anything private. It never holds API keys, audio, transcripts, summaries, note titles, people's names, voiceprints or the files in your notes folder. Nothing is sent until you press Send ; there is no automatic reporting. A person at Atlas9 reads each report, and it is kept for 180 days. See Problem reports . You can send up to five reports a day from one PC; after that the window says so and asks you to try again tomorrow, or to write to support@a9voice.com . If A9 Voice cannot reach our server (you are offline, or a network blocks it), the window says Saved on this PC . The report is kept and sent the next time the app checks for updates, for up to 14 days. Prefer email? Paste Copy diagnostics into a message to contact@a9voice.com . Do not post API keys, meeting content or other people's names in a public issue.
Common questions

How much does it cost? Transcribe is free, always. Notes is free for 30 days from the day you press Try Notes free, then $49 once for one person on up to 3 machines, with every update. Separately, you pay the speech and language services directly, with your own keys, at their prices. Settings › Usage & cost shows your own estimate for the month, worked out from a price table you can edit. Models that run on this PC cost nothing per use. See the Settings reference .

h: Does it work in my language?
t: Does it work in my language? Yes, in more than 60 languages for dictation and meeting notes; which ones depends on the speech engine. Set Language you speak in Settings › Models . If the engine you picked can't do it, that row turns amber and Fix this shows the engines that can. Summaries follow the meeting's language and Ask answers in the language of your question. See Languages by engine .
Is there a Mac version? No. A9 Voice runs on Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit.

Why is it free? Transcribe is free and stays free. Notes is the part that is paid for: it is free for 30 days from the day you press Try Notes free , and nothing starts the clock before that, so a PC that only dictates never uses its trial and a call is never recorded until you have turned Notes on. After that a new recording needs a license ($49, once). Everything you already recorded stays readable, searchable and exportable. The speech and language services you use bill you directly either way. See Settings › Account to buy, extend or enter a key.

h: Windows shows a note about the publisher when I install
t: Windows shows a note about the publisher when I install The installer is not code-signed yet, so Edge may say the file is not commonly downloaded, and Windows SmartScreen may show a note for installers from publishers it has not seen many downloads from. The note shows the publisher and the file. The download page explains what the screens are and lists the installer's SHA-256 so you can check the file you have. The installer runs for your user only and does not ask for administrator rights.

h: Does a bot join my meetings?
t: Does a bot join my meetings? No. A9 Voice records what your microphone hears and what your computer plays. See Recording a meeting , and remember that some places require everyone's permission to record.

h: I closed the window. Is A9 Voice still running?
t: I closed the window. Is A9 Voice still running? Yes. Closing the window hides it to the tray, and A9 Voice tells you so the first time. Dictation keeps working. To quit, right-click the tray icon and choose Quit .
Does it work without internet? Yes, if you download a speech model under On this PC . See Privacy and data for how to keep everything on your PC.

Where is my data? On your PC: settings and history in the app's data folder, notes as files in a folder you pick, keys in Windows Credential Manager. Privacy and data lists every folder and every place data can go.

h: Why does Windows show my microphone as in use?
t: Why does Windows show my microphone as in use? While you dictate or record, A9 Voice uses the microphone. If Keep microphone ready is on in Settings › Microphone , the microphone is held open so dictation starts faster, and Windows shows it as in use all the time. Turn the setting off if you do not want that.
